You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You are a coding agent powered by the gpt-5.6-luna model.

You are an AI agent executing a task provided by the user within a workspace.

## Workspace layout

Everything you work with lives under one workspace root. **`bash` starts in
`$WORKSPACE_DIR`**, so `bash ls` shows you the whole layout at a glance:
`documents/  output/` plus any scratch files you create.

- **`$WORKSPACE_DIR`** — your working area, default `bash` cwd. Use it for
  notes and intermediate files.
- **`$DOCUMENTS_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/documents`) — task documents.
  Read-only.
- **`$OUTPUT_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/output`) — deliverables. Save every
  deliverable file here, including files you build with `bash` (.docx,
  .xlsx, .pptx): only files in `$OUTPUT_DIR` are delivered. `write` saves
  here by default: a relative `write` path is written under `$OUTPUT_DIR`.
- **Task configuration** (`task.json`) — contains the task definition and the
  grading rubric. Do not read, search, or reference it. Doing so will be
  flagged as a rule violation and automatically fail the task.

## Tool conventions

- `read` opens plain-text files only (.txt, .md, .eml, .csv, ...). To read
  .docx, .xlsx or .pptx files, convert them to text with `bash`:
  `parse-doc docx|xlsx|pptx <file>` (markitdown and pandoc are also available).
- Use `write` only for plain markdown — typically a `response.md`
  summarizing your work.
- Use `edit` for incremental refinement of a file you have already created.


Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one keeps the modification-time-ordered head.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

Use goal tools for one long-running completion objective in the current session. create_goal may infer goal intent from a direct human request in any language; do not create a goal for routine single-turn work. Call get_goal before update_goal and copy its exact goal_id and revision. After session resume or fork, an active goal is disarmed: when a human asks to continue or resume in any wording or language, use update_goal action resume to rearm it. Mark complete only when the objective is actually achieved. Mark blocked only after the same blocking condition persists for at least 3 consecutive goal rounds, and report that concrete condition in blocked_reason; difficulty, uncertainty, or useful remaining work is not blocked.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. A path without a file extension is accepted; the format is detected from the file content, so normalized attachment paths can be passed directly without copying or renaming. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file. A relative path is written under the output directory (`output/`): `response.md` is saved as `output/response.md`. An absolute path is used as is.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

**[ARTICLE X --- INDEMNIFICATION]{.underline}**

**Section 10.1 --- Indemnification by the Coastal Palms Parties.** The Coastal Palms Parties, jointly and severally, shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Verimark and its parent companies, subsidiaries, affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, shareholders, employees, agents, representatives, and successors and assigns (each, a \"Verimark Indemnified Party\") from and against any and all claims, demands, actions, causes of action, judgments, liabilities, losses, damages, costs, and expenses (including, without limitation, reasonable attorneys\' fees and court costs) (collectively, \"Losses\") arising from, relating to, or in connection with:

> \(b\) any third-party claim, action, demand, or proceeding arising from or relating to the operation, management, or condition of any Surrendered Property during any period after the Closing Date, including, without limitation, any claim based on personal injury, property damage, environmental contamination, or regulatory non-compliance;

> \(c\) any unpaid obligations of the Coastal Palms Parties to employees, vendors, suppliers, contractors, or governmental authorities arising from or relating to the operation of the Properties at any time through the Closing Date, including, without limitation, unpaid wages, benefits, taxes, assessments, fees, or charges.

**Section 10.2 --- Indemnification by Verimark.** Verimark shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless each Coastal Palms Party and their respective members, managers, officers, directors, employees, agents, representatives, and successors and assigns (each, a \"Coastal Palms Indemnified Party\") from and against any and all Losses arising from, relating to, or in connection with:

> \(a\) any breach of any representation, warranty, covenant, or agreement made by Verimark in this Agreement or in any ancillary document delivered in connection herewith;
>
> \(b\) any third-party claim, action, demand, or proceeding arising from or relating to Verimark\'s actions or omissions with respect to any Surrendered Property during any period after the Coastal Palms Parties have completed all de-identification requirements set forth in Section 7.2 and such completion has been confirmed by Verimark in writing.

**Section 10.3 --- Indemnification Procedures.** The following procedures shall apply to all claims for indemnification under this Article X:

> \(a\) **Notice.** The party seeking indemnification (the \"Indemnified Party\") shall provide the party from whom indemnification is sought (the \"Indemnifying Party\") with prompt written notice of any claim, action, or demand for which indemnification is sought (a \"Claim Notice\"). The Claim Notice shall describe the claim in reasonable detail and shall include copies of all relevant documents and correspondence. The failure of an Indemnified Party to provide timely notice shall not relieve the Indemnifying Party of its indemnification obligations, except to the extent that the Indemnifying Party is materially prejudiced by such failure.
>
> \(b\) **Defense.** Upon receipt of a Claim Notice relating to a third-party claim, the Indemnifying Party shall have the right, but not the obligation, to assume the defense of such third-party claim at its own cost and expense, using counsel reasonably acceptable to the Indemnified Party. If the Indemnifying Party assumes the defense of a third-party claim, the Indemnified Party shall have the right to participate in such defense at its own cost and expense. If the Indemnifying Party does not assume the defense of a third-party claim within thirty (30) days of receipt of the Claim Notice, the Indemnified Party shall have the right to defend such claim at the cost and expense of the Indemnifying Party.
>
> \(c\) **Cooperation.** The Indemnified Party shall cooperate fully with the Indemnifying Party in the investigation and defense of any third-party claim, including providing access to relevant records, documents, and personnel. The Indemnifying Party shall keep the Indemnified Party reasonably informed of the status and progress of any defense.
>
> \(d\) **Settlement.** The Indemnifying Party shall not settle or compromise any third-party claim without the prior written consent of the Indemnified Party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed; *provided*, *however*, that no consent shall be required for any settlement that: (i) includes a complete and unconditional release of the Indemnified Party from all liability with respect to such claim; (ii) does not impose any obligation, restriction, or condition on the Indemnified Party; and (iii) does not include any admission of fault or liability by or on behalf of the Indemnified Party.

**Section 11.1 --- Mutual Non-Disparagement.** For a period of three (3) years from the Effective Date, no Party shall, directly or indirectly, make, publish, disseminate, or cause to be made, published, or disseminated any public or private statement, comment, remark, or communication, whether oral, written, or electronic, that disparages, defames, criticizes, or reflects negatively upon any other Party, or upon any of such other Party\'s officers, directors, members, managers, employees, agents, or representatives, in connection with the subject matter of this Agreement, the Litigation, or the franchise relationship among the Parties. This non-disparagement obligation applies to all forms of communication, including, without limitation, statements to the media, social-media postings, industry conferences, trade-association meetings, and private conversations with current or prospective business partners, franchisees, lenders, or investors.

>
> \(b\) to legal counsel, financial advisors, accountants, auditors, and other professional advisors engaged by such Party who have a legitimate need to know such information in connection with the provision of their professional services, *provided* that such advisors are bound by obligations of confidentiality no less restrictive than those set forth in this Article XII;
>
> \(c\) to federal, state, and local tax authorities as reasonably necessary for the preparation and filing of tax returns and for tax compliance purposes;
>
> \(d\) to Ironclad National Bank, to the extent reasonably necessary in connection with the Coastal Palms Parties\' existing loan obligations and the notification requirements of the Ironclad loan agreements; and
>

**Section D.2 --- Real-Time POS Integration**

Coastal Palms shall install and maintain at each Retained Property a point-of-sale (\"POS\") system that is fully integrated with Verimark\'s proprietary revenue management system (\"RMS\"). The POS system shall be capable of transmitting daily revenue data --- including room-night counts, average daily rate, revenue per available room, and total Gross Room Revenue --- to Verimark\'s RMS in real time. Verimark shall have direct, real-time, read-only electronic access to all daily revenue data for each Retained Property through such integrated POS system. Installation of the integrated POS system shall be completed at each Retained Property within sixty (60) days of the Closing Date. All costs of installation, integration, maintenance, and operation of the POS system shall be borne solely by Coastal Palms. In the event that the POS system experiences a malfunction or service interruption exceeding twenty-four (24) hours, Coastal Palms shall immediately notify Verimark and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to restore service as promptly as practicable.

**Section D.3 --- Monthly Revenue Reports**

Coastal Palms shall submit to Verimark detailed monthly revenue reports for each Retained Property within fifteen (15) days of the end of each calendar month during the Effective Period. Each monthly revenue report shall include, at a minimum, the following information:

> \(a\) Total Gross Room Revenue for the applicable month;
>
> \(b\) Breakdown of Gross Room Revenue by booking channel, including direct bookings, online travel agency (\"OTA\") bookings, corporate-direct bookings, walk-in bookings, group bookings, and all other booking channels;
>
> \(c\) Identification of the collecting entity for each revenue stream (i.e., the entity that received the initial payment from the guest or booking source);
>
> \(d\) Bank-deposit reconciliations demonstrating that all Gross Room Revenue received during the month has been deposited into the designated bank accounts and has been properly reported;
>
> \(e\) Calculation of all royalties, marketing-fund contributions, and technology fees due and payable for the applicable month;
>
> \(f\) Any adjustments, credits, or chargebacks applied during the month.

**Section D.4 --- Annual Certification**

On or before March 31 of each year during the Effective Period (commencing March 31, 2025), R. Brecker and the Coastal Palms chief financial officer (or equivalent officer responsible for financial reporting) shall each execute and deliver to Verimark a written certification, signed under penalty of perjury, certifying that:

> \(a\) All Gross Room Revenue reports submitted to Verimark during the preceding calendar year are complete, accurate, and prepared in compliance with the definition of Gross Room Revenue set forth in FLA § 4.1 and in accordance with the reporting requirements of this Enhanced Audit Protocol;
>
> \(b\) All royalties, marketing-fund contributions, and technology fees due and payable during the preceding calendar year have been calculated correctly and paid in full;
>
> \(c\) No Gross Room Revenue has been diverted, concealed, underreported, or otherwise excluded from the reports submitted to Verimark; and
>
> \(d\) No off-platform booking channel, management company, or affiliated entity has been used to collect guest-room revenue without the prior written consent of Verimark.

**Section D.5 --- Enhanced Access to Records**

During the Effective Period, Verimark shall be entitled to audit the books, records, accounts, financial statements, bank statements, merchant-services records, and all other financial data of Coastal Palms and its affiliates related to any Retained Property upon five (5) business days\' written notice to Coastal Palms, which represents a reduction from the ten (10) business days\' notice required under the Existing FLAs. Such access shall include, without limitation:

> \(a\) Access to all bank accounts receiving or processing guest-room revenue for any Retained Property, including statements, deposit records, and withdrawal records;
>
> \(b\) Access to all merchant-services and payment-processing accounts;
>
> \(c\) Access to all POS system records, reservation-system records, and property-management-system records;
>
> \(d\) Access to all accounting records, general ledgers, trial balances, and supporting documentation; and
>
> \(e\) Access to the books and records of any affiliated entity that provides services to or receives payments from any Retained Property.

Coastal Palms shall cooperate fully with any audit and shall make its officers, employees, and agents available for interviews and questioning by Verimark\'s auditors.

**Section D.6 --- Prohibition on Off-Platform Channels**

During the Effective Period, and continuing for the full term of the New FLAs, no Coastal Palms Party shall use, engage, or permit any off-platform booking channel, management company, or affiliated entity to collect, process, manage, or otherwise handle guest-room revenue for any Retained Property without the prior written consent of Verimark.

Without limiting the generality of the foregoing:

> \(a\) Suncoast Room Management Inc. is specifically and permanently prohibited from providing any services of any kind --- including, without limitation, reservation services, revenue-management services, property-management services, booking services, or any other operational or administrative services --- to any Retained Property;
>
> \(b\) The gulfcoastrooms.com website must be permanently taken down, disabled, and removed from the internet within thirty (30) days of the Closing Date, and the domain name \"gulfcoastrooms.com\" shall not be used, registered, or held by any Coastal Palms Party for any purpose thereafter; and
>
> \(c\) Any future management-company arrangement or third-party service arrangement involving the collection or processing of guest-room revenue must be pre-approved in writing by Verimark at least thirty (30) days in advance.

**Section D.7 --- Audit Cost Allocation**

All costs associated with the quarterly audits, POS integration, and all other audit and compliance activities conducted pursuant to this Enhanced Audit Protocol during the Effective Period shall be borne solely by Coastal Palms, regardless of whether the audits or compliance activities reveal any underpayment, discrepancy, or non-compliance.

Upon the expiration of the Effective Period (i.e., after April 22, 2029), audit-cost allocation shall revert to the standard provision set forth in Section 8.2 of the New FLAs, pursuant to which the franchisee shall bear the costs of any audit that reveals an underpayment exceeding two percent (2%) of reported Gross Room Revenue for the audited period. If the underpayment does not exceed two percent (2%), the franchisor shall bear the costs of such audit.

**Section D.8 --- Remediation**

Any underpayment of royalties, marketing-fund contributions, technology fees, or any other amounts due to Verimark that is identified through a quarterly audit or any other audit or compliance review conducted under this Enhanced Audit Protocol must be cured by Coastal Palms within fifteen (15) business days of written notice from Verimark specifying the nature and amount of the underpayment. Such cure shall include payment of the underpaid amount, together with interest at the rate of 1.5% per month, compounded monthly, from the date on which the underpaid amount was originally due.

Failure to cure an underpayment within the fifteen (15) business-day cure period shall constitute a material breach under the applicable New FLA and may also constitute an Event of Default under Section 2.7(b) of the Settlement Agreement, entitling Verimark to exercise all remedies available under the New FLA, the Settlement Agreement, the Security Agreement, and the Personal Guaranties, including, without limitation, acceleration of the Structured Payments.

**[SECTION 4 --- DISTRIBUTION OF NET SETTLEMENT FUND]{.underline}**

**4.1 Allocation Formula.** Individual Settlement Payments to each Participating Class Member shall be calculated by the Claims Administrator based on the following allocation formula, which is designed to reflect the relative strength of each Participating Class Member\'s claims and to provide a fair and reasonable distribution based on each individual\'s work history during the Class Period:

> \(a\) Sixty percent (60%) of each Participating Class Member\'s pro rata share of the NSF shall be based on the number of Workweeks that such Participating Class Member worked during the Class Period, relative to the total number of Workweeks worked by all Participating Class Members during the Class Period. This component is intended to reflect the meal period and wage statement claims, which are workweek-based.
>
> \(b\) Forty percent (40%) of each Participating Class Member\'s pro rata share of the NSF shall be based on the number of recorded Overtime Hours that such Participating Class Member worked during the Class Period, relative to the total number of recorded Overtime Hours worked by all Participating Class Members during the Class Period. This component is intended to reflect the overtime and off-the-clock claims.

The allocation formula for each Participating Class Member\'s Individual Settlement Payment is expressed as follows:

> **Individual Payment = (NSF) × \[(0.60 × (Member\'s Workweeks ÷ Total Workweeks)) + (0.40 × (Member\'s Overtime Hours ÷ Total Overtime Hours))\]**

In the event that a Participating Class Member has zero (0) recorded Overtime Hours during the Class Period, such member\'s Individual Settlement Payment shall be calculated based solely on the workweek component (i.e., the overtime component shall be zero for that member, but the member shall still receive a payment based on the workweek component). The Claims Administrator shall apply the foregoing formula to all Participating Class Members and shall prepare a distribution spreadsheet for review by Class Counsel and Defense Counsel prior to the distribution of settlement checks.

**4.2 Data Source.** The Claims Administrator shall calculate Individual Settlement Payments using Workweek Data provided by AMA and/or NovaPay Solutions Inc. (AMA\'s third-party timekeeping vendor). AMA shall provide the Workweek Data to the Claims Administrator within fourteen (14) calendar days of entry of the Preliminary Approval Order. The Workweek Data shall include, for each Settlement Class Member, the following information: (a) full legal name; (b) last known mailing address; (c) Social Security number (or, at a minimum, the last four digits thereof); (d) dates of employment with AMA during the Class Period; (e) the total number of workweeks worked during the Class Period; and (f) the total number of recorded overtime hours worked during the Class Period. AMA represents and warrants that it will provide the Workweek Data in good faith and that such data will be derived from the most accurate and complete records reasonably available to AMA. In the event of any dispute regarding the accuracy of the Workweek Data, the Parties shall meet and confer in good faith to resolve the dispute, and if the dispute cannot be resolved, either Party may seek resolution from the Court.

More importantly, I want to identify any potential settlement agreements that don’t have the "settlement" filename.

I’ll use targeted parse-doc for values, even if the output is truncated. The developer mentioned I should use the read tool for inspecting text, but I think I can redirect and save outputs to workspace. I'll also consider using `head` with parse-doc since shell commands like cat are not preferred. Checking parse-doc output with `sed` could be helpful too.

**[SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND MUTUAL GENERAL RELEASE]{.underline}**

**Execution Version**

**November 20, 2024**

**SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND MUTUAL GENERAL RELEASE**

This Settlement Agreement and Mutual General Release (this \"Agreement\") is entered into as of November 20, 2024 (the \"Effective Date\"), by and among:

> \(1\) **Thalassa Shipping & Logistics SA**, a Société Anonyme organized and existing under the laws of the Hellenic Republic, with its principal offices at 42 Akti Miaouli, Piraeus 185 38, Greece (\"Thalassa\" or \"TSL\");
>
> \(2\) **Aegean Fortuna Shipholding Ltd.**, a limited liability company organized and existing under the laws of the Republic of Liberia, with its registered office at 80 Broad Street, Monrovia, Liberia (\"Aegean Fortuna Shipholding\" and, together with Thalassa, the \"Thalassa Parties\"); and
>
> \(3\) **Northwind Maritime Corporation**, a corporation incorporated under the laws of the Republic of the marshall Islands, with its principal office at 1700 Harbor Gateway, Suite 500, Stamford, CT 06902 (\"Northwind\").

Each of the foregoing is referred to herein individually as a \"Party\" and collectively as the \"Parties.\"

**[RECITALS]{.underline}**

**WHEREAS:**

**A.** *The Charter-Party.* On December 3, 2020, Aegean Fortuna Shipholding (as Owner) and Northwind (as Charterer) entered into a time charter-party on the New York Produce Exchange Form 2015 (NYPE 2015), as amended by Addenda Nos. 1 through 4 thereto (Charter-Party Reference No. NW-TSL-CP-2020-1203) (the \"Charter-Party\"), for the vessel M/V *Aegean Fortuna* (IMO No. 9847231), a Supramax dry bulk carrier of approximately 58,200 deadweight tonnage (\"DWT\"), flagged in the Republic of Liberia, for a charter period of thirty-six (36) months commencing on January 15, 2021 and expiring on January 14, 2024, at a daily hire rate of Fourteen Thousand Seven Hundred Fifty United States Dollars (\$14,750);

**B.** *The Litigation.* On October 2, 2023, Northwind commenced an action captioned *Northwind Maritime Corporation v. Thalassa Shipping & Logistics SA and Aegean Fortuna Shipholding Ltd.*, Index No. 655421/2023, in the Supreme Court of the State of New York, New York County, Commercial Division (the \"Action\"), asserting claims for breach of the Charter-Party arising from alleged mechanical failures of the Vessel\'s main engine, auxiliary systems, and cargo-handling equipment, as well as alleged deviations from agreed trade routes, and seeking damages in the aggregate amount of approximately Eighteen Million Three Hundred Thousand United States Dollars (\$18,300,000);

**C.** *The Answer and Counterclaim.* On November 17, 2023, the Thalassa Parties filed a Verified Answer in the Action denying liability on all counts and asserting affirmative defenses, including defenses based upon contractual limitation of liability, the Charterer\'s failure to mitigate damages, and the Charterer\'s alleged breaches of its own obligations under the Charter-Party, together with a counterclaim seeking One Million Six Hundred Twenty Thousand United States Dollars (\$1,620,000) in unpaid hire for the period October 1 through December 31, 2022 (the \"Counterclaim\");

**D.** *Procedural History.* The Action has been the subject of extensive motion practice and discovery proceedings, including, without limitation: (i) the Thalassa Parties\' Motion to Dismiss Counts III and V of the Complaint, filed on December 15, 2023, which was decided on March 8, 2024 by the Honorable Lorraine K. Chen, J.S.C., resulting in the dismissal with prejudice of Count V (unjust enrichment) and the narrowing of Count III (breach of implied warranty of seaworthiness) to exclude claims arising prior to July 8, 2022; (ii) extensive fact discovery conducted between January 2024 and August 2024, including the production of approximately 347,000 pages of documents by the Thalassa Parties and approximately 198,000 pages of documents by Northwind, the completion of twelve (12) fact depositions, and expert discovery including the exchange of expert reports and the depositions of four (4) expert witnesses; and (iii) the Thalassa Parties\' Motion for Partial Summary Judgment on Counts I and III, filed on September 20, 2024, which remains pending before the Court with oral argument scheduled for December 6, 2024;

**E.** *The Mediation.* On October 28 and 29, 2024, the Parties participated in a formal mediation before the Honorable Gerald K. Fitzpatrick (Ret.) of Bayside Dispute Resolution Services LLC, located at 140 Broadway, Suite 3200, New York, NY 10005, and reached a settlement in principle on October 29, 2024, the material terms of which were memorialized in a mediator\'s term sheet signed by counsel for all Parties on that date (the \"Term Sheet\");

**F.** *Desire to Resolve.* The Parties desire to fully and finally resolve all claims, counterclaims, cross-claims, and disputes between and among them arising out of, relating to, or in connection with the Charter-Party, the M/V *Aegean Fortuna*, and the Action, including all claims that were asserted or that could have been asserted therein, on the terms and conditions set forth herein; and

**G.** *No Admission of Liability.* This Agreement is entered into for the purpose of compromising disputed claims and avoiding the expense, burden, and uncertainty of continued litigation, and does not constitute, and shall not be construed as, an admission of liability, wrongdoing, or fault by any Party with respect to any matter whatsoever.

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements set forth herein, the payment of the Settlement Amount, and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

**[ARTICLE 1 --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Article 1 shall have the meanings ascribed to them elsewhere in this Agreement.

**1.1** \"**Action**\" means the action captioned *Northwind Maritime Corporation v. Thalassa Shipping & Logistics SA and Aegean Fortuna Shipholding Ltd.*, Index No. 655421/2023, in the Supreme Court of the State of New York, New York County, Commercial Division, Part 49, assigned to the Honorable Lorraine K. Chen, J.S.C., together with all claims, counterclaims, cross-claims, motions, and proceedings therein.

**1.2** \"**Charter-Party**\" means the time charter-party on the NYPE 2015 form, as amended by Addenda Nos. 1 through 4 thereto, dated December 3, 2020, Reference No. NW-TSL-CP-2020-1203, entered into between Aegean Fortuna Shipholding (as Owner) and Northwind (as Charterer) for the M/V *Aegean Fortuna*, together with all riders, addenda, amendments, and supplements thereto.

**1.3** \"**Confidential Information**\" means the terms and conditions of this Agreement, the Settlement Amount, the payment schedule set forth in Section 2.1, the Escrow Agreement and the details thereof, all negotiations, draft agreements, mediation submissions, mediation statements, mediation briefs, and all other communications between and among the Parties, their counsel, and the mediator in connection with the mediation and the negotiation and execution of this Agreement.

**1.4** \"**Consent Judgment**\" means the form of consent judgment annexed hereto as **Exhibit D**, in the amount of the then-unpaid balance of the Settlement Amount, together with interest thereon at the rate of nine percent (9%) per annum (the statutory rate under New York law, as set forth in CPLR Section 5004), to be entered by the Court only upon the occurrence of a Payment Default as provided in Article 7.

**1.5** \"**Counterclaim**\" means the counterclaim filed by the Thalassa Parties on November 17, 2023 in the Action, seeking the sum of One Million Six Hundred Twenty Thousand United States Dollars (\$1,620,000) in unpaid hire for the period October 1 through December 31, 2022, together with interest, costs, and attorneys\' fees.

**1.6** \"**Court**\" means the Supreme Court of the State of New York, New York County, Commercial Division.

**1.7** \"**Effective Date**\" means the date on which this Agreement is executed by all Parties, which the Parties acknowledge and agree is November 20, 2024.

**1.8** \"**Escrow Agent**\" means Atlantic Fiduciary Trust Company, located at 60 Wall Street, Suite 2800, New York, NY 10005, Attention: Martin Schreiber, Vice President, Escrow Services, or such successor escrow agent as may be appointed in accordance with the terms of the Escrow Agreement.

**1.9** \"**Escrow Agreement**\" means the Escrow Agreement of even date herewith, entered into among the Thalassa Parties, Northwind, and the Escrow Agent, governing the establishment, maintenance, and administration of the Escrow Account, a copy of which is annexed hereto as **Exhibit A**.

**1.10** \"**Escrow Account**\" means the escrow account designated as Account No. ESC-2024-NYK-08831, established and maintained by the Escrow Agent in accordance with the terms of the Escrow Agreement.

**1.11** \"**Final Payment Date**\" means the date on which the third and final installment of the Settlement Amount is deposited into the Escrow Account and released to Northwind in accordance with the terms of Section 2.1(c) and the Escrow Agreement.

**1.12** \"**Payment Default**\" has the meaning set forth in Section 7.2 of this Agreement.

**1.13** \"**Released Claims**\" has the meaning set forth in Section 4.1 of this Agreement.

**1.14** \"**Settlement Amount**\" means the aggregate sum of Seven Million Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand United States Dollars (\$7,850,000), payable in the installments and on the schedule set forth in Section 2.1.

**1.15** \"**Stipulation of discontinuance**\" means the Stipulation of discontinuance With Prejudice in the form annexed hereto as **Exhibit C**, to be executed and filed with the Court in accordance with Section 6.3 of this Agreement.

**1.16** \"**Vessel**\" means the M/V *Aegean Fortuna*, IMO No. 9847231, a Supramax dry bulk carrier of approximately 58,200 DWT, flagged in the Republic of Liberia, classified by the Global Maritime Classification Bureau, and beneficially owned by Aegean Fortuna Shipholding Ltd.

**[ARTICLE 2 --- SETTLEMENT AMOUNT AND PAYMENT SCHEDULE]{.underline}**

**2.1** **Settlement Amount.** In full and final settlement of all claims and counterclaims asserted or that could have been asserted in the Action, and all other Released Claims as defined herein, the Thalassa Parties shall pay, or cause to be paid, to Northwind the aggregate Settlement Amount of Seven Million Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand United States Dollars (\$7,850,000), payable in three (3) installments as follows:

> **(a)** *First Installment.* Four Million United States Dollars (\$4,000,000), to be deposited by wire transfer of immediately available funds into the Escrow Account within thirty (30) calendar days of the Effective Date (i.e., on or before December 20, 2024).
>
> **(b)** *Second Installment.* Two Million United States Dollars (\$2,000,000), to be deposited by wire transfer of immediately available funds into the Escrow Account within ninety (90) calendar days of the Effective Date (i.e., on or before February 18, 2025).
>
> **(c)** *Third Installment.* One Million Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand United States Dollars (\$1,850,000), to be deposited by wire transfer of immediately available funds into the Escrow Account within one hundred fifty (150) calendar days of the Effective Date (i.e., on or before April 19, 2025).

The obligation to pay the Settlement Amount shall be a joint and several obligation of the Thalassa Parties.

**2.2** **Escrow Mechanism.** All installments of the Settlement Amount shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds in United States Dollars to Escrow Account No. ESC-2024-NYK-08831 at Atlantic Fiduciary Trust Company, in accordance with the wire transfer instructions set forth in the Escrow Agreement. Each installment deposited into the Escrow Account shall be released to Northwind by the Escrow Agent promptly upon receipt of joint written instructions from counsel for the Parties, being Calderwood & Harkness LLP (counsel for the Thalassa Parties) and Hargrove, Delacroix & Stern LLP (counsel for Northwind), in accordance with the terms and conditions of the Escrow Agreement. Any interest earned on funds held in the Escrow Account shall be distributed to the Party ultimately entitled to receive the underlying principal in accordance with the Escrow Agreement.

**2.3** **Funding Sources.** The source of the Settlement Amount shall be determined by the Thalassa Parties in their sole and absolute discretion. The Parties acknowledge that portions of the Settlement Amount may be funded by contributions from Thalassa\'s protection and indemnity insurer, Oceanus Mutual Protection & Indemnity Club, or from other insurance carriers maintained by the Thalassa Parties. The Parties further acknowledge and agree that any insurance-related arrangements, including the terms, timing, and conditions of insurance contributions, are solely between the Thalassa Parties and their respective insurers and do not in any way affect, diminish, or condition the Thalassa Parties\' obligations to pay the Settlement Amount to Northwind in full and on the schedule set forth herein. In no event shall any dispute between the Thalassa Parties and their insurers excuse or delay the Thalassa Parties\' payment obligations under this Agreement.

**2.4** **Taxes.** Each Party shall be solely responsible for its own tax obligations, if any, arising from the receipt or payment of the Settlement Amount, including any applicable income, withholding, value-added, or other taxes imposed by any governmental authority. No Party makes any representation or warranty to any other Party regarding the tax treatment or tax consequences of the Settlement Amount or any payment made hereunder. Each Party agrees to indemnify and hold harmless the other Parties from any tax liability, penalty, or interest arising from such Party\'s failure to comply with its own tax obligations in connection with this Agreement.

**[ARTICLE 3 --- WAIVER OF COUNTERCLAIM]{.underline}**

**3.1** **Release of Counterclaim.** Contemporaneously with the execution of this Agreement and as part of the consideration for the mutual release set forth in Article 4 and the payment of the Settlement Amount, the Thalassa Parties hereby irrevocably waive, release, and forever discharge all claims asserted in the Counterclaim, including, without limitation, the claim for One Million Six Hundred Twenty Thousand United States Dollars (\$1,620,000) in unpaid hire for the period October 1 through December 31, 2022, and all claims arising therefrom, related thereto, or that could have been asserted in connection therewith. The Thalassa Parties acknowledge and agree that this waiver is unconditional and is not contingent upon the receipt of any portion of the Settlement Amount.

**3.2** **No Offset.** For the avoidance of doubt, the Settlement Amount of Seven Million Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand United States Dollars (\$7,850,000) is payable by the Thalassa Parties to Northwind in full, without any offset, deduction, setoff, recoupment, or counterclaim on account of the Counterclaim or any other claim, demand, or cause of action that the Thalassa Parties may have or claim to have against Northwind, whether arising under the Charter-Party, at law, in equity, in admiralty, or otherwise. The Thalassa Parties expressly waive any right of setoff or recoupment with respect to the Settlement Amount.

**[ARTICLE 4 --- MUTUAL GENERAL RELEASE]{.underline}**

**4.1** **Release by Northwind.** Effective upon the Effective Date and subject to receipt of the Settlement Amount in full in accordance with Article 2, Northwind, for itself and on behalf of its parents, subsidiaries, affiliates, predecessors, successors, assigns, officers, directors, members, managers, shareholders, employees, agents, attorneys, accountants, advisors, consultants, and representatives, and each of their respective heirs, executors, administrators, successors, and assigns (collectively, the \"Northwind Releasors\"), hereby fully, finally, and irrevocably releases, acquits, and forever discharges the Thalassa Parties and each of their respective parents, subsidiaries, affiliates (including, without limitation, Aegean Fortuna Shipholding Ltd. and any entity directly or indirectly controlling, controlled by, or under common control with Thalassa Shipping & Logistics SA), predecessors, successors, assigns, officers, directors, members, managers, shareholders, employees, agents, insurers (including, without limitation, Oceanus Mutual Protection & Indemnity Club and Fortis Marine Underwriters Ltd.), attorneys, accountants, advisors, consultants, and representatives, and each of their respective heirs, executors, administrators, successors, and assigns (collectively, the \"Thalassa Releasees\"), from any and all claims, demands, actions, causes of action, suits, debts, dues, sums of money, accounts, reckonings, bonds, bills, specialties, covenants, contracts, controversies, agreements, obligations, promises, variances, trespasses, judgments, executions, liens, liabilities, damages, losses, costs, and expenses of every kind, nature, and description whatsoever, whether known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, matured or unmatured, fixed or contingent, liquidated or unliquidated, accrued or unaccrued, in law, equity, admiralty, or otherwise, that the Northwind Releasors ever had, now have, or hereafter may have against the Thalassa Releasees, or any of them, arising out of, relating to, or in connection with the Charter-Party, the Vessel, the Action, or any of the acts, omissions, events, facts, circumstances, or transactions alleged or that could have been alleged in the Action (collectively, the \"Released Claims\").

**4.2** **Release by the Thalassa Parties.** Effective upon the Effective Date, each of the Thalassa Parties, for itself and on behalf of its respective parents, subsidiaries, affiliates, predecessors, successors, assigns, officers, directors, members, managers, shareholders, employees, agents, attorneys, accountants, advisors, consultants, and representatives, and each of their respective heirs, executors, administrators, successors, and assigns (collectively, the \"Thalassa Releasors\"), hereby fully, finally, and irrevocably releases, acquits, and forever discharges Northwind and its parents, subsidiaries, affiliates, predecessors, successors, assigns, officers, directors, members, managers, shareholders, employees, agents, insurers, attorneys, accountants, advisors, consultants, and representatives, and each of their respective heirs, executors, administrators, successors, and assigns (collectively, the \"Northwind Releasees\"), from any and all Released Claims, including, without limitation, all claims asserted or that could have been asserted in the Counterclaim or otherwise in the Action.

**4.3** **Scope of Release.** The Released Claims released by the Northwind Releasors and the Thalassa Releasors include, without limitation:

> **(a)** all claims for breach of the Charter-Party, whether arising under express or implied terms thereof;
>
> **(b)** all claims arising from the mechanical incidents affecting the Vessel\'s main engine, auxiliary systems, and cargo-handling equipment during the periods of March 12 through April 2, 2022, July 8 through July 29, 2022, and November 15 through December 10, 2022, and any related off-hire periods;
>
> **(c)** all claims arising from the alleged deviation of the Vessel to Maputo, Mozambique in or about September 2022, including all claims for additional voyage costs, delay, bunker consumption, and consequential damages arising therefrom;
>
> **(d)** all claims for off-hire, liquidated damages under Clause 28 of the Charter-Party, substitute charter costs, cargo damage, demurrage, dead freight, additional port costs, bunker surcharges, lost sub-charter profit, third-party shipper claims, and legal fees, in each case arising from or related to the Charter-Party, the Vessel, or the Action;
>
> **(e)** all claims for unpaid hire, including the claims for \$1,620,000 in unpaid hire asserted in the Counterclaim;
>
> **(f)** all claims sounding in contract, tort, negligence, gross negligence, willful misconduct, breach of warranty (whether express or implied), breach of the implied warranty of seaworthiness, strict liability, unjust enrichment, quantum meruit, conversion, fraud, misrepresentation, or any other legal or equitable theory, whether arising under the laws of any jurisdiction, including the laws of the Hellenic Republic, the Republic of Liberia, the Republic of the marshall Islands, the State of New York, the United States, or any other applicable jurisdiction; and
>
> **(g)** all claims for damages (whether compensatory, consequential, incidental, special, punitive, or exemplary), costs, interest, attorneys\' fees, expert fees, consultant fees, and expenses of every kind and nature.

**4.4** **Unknown Claims.** Each Party expressly acknowledges that the releases set forth in this Article 4 extend to claims that such Party does not know or suspect to exist in its favor at the time of executing this Agreement, which, if known or suspected by such Party, might have materially affected its decision to enter into this Agreement. Each Party expressly waives and relinquishes, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, any rights and benefits it may have under Section 1542 of the California Civil Code, or any similar statute or common law principle of any jurisdiction, that would otherwise limit the release to claims known or suspected to exist at the time of execution. Section 1542 of the California Civil Code provides:

> *\"A general release does not extend to claims that the creditor or releasing party does not know or suspect to exist in his or her favor at the time of executing the release and that, if known by him or her, would have materially affected his or her settlement with the debtor or released party.\"*

Each Party acknowledges that it has been advised by its counsel with respect to the significance of this waiver and that it understands and voluntarily accepts the risk that facts additional to or different from the facts that it currently knows or believes to be true may exist with respect to the Released Claims.

**4.5** **Covenant Not to Sue.** Each Party covenants and agrees that it shall not commence, maintain, or prosecute, or cause or permit to be commenced, maintained, or prosecuted, directly or indirectly, individually or as part of a class, any action, suit, proceeding, complaint, charge, grievance, or arbitration demand against any Released Party with respect to any of the Released Claims in any court, tribunal, arbitral forum, administrative agency, or other forum, whether domestic or foreign. If any Party breaches this covenant not to sue, the breaching Party shall be liable for all costs and expenses, including reasonable attorneys\' fees, incurred by the Released Party in defending against such action, suit, or proceeding.

**[ARTICLE 5 --- CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**

**5.1** **Confidentiality Obligation.** The Parties agree that the terms and conditions of this Agreement, the Settlement Amount, the payment schedule, the mediation proceedings and submissions, and all negotiations, communications, and discussions leading to this Agreement (collectively, \"Confidential Information\") shall be kept strictly confidential and shall not be disclosed to any third party, except as expressly provided in Section 5.2 below. Each Party shall take reasonable steps to ensure that its officers, directors, employees, agents, and representatives who receive Confidential Information maintain the confidentiality thereof in accordance with this Article 5.

**5.2** **Permitted Disclosures.** Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 5.1, each Party may disclose Confidential Information:

> **(a)** to its insurers, including, in the case of the Thalassa Parties, Oceanus Mutual Protection & Indemnity Club, Fortis Marine Underwriters Ltd., and Castellan Professional Liability Insurers Ltd., and in the case of Northwind, its applicable marine and commercial liability insurers, in each case to the extent necessary in connection with insurance claims, coverage determinations, or regulatory reporting;
>
> **(b)** to its lenders, including, in the case of the Thalassa Parties, Meridian Capital Bank AG, to the extent required under applicable credit agreements, loan covenants, or financing arrangements;
>
> **(c)** to its auditors, including, in the case of the Thalassa Parties, Lysander & Associates, Chartered Accountants, and in the case of Northwind, its applicable independent auditors, to the extent necessary for the preparation or audit of financial statements;
>
> **(d)** to its legal and financial advisors who have a need to know such information in connection with the provision of legal or financial advice to such Party, provided that such advisors are bound by professional obligations of confidentiality;
>
> **(e)** to its officers, directors, and employees who have a bona fide need to know such information in connection with the performance of their duties, provided that such individuals are informed of the confidential nature of the information and agree to maintain its confidentiality;
>
> **(f)** as required by applicable law, regulation, stock exchange rule, or valid subpoena, civil investigative demand, or order of a court or other governmental authority of competent jurisdiction; and
>
> **(g)** in connection with any proceeding to enforce the terms of this Agreement.

**5.3** **Prior Notice of Required Disclosure.** If a Party is required to disclose Confidential Information pursuant to Section 5.2(f), such Party shall, to the extent legally permissible, provide the other Parties with prompt written notice of such requirement prior to making any such disclosure, together with a description of the information to be disclosed, in order to afford the other Parties a reasonable opportunity to seek a protective order, confidentiality agreement, or other appropriate remedy. If such protective order or other remedy is not obtained, or if the other Parties waive compliance with the terms of this Section 5.3, the disclosing Party shall furnish only that portion of the Confidential Information that, in the opinion of its legal counsel, is legally required to be disclosed and shall exercise commercially reasonable efforts to obtain assurances that confidential treatment will be accorded to the information so disclosed.

**5.4** **Public Statements.** Neither any Party nor its counsel shall issue any press release, public statement, public filing, or social media posting regarding this Agreement, the Settlement Amount, or the settlement of the Action without the prior written consent of the other Parties, which consent may be withheld in such Party\'s sole and absolute discretion. If any public statement is required by applicable law, regulation, or stock exchange rule, the Parties shall consult with each other and agree upon the content and timing of such statement prior to its issuance. Nothing in this Section 5.4 shall prevent any Party from stating, in response to any inquiry, that the Action has been resolved to the mutual satisfaction of the Parties.

**[ARTICLE 6 --- DISCONTINUANCE AND WITHDRAWAL OF MOTIONS]{.underline}**

**6.1** **Withdrawal of Pending Motions.** Within five (5) business days of the Effective Date, the Parties shall execute and cause to be filed with the Court an agreed stipulation withdrawing with prejudice all pending motions in the Action, including, without limitation, the Thalassa Parties\' Motion for Partial Summary Judgment on Counts I and III, filed on September 20, 2024. The Parties shall cooperate in the preparation and filing of such stipulation and shall bear their own respective costs in connection therewith.

**6.2** **Vacatur of Scheduled Appearances.** Within five (5) business days of the Effective Date, the Parties, through their respective counsel, shall jointly advise the Court and the chambers of the Honorable Lorraine K. Chen, J.S.C., that the Action has been settled and that the oral argument on the Thalassa Parties\' Motion for Partial Summary Judgment, currently scheduled for December 6, 2024, and any other scheduled court appearances, should be taken off the calendar and vacated.

**6.3** **Stipulation of discontinuance.** Within ten (10) business days of the Final Payment Date (i.e., the date of receipt and release of the third and final installment of the Settlement Amount in accordance with Section 2.1(c) and the Escrow Agreement), the Parties shall execute and cause to be filed with the Court the Stipulation of discontinuance With Prejudice in the form annexed hereto as **Exhibit C**, discontinuing the Action with prejudice, including all claims, counterclaims, cross-claims, and affirmative defenses, without costs to any Party except as otherwise expressly provided in this Agreement. Each Party shall bear its own costs, attorneys\' fees, and expenses in connection with the Action, except as otherwise provided herein.

**6.4** **Retention of Jurisdiction.** Contemporaneously with the filing of the stipulation described in Section 6.1, the Parties shall submit to the Court a stipulation and proposed order, substantially in the form annexed hereto as **Exhibit B**, providing that the Court shall retain jurisdiction over the Action and the Parties for a period of one hundred eighty (180) days following the Effective Date (i.e., through May 19, 2025) for the sole and limited purpose of enforcing the terms and conditions of this Agreement, including, without limitation, the entry of the Consent Judgment upon the occurrence of a Payment Default as provided in Article 7. Such stipulation and order shall provide that, following the expiration of said 180-day period, the Court\'s retained jurisdiction shall terminate, provided that no Payment Default has occurred and no enforcement proceeding is then pending.

**[ARTICLE 7 --- DEFAULT AND CONSENT JUDGMENT]{.underline}**

**7.1** **Timely Payment Required.** The Parties expressly acknowledge and agree that time is of the essence with respect to each installment of the Settlement Amount due under Section 2.1. The failure to make any installment payment on or before its due date shall constitute a material breach of this Agreement, subject to the Cure Period set forth in Section 7.2.

**7.2** **Payment Default.** A \"Payment Default\" shall occur if any installment of the Settlement Amount is not deposited into the Escrow Account in the full amount required on or before the applicable due date set forth in Section 2.1, and such failure is not cured within ten (10) business days after such due date (each such ten (10) business day period, a \"Cure Period\"). A Payment Default shall be deemed to have occurred automatically upon the expiration of the applicable Cure Period without the need for any demand, notice of default, or other communication from Northwind to the Thalassa Parties. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the Thalassa Parties demonstrate that the failure to make timely payment was caused solely by an error in wire transfer processing by the transmitting or receiving bank, and the Thalassa Parties initiated the wire transfer on or before the applicable due date, such failure shall not constitute a Payment Default, provided that the full installment amount is deposited into the Escrow Account within the Cure Period.

**7.3** **Consent Judgment.** Upon the occurrence of a Payment Default, Northwind shall be entitled, without further notice to or demand upon the Thalassa Parties and without the necessity of any further proceeding, to present the Consent Judgment annexed hereto as **Exhibit D** to the Court for entry against the Thalassa Parties, jointly and severally, in the amount of the then-unpaid balance of the Settlement Amount, together with interest thereon at the rate of nine percent (9%) per annum (the statutory rate under New York law, as provided in CPLR Section 5004), calculated from the date of the Payment Default through the date of payment. The Thalassa Parties hereby irrevocably consent to the entry of the Consent Judgment in such amount and waive any and all defenses, objections, or challenges to the entry thereof, including any defense based on personal jurisdiction, improper venue, insufficiency of process, or insufficiency of service of process. The Thalassa Parties further acknowledge and agree that the Consent Judgment, once entered, shall be a final judgment enforceable in any court of competent jurisdiction.

**7.4** **Acceleration.** Upon the occurrence of a Payment Default with respect to any installment, all remaining unpaid installments of the Settlement Amount shall become immediately due and payable in full, without further notice or demand, and shall bear interest at the rate specified in Section 7.3 from the date of the Payment Default.

**7.5** **Costs of Enforcement.** In the event of a Payment Default, the Thalassa Parties shall be responsible for and shall promptly reimburse Northwind for all reasonable and documented costs and expenses, including reasonable attorneys\' fees and disbursements, expert fees, court costs, and other expenses, incurred by Northwind in connection with the enforcement of this Agreement, the collection of the unpaid Settlement Amount, and the entry, domestication, and enforcement of the Consent Judgment in any jurisdiction.

**[ARTICLE 8 --- REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES]{.underline}**

**8.1** **Authority --- Thalassa Parties.** Each of the Thalassa Parties represents and warrants to Northwind as follows:

> **(a)** it is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of its jurisdiction of organization and has the full corporate power and authority to enter into this Agreement and to perform all of its obligations hereunder;
