**[SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND MUTUAL RELEASE]{.underline}**

**EXECUTION VERSION**

**June 16, 2025**

**BETWEEN AND AMONG**

**SOLSTICE BIOMEDICAL DEVICES LTD.** a private limited company organized under the laws of Ireland

**SOLSTICE BIOMEDICAL, INC.** a Delaware corporation

and

**APEX SURGICAL INNOVATIONS, INC.** a Delaware corporation

**SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND MUTUAL RELEASE**

This Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release (this \"**Agreement**\") is entered into as of June 16, 2025 (the \"**Effective Date**\"), by and among:

**Solstice Biomedical Devices Ltd.**, a private limited company organized and existing under the laws of Ireland (CRO No. 648217), with its registered office at Unit 14, Clonskeagh Business Park, Clonskeagh Road, Dublin 14, D14 YF28, Ireland (\"**SBD**\" or \"**Solstice Parent**\");

**Solstice Biomedical, Inc.**, a corporation organized and existing under the laws of the State of Delaware (EIN: 84-3291056), with its principal offices at 3800 Concord Pike, Suite 410, Wilmington, Delaware 19803 (\"**Solstice US**,\" and together with Solstice Parent, \"**Solstice**\"); and

**Apex Surgical Innovations, Inc.**, a corporation organized and existing under the laws of the State of Delaware (EIN: 51-0483762), with its principal office at 1220 North Market Street, Suite 550, Wilmington, Delaware 19801 (\"**Apex**\").

Solstice and Apex are each referred to herein individually as a \"**Party**\" and collectively as the \"**Parties**.\"

**[RECITALS]{.underline}**

**A.** Apex is the owner by assignment of all right, title, and interest in and to certain United States utility patents, including: (i) U.S. Patent No. 9,814,237 (the \"**\'237 Patent**\"), entitled \"Locking Seal Assembly for Minimally Invasive Surgical Access Device,\" issued on November 14, 2017 by the United States Patent and Trademark Office (\"**USPTO**\"), with an expiration date of June 22, 2035; (ii) U.S. Patent No. 10,271,884 (the \"**\'884 Patent**\"), entitled \"Retractable Blade Deployment Mechanism for Trocar Systems,\" issued on April 30, 2019, with an expiration date of September 15, 2036; and (iii) U.S. Patent No. 10,932,105 (the \"**\'105 Patent**\"), entitled \"Integrated Insufflation Valve and Seal for Laparoscopic Trocar,\" issued on March 2, 2021, with an expiration date of January 10, 2038. The \'237 Patent, \'884 Patent, and \'105 Patent are collectively referred to herein as the \"**Asserted Patents**.\" The named inventor on each of the Asserted Patents is Dr. Raymond Szabo, Vice President of Engineering at Apex. The Asserted Patents form part of a broader patent family comprising fourteen (14) issued United States patents and six (6) pending continuation applications (the \"**Apex Trocar Patent Family**\"), as more fully described in Exhibit C attached hereto.

**B.** Solstice Parent is an Irish-domiciled private limited company that designs, develops, manufactures, and distributes minimally invasive surgical instruments and related accessories. Solstice Parent was founded in 2011, reported fiscal year 2023 revenue of approximately €187.4 million, and employs approximately 620 persons worldwide. Solstice US is a wholly owned subsidiary of Solstice Parent and is responsible for the marketing, distribution, and sale of Solstice\'s products within the United States. Among its product lines, Solstice designs, manufactures, and sells laparoscopic trocar assemblies under the PrecisionEdge™ brand, including the PE-5000 Series (5 mm diameter), the PE-12000 Series (12 mm diameter), and the PE-15000 Series (15 mm diameter) (collectively, the \"**Accused Products**\").

**C.** On May 9, 2024, Apex filed a complaint for patent infringement against Solstice US in the United States District Court for the District of Delaware, captioned *Apex Surgical Innovations, Inc. v. Solstice Biomedical, Inc.*, Case No. 1:24-cv-00587-RGA, assigned to Chief Judge Richard G. Andrews (the \"**Action**\" or \"**Litigation**\"). In the Action, Apex alleged that the Accused Products infringe one or more claims of the Asserted Patents, specifically: (i) the PE-5000 Series was alleged to infringe the \'237 Patent and the \'884 Patent; (ii) the PE-12000 Series was alleged to infringe all three Asserted Patents; and (iii) the PE-15000 Series was alleged to infringe the \'884 Patent and the \'105 Patent. Solstice US was served with the complaint on May 23, 2024, and on June 14, 2024 filed its Answer, Affirmative Defenses, and Counterclaims, asserting, among other things, non-infringement of each of the Asserted Patents, invalidity of the asserted claims under 35 U.S.C. §§ 102 and 103, inequitable conduct, and counterclaims for declaratory judgment of non-infringement and invalidity of the Asserted Patents. Thereafter, the Parties engaged in extensive fact and expert discovery, exchanged opening and rebuttal expert reports, and participated in a *Markman* hearing on November 18, 2024 before Chief Judge Andrews. The Court issued its Claim Construction Order on December 6, 2024. Cross-motions for summary judgment were fully briefed and argued, and were denied by Order dated May 5, 2025. The Action was scheduled for trial on September 30, 2025.

**D.** The Parties participated in a mediation session on March 17, 2025 before the Honorable Margaret Forsythe (Ret.) of Amberstone ADR Services in Wilmington, Delaware. That mediation did not result in a resolution of the dispute. The Parties subsequently participated in a second settlement conference on May 12, 2025 before Magistrate Judge Colleen Pratt. Following intensive arm\'s-length settlement negotiations conducted between May 19 and June 4, 2025, the Parties reached agreement in principle on the key terms of settlement and memorialized those terms in a Term Sheet executed by authorized representatives of the Parties on June 10, 2025 (the \"**Term Sheet**\").

**E.** The Parties now desire to fully and finally resolve all claims, counterclaims, defenses, and disputes between and among them arising out of or relating to the Action, the Asserted Patents, the Accused Products, and the Apex Trocar Patent Family, on the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement. Solstice\'s outside litigation counsel in the Action is the firm of Calderwood & Harkness LLP (Marcus Delgado, Responsible Partner), 1201 Market Street, Suite 2500, Wilmington, Delaware 19801. Apex\'s outside litigation counsel in the Action is the firm of Hargrove, Tate & Bennington LLP (Victoria Stanton, Lead Partner), 900 North King Street, Suite 1200, Wilmington, Delaware 19801.

**F.** NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual promises, covenants, releases, and other obligations set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged by each Party, the Parties agree as follows:

**[ARTICLE I --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 1.1 --- Defined Terms.** As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Section 1.1 shall have the meanings assigned to them elsewhere in this Agreement.

\"**Accused Products**\" means the PrecisionEdge™ PE-5000 Series (5 mm), PE-12000 Series (12 mm), and PE-15000 Series (15 mm) laparoscopic trocar assemblies designed, manufactured, marketed, and sold by Solstice, as identified in the complaint and amended pleadings in the Action.

\"**Action**\" means the civil action captioned *Apex Surgical Innovations, Inc. v. Solstice Biomedical, Inc.*, Case No. 1:24-cv-00587-RGA, pending in the United States District Court for the District of Delaware.

\"**Affiliate**\" means, with respect to a Party, any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with such Party, where \"control\" means the direct or indirect ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting securities of, or equivalent ownership interest in, such entity.

\"**Agreed Joint Public Statement**\" means the joint public statement agreed upon by the Parties in the form attached hereto as Exhibit F.

\"**Apex Trocar Patent Family**\" means the fourteen (14) issued United States patents and six (6) pending continuation applications related to trocar and laparoscopic access device technology owned by Apex as listed on Exhibit C attached hereto, including the Asserted Patents.

\"**Asserted Patents**\" means, collectively, U.S. Patent No. 9,814,237, U.S. Patent No. 10,271,884, and U.S. Patent No. 10,932,105.

\"**Calendar Quarter**\" means each three-month period ending on March 31, June 30, September 30, and December 31 of each calendar year. For purposes of this Agreement, the first Calendar Quarter following the Effective Date shall include the period from the Effective Date through June 30, 2025, and the last Calendar Quarter shall include the period through the expiration of the last-to-expire Licensed Patent.

\"**Change of Control**\" means, with respect to Solstice Parent or Solstice US, as applicable, any of the following: (i) the acquisition by any third party (other than an Affiliate) of more than fifty percent (50%) of the outstanding voting securities of Solstice Parent or Solstice US; (ii) any merger, consolidation, or similar business combination transaction involving Solstice Parent or Solstice US following which the holders of the voting securities of the applicable Solstice entity immediately prior to such transaction do not retain majority control of the surviving or resulting entity; or (iii) the sale, transfer, exclusive license, or other disposition of all or substantially all of the assets of Solstice Parent or Solstice US.

\"**Confidential Information**\" means the terms and conditions of this Agreement (including all Exhibits hereto), the Escrow Agreement, the Term Sheet, the Side Letter, and all oral and written communications, proposals, draft agreements, negotiation correspondence, and other materials exchanged between or among the Parties and their respective counsel, agents, and representatives in connection with the settlement negotiations that gave rise to this Agreement, subject to the exceptions set forth in Section 9.1.

\"**Covenant Not to Sue**\" means the covenant set forth in Section 4.2 of this Agreement and more fully described in the document attached hereto as Exhibit B.

\"**Effective Date**\" means June 16, 2025, the date on which this Agreement has been fully executed by all Parties.

\"**Escrow Agent**\" means Tidewater Fiduciary Services, Inc., a Delaware corporation, with offices at 300 Delaware Avenue, Suite 1400, Wilmington, Delaware 19801.

\"**Escrow Agreement**\" means the escrow agreement of even date herewith entered into by and among Solstice, Apex, and the Escrow Agent, governing the deposit, holding, and release of the Lump-Sum Payment.

\"**Licensed Field**\" means laparoscopic surgical access devices, including laparoscopic trocars, trocar assemblies, and related components for use in minimally invasive surgical procedures.

\"**Licensed Patents**\" means the Asserted Patents and any continuations, divisionals, reissues, or reexamination certificates thereof.

\"**Licensed Products**\" means the PrecisionEdge™ PE-5000 Series, PE-12000 Series, and PE-15000 Series laparoscopic trocar assemblies, and any successor products thereto, but only to the extent such products fall within the scope of one or more claims of the Licensed Patents in the Licensed Field.

\"**Lower Rate License**\" has the meaning set forth in Section 5.1.

\"**Lump-Sum Payment**\" means the aggregate sum of Eight Million Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand United States Dollars (\$8,750,000) payable by Solstice to Apex pursuant to Section 3.1.

\"**Net Sales**\" means the gross amounts invoiced by Solstice or any of its Affiliates or authorized sublicensees for sales of Licensed Products to unaffiliated third parties, less the following deductions to the extent actually incurred or accrued and separately identified on the applicable invoice or in Solstice\'s books and records maintained in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (\"GAAP\") or International Financial Reporting Standards (\"IFRS\"), as applicable: (a) returns, credits, and allowances actually granted; (b) trade discounts, quantity discounts, rebates, and chargebacks actually allowed or paid; (c) freight, shipping, handling, and insurance charges included in the invoiced price; and (d) sales, use, value-added, excise, and similar governmental taxes and duties included in the invoiced price. Net Sales shall not include sales or transfers between or among Solstice and its Affiliates for resale, provided that Net Sales shall include the subsequent sale to an unaffiliated third party. In the event a Licensed Product is sold as part of a combination or bundled product together with other products or components that are not Licensed Products, Net Sales for purposes of calculating the Running Royalty shall be calculated by multiplying the gross amount invoiced for such combination product by a fraction, the numerator of which is the average standalone selling price of the Licensed Product component and the denominator of which is the average standalone selling price of all components of the combination product, each as determined from Solstice\'s price lists or, if no standalone prices exist, as reasonably determined by Solstice and subject to audit under Article VI.

\"**Patent License Agreement**\" means the Non-Exclusive Patent License Agreement in the form attached hereto as Exhibit A.

\"**Royalty Cap**\" means One Million Eight Hundred Thousand United States Dollars (\$1,800,000) per calendar year, as more fully described in Section 3.2(b).

\"**Royalty Floor**\" means Five Hundred Thousand United States Dollars (\$500,000) per calendar year, beginning with calendar year 2026, as more fully described in Section 3.2(a).

\"**Running Royalty**\" means the royalty of three and three-quarters percent (3.75%) of Net Sales of Licensed Products payable by Solstice to Apex pursuant to Section 3.2.

\"**Side Letter**\" means the side letter agreement of even date herewith between Solstice and Apex relating to the notification protocol for the most-favored licensee provision set forth in Article V.

\"**Stipulation of Dismissal**\" means the stipulation of dismissal with prejudice in substantially the form attached hereto as Exhibit E, to be filed in the Action.

\"**Term Sheet**\" means the binding term sheet executed by authorized representatives of the Parties on June 10, 2025, setting forth the principal terms of settlement, which term sheet is superseded in its entirety by this Agreement.

\"**Tranche 1**\" means Five Million Two Hundred Fifty Thousand United States Dollars (\$5,250,000), as more fully described in Section 3.1(a).

\"**Tranche 2**\" means Three Million Five Hundred Thousand United States Dollars (\$3,500,000), as more fully described in Section 3.1(b).

**Section 1.2 --- Rules of Construction.** Unless the context otherwise requires: (a) the headings of Articles and Sections contained in this Agreement are for convenience of reference only and shall not affect in any way the meaning or interpretation of this Agreement; (b) words importing the singular shall include the plural and vice versa, and words importing any gender shall include all genders; (c) the word \"including\" (and its grammatical variations) means \"including, without limitation,\" and shall not be construed to limit any general statement that it follows to the specific or similar items or matters immediately following it; (d) references to \"Sections,\" \"Articles,\" and \"Exhibits\" are to Sections, Articles, and Exhibits of and to this Agreement unless the context otherwise requires; (e) references to any agreement, document, or instrument shall mean such agreement, document, or instrument as amended, supplemented, or modified from time to time in accordance with its terms and this Agreement; (f) references to any statute, rule, or regulation shall include all amendments thereto and all rules and regulations promulgated thereunder; and (g) references to \"days\" shall mean calendar days unless \"business days\" is expressly specified.

**[ARTICLE II --- REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES]{.underline}**

**Section 2.1 --- Mutual Representations and Warranties.** Each Party hereby represents and warrants to each other Party, as of the Effective Date, as follows:

> \(a\) **Organization and Good Standing.** Such Party is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of its jurisdiction of organization: Solstice Parent under the laws of Ireland; Solstice US under the laws of the State of Delaware; and Apex under the laws of the State of Delaware. Each Party is duly qualified or licensed to do business in each jurisdiction in which the nature of its business or the ownership or leasing of its properties requires such qualification, except where the failure to be so qualified would not reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on such Party\'s ability to perform its obligations under this Agreement.
>
> \(b\) **Authority.** Such Party has full corporate power and authority to enter into, execute, deliver, and perform its obligations under this Agreement and each of the ancillary documents contemplated hereby to which it is or will be a party.
>
> \(c\) **Due Authorization.** The execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement and the ancillary documents contemplated hereby have been duly authorized by all necessary corporate action on the part of such Party, including all requisite approvals of such Party\'s board of directors (or equivalent governing body). No additional corporate action on the part of such Party or its shareholders or members is necessary to authorize the execution, delivery, or performance of this Agreement.
>
> \(d\) **Enforceability.** This Agreement constitutes a legal, valid, and binding obligation of such Party, enforceable against such Party in accordance with its terms, subject to applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, fraudulent conveyance, and other similar laws affecting creditors\' rights and remedies generally, and subject, as to enforceability, to general principles of equity, including principles of commercial reasonableness, good faith, and fair dealing (regardless of whether enforcement is sought in a proceeding at law or in equity).
>
> \(e\) **No Consents Required.** No consent, approval, order, or authorization of, or registration, declaration, or filing with, any governmental authority, regulatory body, or third party is required on the part of such Party in connection with the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement, except as expressly contemplated herein or as may be required in connection with the filing of the Stipulation of Dismissal or any required reports under applicable securities laws.
>
> \(f\) **No Conflicts.** The execution, delivery, and performance by such Party of this Agreement and the ancillary documents contemplated hereby do not and will not (i) violate, conflict with, or result in a breach of any provision of such Party\'s certificate of incorporation, bylaws, memorandum of association, articles of association, or other organizational documents; (ii) violate, conflict with, or result in a breach or default (or an event that, with notice or lapse of time or both, would constitute a default) under any material agreement, contract, or instrument to which such Party is a party or by which such Party or its properties are bound; or (iii) violate any applicable law, statute, rule, regulation, order, judgment, decree, or injunction of any court or governmental authority applicable to such Party.

**Section 2.2 --- Apex\'s Representations and Warranties.** Apex hereby additionally represents and warrants to Solstice, as of the Effective Date, as follows:

> \(a\) **Ownership of Asserted Patents.** Apex is the sole and exclusive owner of the entire right, title, and interest in and to each of the Asserted Patents and each patent and patent application in the Apex Trocar Patent Family, free and clear of all liens, encumbrances, security interests, pledges, mortgages, charges, and adverse claims of any kind, other than non-exclusive licenses previously granted by Apex to third parties in the ordinary course of business prior to the Effective Date, none of which would materially impair Apex\'s ability to grant the license and covenant contemplated by this Agreement.
>
> \(b\) **Right to Grant License and Covenant.** Apex has the full and unrestricted right and authority to grant the patent license and covenant not to sue contemplated by Article IV of this Agreement and the exhibits attached hereto without the consent, approval, or authorization of any third party, including without limitation any co-owner, co-inventor, licensee, or other person or entity having any interest in the Asserted Patents or the Apex Trocar Patent Family.
>
> \(c\) **Subsisting Patents.** Each of the Asserted Patents is subsisting, has been duly issued by the USPTO, and has not been adjudicated invalid, unenforceable, or not infringed by any court, tribunal, or administrative body of competent jurisdiction in a final, non-appealable decision. All required maintenance fees for the Asserted Patents have been timely paid, and all necessary post-issuance filings have been duly made.
>
> \(d\) **No Pending Proceedings.** To Apex\'s knowledge, as of the Effective Date, no reexamination, inter partes review, post-grant review, covered business method review, or any other proceeding before the USPTO or any other patent office or administrative body is pending with respect to any of the Asserted Patents.
>
> \(e\) **Inventor Assignment.** Dr. Raymond Szabo, the named inventor on each of the Asserted Patents, has executed valid and binding assignments of all right, title, and interest in and to the Asserted Patents to Apex, and such assignments have been duly recorded with the USPTO. No other individual or entity has any claim to inventorship or ownership of any of the Asserted Patents.

**Section 2.3 --- Solstice\'s Representations and Warranties.** Solstice hereby additionally represents and warrants to Apex, as of the Effective Date, as follows:

> \(a\) **Subsidiary Relationship.** Solstice US is a direct, wholly owned subsidiary of Solstice Parent. All of the outstanding shares of capital stock of Solstice US are owned, beneficially and of record, by Solstice Parent, free and clear of all liens, encumbrances, and restrictions (other than restrictions on transfer imposed by applicable securities laws).
>
> \(b\) **Financial Capability.** Solstice has the present financial capability and sufficient available resources to make all payments contemplated by this Agreement, including the Lump-Sum Payment and the Running Royalty payments, and does not know of any reason that would prevent or impair Solstice from making such payments when due.
>
> \(c\) **Books and Records.** Solstice maintains true, accurate, and complete books and records of all sales, transfers, and other dispositions of Licensed Products, in conformity with GAAP or IFRS, as applicable, in sufficient detail to permit the accurate calculation of Net Sales and the Running Royalty. Solstice shall continue to maintain such books and records throughout the term of this Agreement and for a period of three (3) years following the expiration or termination of this Agreement.

**[ARTICLE III --- PAYMENT TERMS]{.underline}**

**Section 3.1 --- Lump-Sum Payment.** In partial consideration for the releases granted in Article VII, the license granted in Article IV, and the covenant not to sue set forth in Section 4.2 and Exhibit B, Solstice shall pay to Apex an aggregate lump-sum settlement payment of Eight Million Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand United States Dollars (\$8,750,000) (the \"**Lump-Sum Payment**\"), payable in two tranches as follows:

> **(a) Tranche 1.** Within ten (10) business days following the Effective Date (and in no event later than June 30, 2025), Solstice shall pay to the Escrow Agent, by wire transfer of immediately available funds in accordance with the wire instructions set forth in the Escrow Agreement, the sum of Five Million Two Hundred Fifty Thousand United States Dollars (\$5,250,000) (\"**Tranche 1**\"). Upon confirmation of the receipt of Tranche 1 into the escrow account maintained by the Escrow Agent, the Escrow Agent shall release the Tranche 1 funds to Apex by wire transfer to the bank account designated by Apex in the Escrow Agreement within three (3) business days of deposit. Solstice shall provide Apex with written confirmation of the wire transfer to the Escrow Agent promptly following its initiation.
>
> **(b) Tranche 2.** On or before September 15, 2025, Solstice shall pay to the Escrow Agent, by wire transfer of immediately available funds in accordance with the wire instructions set forth in the Escrow Agreement, the sum of Three Million Five Hundred Thousand United States Dollars (\$3,500,000) (\"**Tranche 2**\"). Upon confirmation of the receipt of Tranche 2 into the escrow account maintained by the Escrow Agent, the Escrow Agent shall release the Tranche 2 funds to Apex by wire transfer to the bank account designated by Apex in the Escrow Agreement within three (3) business days of deposit. Solstice shall provide Apex with written confirmation of the wire transfer to the Escrow Agent promptly following its initiation.
>
> **(c) Late Payment.** Any portion of the Lump-Sum Payment or any Running Royalty payment not paid when due shall bear interest from the applicable due date until the date of actual payment at a rate equal to the lesser of (i) one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month (eighteen percent (18%) per annum) and (ii) the maximum rate of interest permitted by applicable law. The accrual of interest under this Section 3.1(c) shall not limit or waive any other rights or remedies available to Apex, including Apex\'s right to terminate the Patent License Agreement upon a material breach of payment obligations, as set forth in Section 10.2 of this Agreement. Any interest payable hereunder shall be computed on the basis of a 360-day year composed of twelve 30-day months.

**Section 3.2 --- Running Royalty.** Beginning on the Effective Date and continuing for the remaining life of each Licensed Patent (with the last-to-expire Licensed Patent being the \'105 Patent, expiring January 10, 2038), Solstice shall pay to Apex a running royalty equal to three and three-quarters percent (3.75%) of Net Sales of Licensed Products (the \"**Running Royalty**\"), subject to the Royalty Floor and Royalty Cap set forth below.

> **(a) Royalty Floor.** Beginning with calendar year 2026, and for each full calendar year thereafter during the term of this Agreement, the minimum annual Running Royalty payable by Solstice to Apex shall be Five Hundred Thousand United States Dollars (\$500,000) (the \"**Royalty Floor**\"). If the aggregate Running Royalty payments actually due and paid with respect to Net Sales for a given calendar year are less than the Royalty Floor, Solstice shall pay the difference between the actual aggregate Running Royalty and the Royalty Floor within thirty (30) days following the end of such calendar year. For the avoidance of doubt, the Royalty Floor shall not apply to the partial calendar year 2025 (i.e., the period from the Effective Date through December 31, 2025), nor to any partial calendar year at the end of the term resulting from the expiration of the last Licensed Patent. The Royalty Floor shall be prorated for any partial calendar year at the end of the term.
>
> **(b) Royalty Cap.** The maximum aggregate Running Royalty payable by Solstice to Apex in any single calendar year shall not exceed One Million Eight Hundred Thousand United States Dollars (\$1,800,000) (the \"**Royalty Cap**\"). Once cumulative Running Royalty payments for a given calendar year reach the Royalty Cap, no further Running Royalty shall be due or payable for the remainder of that calendar year. The Royalty Cap shall be prorated for any partial calendar year at the beginning or end of the term.
>
> **(c) Royalty Reporting.** Solstice shall deliver to Apex a written quarterly royalty report, in substantially the form attached hereto as Exhibit D, within forty-five (45) days after the end of each Calendar Quarter. Each such royalty report shall include, at a minimum, the following information for the applicable Calendar Quarter, broken out by Licensed Product (PE-5000 Series, PE-12000 Series, and PE-15000 Series) and, within each Licensed Product, by geographic market (United States and international): (i) gross invoiced sales; (ii) itemized deductions for returns and allowances, trade discounts, rebates and chargebacks, freight and shipping charges, and applicable taxes; (iii) the resulting calculation of Net Sales; and (iv) the Running Royalty amount due for such Calendar Quarter. Each royalty report shall be certified as true, complete, and accurate by an authorized officer of Solstice, which certification shall be in the form set forth in Exhibit D.
>
> **(d) Royalty Payments.** Running Royalty payments shall be due and payable within forty-five (45) days after the end of each Calendar Quarter, concurrently with the delivery of the corresponding royalty report. All Running Royalty payments shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to a bank account designated by Apex in writing from time to time. Apex shall provide Solstice with its initial wire instructions within five (5) business days of the Effective Date and shall provide not less than fifteen (15) days\' prior written notice of any change in wire instructions. All Running Royalty payments shall be made in United States Dollars. To the extent any Net Sales are invoiced in a currency other than United States Dollars, such amounts shall be converted to United States Dollars at the average daily exchange rate published by the European Central Bank for the applicable Calendar Quarter.

**Section 3.3 --- Tax Treatment.** The Parties agree and acknowledge that the Lump-Sum Payment constitutes consideration for the settlement and release of all claims in the Action and for the grant of the Patent License Agreement and the Covenant Not to Sue, and that the Running Royalty constitutes license royalties for the use of intellectual property rights. Each Party shall be solely responsible for the payment of all taxes, duties, assessments, and other governmental charges imposed on it in connection with the payments made or received under this Agreement. Solstice shall comply with all applicable withholding tax obligations under United States federal, state, and local tax law and under the laws of Ireland, including any applicable provisions of the Convention between the Government of the United States of America and the Government of Ireland for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income and Capital Gains (the \"**U.S.-Ireland Tax Treaty**\"). Apex shall reasonably cooperate with Solstice\'s requests for tax documentation, including the execution and delivery of IRS Form W-9 or such other forms as may be reasonably required to establish Apex\'s tax status and to enable Solstice to comply with its withholding obligations. In the event that any withholding is required, Solstice shall remit the withheld amounts to the appropriate governmental authority, provide Apex with documentation of such withholding, and the net amount received by Apex after such withholding shall be deemed to satisfy Solstice\'s payment obligation with respect to the amount so withheld.

**Section 3.4 --- No Coverage by Insurance.** The Parties acknowledge and agree that the Lump-Sum Payment, the Running Royalty, and all other payment obligations of Solstice under this Article III are not covered by, and Solstice does not expect to receive reimbursement from, any insurance policy maintained by Solstice or any of its Affiliates, including but not limited to intellectual property insurance Policy No. HSI-IP-2023-04891 issued by Halcyon Specialty Insurance Co. or any other insurance policy. Solstice\'s obligation to make all payments under this Article III is absolute and unconditional and shall not be contingent upon, reduced by, or subject to any right of set-off, counterclaim, or deduction related to insurance coverage, insurance reimbursement, or any dispute between Solstice and any insurer.

**[ARTICLE IV --- LICENSE AND COVENANT NOT TO SUE]{.underline}**

**Section 4.1 --- Patent License Grant.** Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement and the Patent License Agreement attached hereto as Exhibit A, Apex hereby grants to Solstice a non-exclusive, non-transferable (except as expressly provided in Section 4.3), worldwide, royalty-bearing license under the Licensed Patents to make, have made, use, import, offer for sale, and sell Licensed Products in the Licensed Field. The license granted under this Section 4.1 shall be effective as of the Effective Date and shall remain in effect for the remaining life of each Licensed Patent, such that the license with respect to any individual Licensed Patent shall expire upon the expiration of that Licensed Patent (i.e., the license under the \'237 Patent shall expire on June 22, 2035; the license under the \'884 Patent shall expire on September 15, 2036; and the license under the \'105 Patent shall expire on January 10, 2038). The license is royalty-bearing, with royalties payable as set forth in Section 3.2 of this Agreement.

Solstice shall have the right to grant sublicenses under the Licensed Patents solely to contract manufacturers engaged by Solstice for the manufacture of Licensed Products, provided that each such sublicense is set forth in a written agreement between Solstice and the sublicensee that contains terms and conditions no less protective of Apex\'s rights than those set forth in this Agreement and the Patent License Agreement, including without limitation obligations relating to confidentiality, record-keeping, and audit rights. Solstice shall provide Apex with written notice of any sublicense granted pursuant to this paragraph within thirty (30) days of its execution, together with a copy of the sublicense agreement (which may be redacted to remove pricing and other competitively sensitive information unrelated to Apex\'s rights). Solstice shall remain fully responsible for the acts and omissions of its sublicensees as if such acts and omissions were those of Solstice.

**Section 4.2 --- Covenant Not to Sue.** As more fully set forth in the Covenant Not to Sue attached hereto as Exhibit B, Apex hereby irrevocably covenants and agrees that, during the term of the Patent License Agreement (as set forth in Section 4.1 and the Patent License Agreement), Apex will not assert, and will not authorize, direct, encourage, or assist any third party to assert, any patent or patent application in the Apex Trocar Patent Family (comprising the fourteen (14) issued United States patents and six (6) pending continuation applications listed on Exhibit C attached hereto) against Solstice, any Affiliate of Solstice, or any authorized sublicensee of Solstice, for or on account of the manufacture, having made, use, importation, offer for sale, or sale of any product within the Licensed Field. The Covenant Not to Sue extends to and encompasses all patents and patent applications in the Apex Trocar Patent Family, including any and all continuations, continuations-in-part, divisionals, reissues, and reexamination certificates thereof. The Covenant Not to Sue shall not extend to any patent or patent application outside the Apex Trocar Patent Family, and shall not limit Apex\'s right to assert patents against Solstice for activities outside the Licensed Field.

**Section 4.3 --- Transferability; Change of Control.** The patent license granted in Section 4.1 and the Covenant Not to Sue granted in Section 4.2 are personal to Solstice and are non-transferable, except as expressly provided in this Section 4.3. In the event of a Change of Control of Solstice Parent or Solstice US, the patent license and Covenant Not to Sue shall automatically transfer to and be binding upon the successor entity, provided that such successor entity executes a written instrument reasonably satisfactory to Apex confirming the successor entity\'s agreement to be bound by all terms and conditions of this Agreement, including without limitation the payment obligations under Article III, the confidentiality obligations under Article IX, and the audit rights under Article VI. Solstice shall provide Apex with written notice of any Change of Control within thirty (30) days of the closing of the transaction giving rise to such Change of Control, which notice shall identify the successor entity and include a copy of the written instrument described in the preceding sentence. For the avoidance of doubt, the patent license and Covenant Not to Sue shall not extend to any products of the successor entity\'s pre-existing product lines that are not Licensed Products.

**Section 4.4 --- No Implied License.** Except as expressly set forth in this Agreement, the Patent License Agreement, and the Covenant Not to Sue, nothing in this Agreement or in the performance or implementation hereof shall be construed to grant to Solstice, by implication, estoppel, or otherwise, any license or right under any patent, patent application, trade secret, trademark, copyright, or other intellectual property right owned, controlled, or licensable by Apex. Without limiting the foregoing, the license granted herein does not extend to any field of use other than the Licensed Field, and does not extend to any patent or intellectual property right other than the Licensed Patents and the Apex Trocar Patent Family as expressly provided herein.

**[ARTICLE V --- MOST-FAVORED LICENSEE]{.underline}**

**Section 5.1 --- Most-Favored Licensee Obligation.** If, at any time during the term of this Agreement following the Effective Date, Apex enters into a license agreement or other arrangement with any third party with respect to any one or more of the Licensed Patents that provides for a running royalty rate (whether expressed as a percentage of net sales or an equivalent per-unit royalty) that is lower than three and three-quarters percent (3.75%) of Net Sales (any such agreement, a \"**Lower Rate License**\"), Apex shall provide written notice to Solstice of such Lower Rate License within thirty (30) days of the execution thereof. Upon delivery of such notice, the Running Royalty rate applicable to Solstice under Section 3.2 of this Agreement shall automatically adjust downward to the lower running royalty rate set forth in the Lower Rate License, effective prospectively as of the first day of the Calendar Quarter following Apex\'s delivery of such notice to Solstice. For the avoidance of doubt, the most-favored licensee adjustment shall apply only to reductions in the running royalty rate and shall not require any retroactive adjustment or refund of royalties previously paid by Solstice at the 3.75% rate.

**[STANDSTILL AND SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT]{.underline}**

**Execution Version**

**April 14, 2025**

Among

**Cascade Retail Holdings Inc.**

**Priya Rathore, Derek Linden, Sonia Kaczmarek, Amara Osei, Brent Halvorsen, Lucia Fernandez-Gill, Nathan Tsao, and Kira Johansson**

and

**Verdana Commerce Group, Inc.**

In Connection With

*Cascade Retail Holdings Inc. v. Rathore et al.* C.A. No. 2025-0198-MTZ Delaware Court of Chancery

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

Right-click to update Table of Contents

**STANDSTILL AND SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT**

This STANDSTILL AND SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT (this \"Agreement\") is made and entered into as of April 14, 2025 (the \"Effective Date\"), by and among:

**CASCADE RETAIL HOLDINGS INC.**, a Delaware corporation, with its principal offices at 2200 Elliott Avenue West, Suite 3400, Seattle, Washington 98119 (\"Cascade\" or \"CRH\" or \"Plaintiff\");

**PRIYA RATHORE**, an individual residing at 14 Harbor Ridge Lane, Bellevue, Washington 98004 (\"Rathore\");

**DEREK LINDEN**, an individual (\"Linden\");

**SONIA KACZMAREK**, an individual (\"Kaczmarek\");

**AMARA OSEI**, an individual (\"Osei\");

**BRENT HALVORSEN**, an individual (\"Halvorsen\");

**LUCIA FERNANDEZ-GILL**, an individual (\"Fernandez-Gill\");

**NATHAN TSAO**, an individual (\"Tsao\");

**KIRA JOHANSSON**, an individual (\"Johansson\");

(Rathore, Linden, Kaczmarek, Osei, Halvorsen, Fernandez-Gill, Tsao, and Johansson are referred to collectively as the \"Individual Defendants\" or the \"Rathore Group\"); and

**VERDANA COMMERCE GROUP, INC.**, a Delaware corporation, with its principal offices at 400 Christiana Gateway, Suite 700, Wilmington, Delaware 19801 (\"Verdana\" or \"VCG\").

Cascade, the Individual Defendants, and Verdana are referred to collectively herein as the \"Parties\" and individually as a \"Party.\"

**[RECITALS]{.underline}**

**WHEREAS**, Cascade is a publicly traded omnichannel retail company listed on the Nasdaq Stock Market LLC under the ticker symbol \"CRHL,\" with annual revenues of approximately Six Billion Eight Hundred Twenty Million Dollars (\$6,820,000,000) for its fiscal year ended January 31, 2025, and a merchandising division that generated approximately Two Billion Three Hundred Million Dollars (\$2,300,000,000) in gross merchandise value during fiscal year 2024;

**WHEREAS**, each of the Individual Defendants was formerly employed by Cascade in senior merchandising roles and, in connection with such employment, each executed an employment agreement containing restrictive covenant provisions, including non-competition, non-solicitation of employees, non-solicitation of vendors, and confidentiality obligations, each governed by the laws of the State of Delaware (collectively, the \"Employment Agreements\");

**WHEREAS**, Rathore was employed by Cascade from June 3, 2019 through February 7, 2025, most recently serving as Senior Vice President, Merchandising, pursuant to an Amended and Restated Employment Agreement dated March 15, 2021 (the \"Rathore Employment Agreement\"), which contained, among other restrictive covenants, an eighteen (18)-month post-termination non-competition covenant, a twenty-four (24)-month non-solicitation covenant covering employees and vendors, and perpetual confidentiality obligations;

**WHEREAS**, the other seven Individual Defendants were employed by Cascade under Employment Agreements containing post-termination non-competition periods ranging from twelve (12) to eighteen (18) months and non-solicitation periods ranging from eighteen (18) to twenty-four (24) months, as more particularly described on Schedule 1 attached hereto;

**WHEREAS**, the Individual Defendants, by virtue of their senior merchandising positions at Cascade, had access to Cascade\'s proprietary and confidential information, including without limitation Cascade\'s vendor negotiation playbooks, seasonal buying algorithms, private-label sourcing strategies, customer segmentation data, ecommerce assortment algorithms, and a confidential five-year category expansion strategic plan known internally as \"Project Ridgeline,\" which was completed in October 2024 and constitutes one of Cascade\'s most competitively sensitive strategic assets (all such information, collectively, the \"Confidential Information\");

**WHEREAS**, on February 7, 2025, all eight Individual Defendants simultaneously submitted letters of resignation from Cascade, effective immediately, and subsequently accepted offers of employment with Verdana, a direct competitor of Cascade in twenty-eight (28) overlapping product categories;

**WHEREAS**, forensic analysis conducted by Pinnacle Forensics LLC (\"Pinnacle\"), an independent digital forensics firm retained by Cascade, determined that between January 10, 2025 and February 4, 2025, approximately fourteen thousand three hundred twenty-seven (14,327) files, comprising approximately 2.8 gigabytes of data, were downloaded from Cascade\'s Aldermere Systems and Pinnacle Health IT environments to personal cloud storage accounts belonging to certain of the Individual Defendants, including Project Ridgeline presentations, vendor negotiation term sheets, private-label cost models, and customer segmentation data (collectively, the \"Exfiltrated Data\");

**WHEREAS**, on March 5, 2025, Cascade filed a Verified Complaint and Motion for Temporary Restraining Order and Preliminary Injunction in the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware, captioned *Cascade Retail Holdings Inc. v. Rathore et al.*, C.A. No. 2025-0198-MTZ (the \"Action\"), asserting claims against the Individual Defendants and Verdana for (1) breach of restrictive covenant, (2) breach of confidentiality obligations, (3) misappropriation of trade secrets under the Delaware Uniform Trade Secrets Act, 6 Del. C. § 2001 *et seq.* (\"DUTSA\"), (4) tortious interference with contractual relations, and (5) civil conspiracy;

**WHEREAS**, on March 7, 2025, Vice Chancellor Margaret T. Zhao of the Delaware Court of Chancery granted Cascade\'s application for a temporary restraining order (the \"TRO\"), restraining all Individual Defendants from commencing employment in merchandising roles at Verdana for a period of fourteen (14) days, and requiring Cascade to post an injunction bond in the amount of Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$2,500,000) through Broadview Surety Corp. (Bond No. BSC-2025-TRO-04419);

**WHEREAS**, the Individual Defendants, through their counsel Whitfield, Nygaard & Doyle LLP, and Verdana, through its counsel Blackhall & Soren LLP, filed opposition to Cascade\'s motion for preliminary injunction on March 15, 2025, and a preliminary injunction hearing was scheduled before Vice Chancellor Zhao for March 21, 2025;

**WHEREAS**, on March 18, 2025, the Parties participated in a full-day mediation session before the Honorable Philip Ashford (Ret.) through Meridian ADR Services LLC (Ref. No. Meridian-2025-0318-CRH), at which the Parties engaged in good-faith negotiations regarding the terms of a potential resolution of the Action;

**WHEREAS**, on March 20, 2025, the Parties reached a framework for settlement of the Action, and on March 21, 2025, the preliminary injunction hearing was adjourned by stipulation of all Parties and a Consent Interim Order was entered by Vice Chancellor Zhao maintaining the status quo during the documentation of the settlement;

**WHEREAS**, the Parties desire to fully, finally, and irrevocably resolve the Action and all related disputes among them on the terms and conditions set forth herein, without any admission of liability or wrongdoing by any Party;

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants, agreements, representations, and warranties contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

**[ARTICLE I --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 1.1 --- Defined Terms.** As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below:

\"**Action**\" means the civil action captioned *Cascade Retail Holdings Inc. v. Rathore et al.*, C.A. No. 2025-0198-MTZ, filed in the Delaware Court of Chancery on March 5, 2025, together with all motions, applications, orders, and proceedings arising therefrom or related thereto.

\"**Affiliate**\" means, with respect to any Person, any other Person that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with such Person. For purposes of this definition, \"control\" means the possession, directly or indirectly, of the power to direct or cause the direction of the management and policies of a Person, whether through the ownership of voting securities, by contract, or otherwise, and the terms \"controlled by\" and \"under common control with\" shall have correlative meanings. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Greystone Capital Partners, LP and Greystone Capital Fund VII, LP shall be deemed Affiliates of Verdana.

\"**Business Day**\" means any day other than a Saturday, a Sunday, or a day on which banks in Wilmington, Delaware or Seattle, Washington are authorized or required by law or executive order to be closed, and shall further exclude any day that is a State of Delaware legal holiday.

\"**Cascade Confidential Information**\" means all proprietary and confidential information of Cascade, including without limitation Project Ridgeline materials, vendor negotiation playbooks, seasonal buying algorithms, private-label sourcing strategies, private-label cost models, customer segmentation data, ecommerce assortment algorithms, merchandising calendars, promotional pricing frameworks, supplier contract terms, logistics and distribution data, category performance analyses, workforce planning models, and any other information designated as confidential, proprietary, or trade secret by Cascade, whether in written, electronic, oral, or other form.

\"**Compliance Monitor**\" means Aldwyn Compliance Solutions LLC, a limited liability company organized under the laws of the State of Pennsylvania, with its principal offices at 1700 Market Street, Suite 2800, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania 19103, or any successor compliance monitor appointed in accordance with this Agreement.

\"**Consent Order**\" means the stipulated consent order to be entered by the Court incorporating certain terms of this Agreement, substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit F.

\"**Cost Reimbursement**\" means the amount of Four Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$425,000) payable by Verdana to Cascade pursuant to Section 4.2 of this Agreement.

\"**Court**\" means the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware.

\"**Effective Date**\" means April 14, 2025.

\"**Employment Agreements**\" means the employment agreements between Cascade and each of the Individual Defendants, as listed and described on Schedule 1 attached hereto, including the Rathore Employment Agreement and the individual employment agreements of each of the other seven Individual Defendants.

\"**Equity Forfeiture Amount**\" means the aggregate equity forfeitures described in Section 4.3 of this Agreement, totaling Eight Hundred Forty-Nine Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$849,500).

\"**Exfiltrated Data**\" means the approximately fourteen thousand three hundred twenty-seven (14,327) files, comprising approximately 2.8 gigabytes of data, identified by Pinnacle Forensics LLC as having been downloaded from Cascade\'s Aldermere Systems and Pinnacle Health IT environments to personal cloud storage accounts of certain Individual Defendants between January 10, 2025 and February 4, 2025, as more particularly described in Pinnacle\'s forensic report dated March 3, 2025.

\"**Forensic Audit**\" means the independent forensic audit of Verdana\'s relevant systems, devices, and repositories to be conducted by the Forensic Auditor pursuant to Section 5.4 of this Agreement.

\"**Forensic Auditor**\" means Pinnacle Forensics LLC, with its offices at 8700 Georgia Avenue, Suite 300, Silver Spring, Maryland 20910, under the engagement leadership of Dr. Rajiv Anand.

\"**Individual Defendants**\" means, collectively, Priya Rathore, Derek Linden, Sonia Kaczmarek, Amara Osei, Brent Halvorsen, Lucia Fernandez-Gill, Nathan Tsao, and Kira Johansson.

\"**Mediator**\" means the Honorable Philip Ashford (Ret.), who mediated the Parties\' dispute through Meridian ADR Services LLC (Ref. No. Meridian-2025-0318-CRH).

\"**Modified Non-Compete Period**\" means, (a) with respect to Rathore, the Rathore Modified Non-Compete Period as defined in Section 3.1(a), and (b) with respect to each other Individual Defendant, the nine (9)-month period defined in Section 3.1(b).

\"**Modified Non-Solicitation Period (Employees)**\" or \"**Employee Non-Solicitation Period**\" means the eighteen (18)-month period described in Section 3.2, running from February 7, 2025 through August 6, 2026.

\"**Modified Non-Solicitation Period (Vendors)**\" or \"**Vendor Non-Solicitation Period**\" means the twelve (12)-month period described in Section 3.3, running from February 7, 2025 through February 6, 2026.

\"**Monitor Period**\" means the twelve (12)-month period commencing on the Effective Date and ending on April 14, 2026.

\"**Payment Date**\" means the date that is thirty (30) days after the Effective Date, or if such date is not a Business Day, the next succeeding Business Day.

\"**Person**\" means any individual, corporation, partnership, limited liability company, trust, estate, governmental entity, or other legal entity.

\"**Project Ridgeline**\" means Cascade\'s confidential five-year category expansion strategic plan completed in October 2024, comprising market opportunity assessments, competitive positioning analyses, capital allocation models, new store format blueprints, private-label brand development roadmaps, and related strategic documents and presentations.

\"**Rathore Employment Agreement**\" means the Amended and Restated Employment Agreement between Cascade and Priya Rathore, dated March 15, 2021.

\"**Resignation Date**\" means February 7, 2025, the date on which all eight Individual Defendants simultaneously submitted their resignations from Cascade.

\"**Restricted Categories**\" means home goods, seasonal décor, and private-label apparel, as such categories are defined in Cascade\'s internal category taxonomy as of the Effective Date.

\"**Settlement Payment**\" means the amount of Eight Million Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$8,750,000) payable by Verdana to Cascade pursuant to Section 4.1 of this Agreement.

\"**Top 50 Vendors**\" means Cascade\'s top fifty (50) vendors measured by aggregate spend during fiscal year 2024, as identified and listed on Exhibit C attached hereto (filed under seal).

\"**TRO**\" means the temporary restraining order entered by Vice Chancellor Margaret T. Zhao of the Delaware Court of Chancery on March 7, 2025, in the Action.

**Section 1.2 --- Rules of Construction.** Unless the context otherwise requires:

\(a\) All headings and captions in this Agreement are for convenience of reference only and shall not define, limit, or affect the construction or interpretation of this Agreement.

\(b\) The word \"including\" and words of similar import shall mean \"including, without limitation,\" and shall not be construed to limit any general statement that precedes or follows such word to the specific or similar items or matters immediately following such word.

\(c\) References to \"days\" shall mean calendar days unless \"Business Days\" is expressly specified.

\(d\) References to \"Sections,\" \"Articles,\" \"Exhibits,\" \"Schedules,\" and \"Annexes\" are to the sections, articles, exhibits, schedules, and annexes of this Agreement unless otherwise indicated.

\(e\) The words \"herein,\" \"hereof,\" \"hereunder,\" \"hereby,\" and \"hereto\" refer to this Agreement as a whole.

\(f\) Words importing the singular shall include the plural and vice versa, and words importing any gender shall include all genders.

\(g\) References to any statute, rule, or regulation shall be deemed to include all amendments thereto, successor provisions, and regulations promulgated thereunder as in effect at the relevant time.

\(h\) The Parties have participated jointly in the negotiation and drafting of this Agreement, and in the event of an ambiguity or question of intent, this Agreement shall be construed as if drafted jointly by the Parties, and no presumption or burden of proof shall arise favoring or disfavoring any Party by virtue of the authorship of any provision of this Agreement.

\(i\) All monetary amounts referenced herein are expressed in United States Dollars.

\(j\) Each Exhibit and Schedule attached to this Agreement is incorporated herein by reference and made a part hereof.

**[ARTICLE II --- STANDSTILL AND CESSATION OF HOSTILITIES]{.underline}**

**Section 2.1 --- Standstill.** Upon execution of this Agreement, the Parties agree to maintain the status quo as established by the Consent Interim Order entered by Vice Chancellor Zhao on March 21, 2025, pending entry of the Consent Order by the Court. No Party shall take any action inconsistent with the terms of this Agreement during the period between execution of this Agreement and entry of the Consent Order by the Court. Each Party shall use its reasonable best efforts to facilitate the prompt entry of the Consent Order and shall refrain from any conduct that could reasonably be expected to frustrate or delay such entry.

**Section 2.2 --- Cessation of Litigation Activities.** Effective as of the execution of this Agreement:

\(a\) Cascade agrees not to pursue any further emergency, expedited, or interim relief in the Action, including but not limited to any renewed motion for preliminary injunction, any motion for contempt, any motion for expedited discovery, or any request for extension or modification of the TRO, provided that the Individual Defendants and Verdana comply with the terms of this Agreement and the Consent Interim Order.

\(b\) The Individual Defendants and Verdana agree not to file any motions to dissolve, vacate, or modify the TRO or the Consent Interim Order, except as expressly contemplated by the terms of this Agreement. The Individual Defendants and Verdana further agree not to file any counterclaims, cross-claims, or third-party claims in the Action or any related proceeding, and hereby waive any right to do so with respect to matters released under Article VII.

\(c\) All discovery obligations in the Action, including any outstanding document requests, interrogatories, and deposition notices, are stayed and shall be deemed withdrawn upon entry of the Consent Order.

**Section 2.3 --- Consent Order.**
