**[SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND MUTUAL RELEASE]{.underline}**

This Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release (this \"**Agreement**\") is entered into as of June 12, 2023 (the \"**Effective Date**\"), by and between:

**Cascade Retail Holdings Inc.**, a Delaware corporation, with its principal place of business at 2200 Elliott Avenue West, Suite 1400, Seattle, WA 98119 (\"**Cascade**\" or \"**CRH**\"); and

**Vantor Holdings Corp.**, a California corporation, with its principal place of business at 18500 Von Karman Avenue, Suite 600, Irvine, CA 92612 (\"**Vantor**\" or \"**VHC**\").

Cascade and Vantor are each referred to herein individually as a \"**Party**\" and collectively as the \"**Parties**.\"

**[RECITALS]{.underline}**

**WHEREAS:**

**A.** *The Action.* On September 7, 2021, Vantor filed a complaint against Cascade in the Superior Court of the State of California, County of Los Angeles, captioned *Vantor Holdings Corp. v. Cascade Retail Holdings Inc.*, Case No. 21STCV-34872 (the \"**Action**\"). Cascade was duly served with the summons and complaint on September 28, 2021. The Action has been pending before the Honorable Sandra Gutierrez-Torres, Department 14 of the Los Angeles County Superior Court, Stanley Mosk Courthouse, since that time.

**B.** *Claims Asserted.* In the Action, Vantor asserted three causes of action against Cascade: (1) tortious interference with contractual relations; (2) tortious interference with prospective economic advantage; and (3) unfair business practices in violation of California Business and Professions Code Section 17200 *et seq*. Specifically, Vantor alleged that Cascade knowingly and intentionally induced three of Vantor\'s key consumer-goods suppliers --- Hemsworth Consumer Products LLC (\"**Hemsworth**\"), Tridale Manufacturing Inc. (\"**Tridale**\"), and Orion Lifestyle Brands Corp. (\"**Orion**\") --- to breach their respective exclusive supply agreements with Vantor by, among other things, offering substantially more favorable pricing and volume commitments to those suppliers through a coordinated procurement initiative that Cascade internally designated as \"Project Atlas.\" Vantor alleged that, as a direct and proximate result of Cascade\'s conduct, Vantor suffered total damages in an amount of approximately Eighty-Seven Million Four Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$87,400,000), comprising lost revenues, lost profits, increased procurement costs from replacement suppliers, and reputational harm.

**C.** *Cascade\'s Defenses.* Cascade denied all of the material allegations set forth in Vantor\'s complaint. On October 18, 2021, Cascade timely filed its answer and asserted numerous affirmative defenses, including, among others, that Cascade lacked actual or constructive knowledge of the exclusivity provisions contained in Vantor\'s supplier agreements, that the Suppliers independently and voluntarily chose to enter into supply agreements with Cascade based on legitimate business considerations, that the Suppliers properly exercised termination-for-convenience clauses contained in their respective agreements with Vantor prior to entering into agreements with Cascade, that Vantor\'s exclusivity provisions were unenforceable as unreasonable restraints on trade, and that Vantor failed to mitigate its alleged damages.

**D.** *Partial Summary Judgment.* On February 28, 2023, Cascade filed a motion for partial summary judgment on all three of Vantor\'s causes of action, supported by declarations, deposition transcripts, and documentary evidence obtained during the course of discovery. On April 14, 2023, after full briefing and oral argument, the Court entered an order (i) granting summary judgment in favor of Cascade on Vantor\'s third cause of action for unfair business practices under California Business and Professions Code Section 17200, finding that Vantor had failed to demonstrate a sufficient causal nexus between Cascade\'s alleged conduct and any injury to the public, and (ii) denying summary judgment as to Vantor\'s first and second causes of action for tortious interference with contractual relations and tortious interference with prospective economic advantage, respectively, finding that genuine issues of material fact remained as to Cascade\'s knowledge of the exclusivity provisions and intent to interfere.

**E.** *Settlement Conference and Agreement in Principle.* On April 28, 2023, the Parties participated in a mandatory settlement conference before the Honorable Margaret Chen (Ret.) at JAMS in Los Angeles, California. After a full day of mediation, the Parties were unable to reach a resolution at the conference. However, through subsequent negotiations conducted by their respective counsel, the Parties reached an agreement in principle on May 15, 2023, to settle and resolve the Action on the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement.

**F.** *Desire to Resolve.* The Parties desire to fully and finally settle, compromise, and resolve any and all claims, counterclaims, causes of action, disputes, and controversies between them that have been asserted, or that could have been asserted, arising out of or in any way related to the Action, on the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement. The Parties enter into this Agreement to avoid the expense, burden, inconvenience, and uncertainty of further litigation, without any admission of liability, wrongdoing, fault, or any violation of law by either Party.

**G.** *Counsel.* Cascade is represented in the Action and in connection with this Agreement by Calderwood & Harkness LLP (Douglas Carmichael, Responsible Partner; Francesca Morano, Billing Partner), with offices located at 600 South Grand Avenue, Suite 3200, Los Angeles, CA 90071. Vantor is represented in the Action and in connection with this Agreement by Kessler, Brandt & Whitfield LLP (Martin Kessler, Senior Partner; Natalie Whitfield, Partner), with offices located at 1999 Avenue of the Stars, Suite 2800, Los Angeles, CA 90067.

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants, promises, and agreements set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

**[ARTICLE I --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Article I shall have the meanings ascribed to them elsewhere in this Agreement.

**Section 1.1 --- \"Action.\"** \"Action\" means the civil action captioned *Vantor Holdings Corp. v. Cascade Retail Holdings Inc.*, Case No. 21STCV-34872, filed in and pending before the Superior Court of the State of California, County of Los Angeles, including all claims, cross-claims, counterclaims, and motions filed therein.

**Section 1.2 --- \"Cascade Released Parties.\"** \"Cascade Released Parties\" means, collectively, Cascade Retail Holdings Inc. and each of its past, present, and future officers, directors, employees, agents, representatives, subsidiaries, affiliates, parent entities, successors, assigns, attorneys (including Calderwood & Harkness LLP and all individual attorneys who have appeared or provided services in connection with the Action), accountants, auditors (including, without limitation, Granville & Associates, P.C.), insurers (including, without limitation, Pinnacle National Insurance Co.), consultants (including, without limitation, Archer & Colvin Consulting Group), and any other person or entity acting on behalf of or for the benefit of any of the foregoing.

**Section 1.3 --- \"Vantor Released Parties.\"** \"Vantor Released Parties\" means, collectively, Vantor Holdings Corp. and each of its past, present, and future officers, directors, employees, agents, representatives, subsidiaries, affiliates, parent entities, successors, assigns, attorneys (including Kessler, Brandt & Whitfield LLP and all individual attorneys who have appeared or provided services in connection with the Action), accountants, auditors, insurers, consultants (including, without limitation, Meridian Forensic Economics LLC), and any other person or entity acting on behalf of or for the benefit of any of the foregoing.

**Section 1.4 --- \"Effective Date.\"** \"Effective Date\" means June 12, 2023, the date first written above.

**Section 1.5 --- \"Released Claims.\"** \"Released Claims\" means any and all claims, demands, actions, causes of action, suits, debts, dues, sums of money, accounts, reckonings, bonds, bills, specialties, covenants, contracts, controversies, agreements, promises, variances, trespasses, damages, judgments, extents, executions, obligations, liabilities, losses, costs, expenses, and attorneys\' fees, of every kind and nature whatsoever, whether known or unknown, asserted or unasserted, suspected or unsuspected, fixed or contingent, accrued or unaccrued, liquidated or unliquidated, matured or unmatured, at law, in equity, or otherwise, arising out of, relating to, or in any way connected with: (a) the Action; (b) the allegations, claims, defenses, and subject matter asserted or that could have been asserted in the Action; (c) the supplier relationships between Vantor and Hemsworth Consumer Products LLC, Tridale Manufacturing Inc., and Orion Lifestyle Brands Corp., to the extent such relationships are the subject of or relate to the allegations in the Action; (d) the supplier relationships between Cascade and Hemsworth Consumer Products LLC, Tridale Manufacturing Inc., and Orion Lifestyle Brands Corp., to the extent such relationships are the subject of or relate to the allegations in the Action; (e) Cascade\'s \"Project Atlas\" initiative as alleged in the Action; and (f) any conduct, acts, omissions, transactions, events, or occurrences alleged in the complaint, answer, or any pleading, motion, or discovery response filed in the Action or relating to the matters described therein.

**Section 1.6 --- \"Settlement Amount.\"** \"Settlement Amount\" means Fourteen Million Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars and No Cents (\$14,750,000.00).

**Section 1.7 --- \"Suppliers.\"** \"Suppliers\" means, collectively: (a) Hemsworth Consumer Products LLC, an Oregon limited liability company with its principal place of business at 4720 NW Yeon Avenue, Portland, OR 97210; (b) Tridale Manufacturing Inc., a Nevada corporation with its principal place of business at 6300 South Pecos Road, Suite 210, Las Vegas, NV 89120; and (c) Orion Lifestyle Brands Corp., a California corporation with its principal place of business at 1900 Avenue of the Stars, Suite 1050, Los Angeles, CA 90067.

**[ARTICLE II --- SETTLEMENT PAYMENT]{.underline}**

**Section 2.1 --- Payment Amount.** In consideration of the mutual covenants, releases, and agreements set forth in this Agreement, Cascade shall pay to Vantor the Settlement Amount of Fourteen Million Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars and No Cents (\$14,750,000.00) in full and final satisfaction of all Released Claims. The Settlement Amount represents the total and complete consideration to be paid by Cascade or any of the Cascade Released Parties in connection with the settlement of the Action, and no additional amounts shall be owed or payable by Cascade or any Cascade Released Party to Vantor or any Vantor Released Party in connection with the Released Claims.

**Section 2.2 --- Payment Method and Timing.** The Settlement Amount shall be paid by Cascade to Vantor by wire transfer of immediately available funds in United States Dollars to a bank account designated by Vantor in writing. Vantor shall provide Cascade with complete and accurate wire transfer instructions, including the name of the receiving financial institution, ABA routing number, account number, account name, and any required reference information, within five (5) business days following the full execution and delivery of this Agreement by both Parties. Cascade shall cause the wire transfer of the full Settlement Amount to be initiated within thirty (30) calendar days following the Effective Date. Cascade\'s payment obligation shall be deemed satisfied upon confirmation by Cascade\'s bank that the wire transfer has been initiated in accordance with the wire instructions provided by Vantor. In the event that Vantor fails to provide wire transfer instructions within the time period specified herein, the thirty (30) calendar day payment deadline shall be extended on a day-for-day basis until the wire instructions are received by Cascade.

**Section 2.3 --- Tax Treatment.** The Parties make no representations or warranties regarding the tax characterization or tax treatment of the Settlement Amount under federal, state, local, or foreign tax law. Each Party shall be solely responsible for the payment of any and all taxes, including income taxes, penalties, and interest, owed by such Party in connection with the receipt or payment of the Settlement Amount. Vantor shall be solely responsible for determining whether the issuance of any IRS Form 1099 or other tax reporting form is required in connection with its receipt of the Settlement Amount, and, if so required, for the timely issuance thereof. Neither Party shall have any obligation to indemnify or hold harmless the other Party with respect to any tax liability arising from the receipt or payment of the Settlement Amount.

**Section 2.4 --- Source of Funds.** The Settlement Amount shall be funded from Cascade\'s operating funds and applicable insurance proceeds. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the source or sources from which Cascade funds the Settlement Amount shall not affect, diminish, or otherwise modify Cascade\'s obligation to make timely payment of the full Settlement Amount to Vantor in accordance with Section 2.2. In the event that any insurer fails or refuses to fund any portion of the Settlement Amount, Cascade shall remain solely and fully responsible for payment of the entire Settlement Amount.

**[ARTICLE III --- NON-ADMISSION OF LIABILITY]{.underline}**

**Section 3.1 --- No Admission by Cascade.** This Agreement, the payment of the Settlement Amount, and the settlement of the Action shall not constitute, and shall not be construed as, an admission of liability, wrongdoing, fault, negligence, or any violation of any statute, regulation, or rule of law by Cascade or any of the Cascade Released Parties. Cascade specifically and expressly denies all allegations of liability, wrongdoing, and fault asserted by Vantor in the Action. The Parties acknowledge that Cascade is entering into this Agreement solely to avoid the expense, burden, inconvenience, distraction, and uncertainty associated with continued litigation.

**Section 3.2 --- No Admission by Vantor.** This Agreement shall not constitute, and shall not be construed as, a concession, admission, or acknowledgment by Vantor that any of its claims asserted in the Action lacked merit, were frivolous, were brought in bad faith, or were otherwise deficient in any respect. The Parties acknowledge that Vantor is entering into this Agreement in the exercise of its reasonable business judgment and in consideration of the Settlement Amount and the other terms and conditions set forth herein.

**Section 3.3 --- Inadmissibility.** This Agreement, including all of its terms and conditions, the negotiations and discussions leading to the execution of this Agreement, the Settlement Amount, and any statements, offers, or representations made by either Party or its counsel during the course of settlement negotiations shall be inadmissible in any judicial, arbitral, administrative, or other legal proceeding for any purpose, including but not limited to as evidence of liability, wrongdoing, or the validity or invalidity of any claim or defense. Notwithstanding the foregoing, this Agreement may be introduced into evidence and used in any proceeding to enforce the terms and provisions of this Agreement, to enforce the Joint Stipulation of Dismissal with Prejudice referenced in Article V, or to assert the releases set forth in Article IV as a defense to any claim.

**[ARTICLE IV --- MUTUAL RELEASE]{.underline}**

**Section 4.1 --- Release by Vantor.** Effective upon the Effective Date and conditioned upon Cascade\'s timely payment of the Settlement Amount in accordance with Article II, Vantor, on behalf of itself, its successors, assigns, and each of the Vantor Released Parties, hereby fully, finally, unconditionally, and irrevocably releases, acquits, and forever discharges Cascade and each of the Cascade Released Parties from any and all Released Claims, including but not limited to:

> \(a\) Vantor\'s first cause of action for tortious interference with contractual relations, as asserted in the Action;
>
> \(b\) Vantor\'s second cause of action for tortious interference with prospective economic advantage, as asserted in the Action;
>
> \(c\) Vantor\'s third cause of action for unfair business practices under California Business and Professions Code Section 17200 *et seq.*, as asserted in the Action (which cause of action was dismissed by the Court\'s order of April 14, 2023, granting Cascade\'s motion for partial summary judgment);
>
> \(d\) Any and all claims, whether or not asserted in the Action, arising from or related to the supplier relationships between Vantor and each of the Suppliers --- Hemsworth Consumer Products LLC, Tridale Manufacturing Inc., and Orion Lifestyle Brands Corp. --- to the extent such claims relate to the subject matter of the Action;
>
> \(e\) Any and all claims, whether or not asserted in the Action, arising from or related to Cascade\'s \"Project Atlas\" initiative, including any procurement activities, negotiations, or agreements entered into by Cascade with any of the Suppliers; and
>
> \(f\) Any and all claims for damages, including but not limited to compensatory damages, consequential damages, lost profits, punitive damages, statutory damages, restitution, disgorgement, injunctive relief, declaratory relief, attorneys\' fees, costs, and interest, arising out of or related to any of the foregoing.

**Section 4.2 --- Release by Cascade.** Effective upon the Effective Date, Cascade, on behalf of itself, its successors, assigns, and each of the Cascade Released Parties, hereby fully, finally, unconditionally, and irrevocably releases, acquits, and forever discharges Vantor and each of the Vantor Released Parties from any and all Released Claims, including but not limited to:

> \(a\) Any claims for malicious prosecution arising out of or related to the filing or prosecution of the Action;
>
> \(b\) Any claims for abuse of process arising out of or related to the Action;
>
> \(c\) Any claims for tortious interference, defamation, trade libel, or unfair competition arising out of or related to statements, allegations, or conduct by Vantor or any Vantor Released Party in connection with the Action or the events giving rise to the Action;
>
> \(d\) Any claims for attorneys\' fees, costs, or sanctions arising out of or related to the Action; and
>
> \(e\) Any and all other claims, whether known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, arising out of or related to the Action or the subject matter thereof.

**Section 4.3 --- Waiver of California Civil Code Section 1542.** Each Party acknowledges that it has been advised by its counsel regarding the provisions of Section 1542 of the California Civil Code. Each Party expressly waives and relinquishes all rights and benefits afforded by Section 1542 of the California Civil Code, which provides as follows:

> *\"A general release does not extend to claims that the creditor or releasing party does not know or suspect to exist in his or her favor at the time of executing the release and that, if known by him or her, would have materially affected his or her settlement with the debtor or released party.\"*

Each Party understands and acknowledges the significance and consequence of this specific waiver of Section 1542 of the California Civil Code. Each Party acknowledges that it may discover facts different from, or in addition to, those it now knows or believes to be true with respect to the Released Claims, the subject matter of this Agreement, or the Action, and each Party agrees that this Agreement shall be and remain effective in all respects notwithstanding such different or additional facts or the discovery thereof. Each Party assumes the risk of any mistake of fact or law with respect to any Released Claim, and each Party agrees that this release is intended to be, and is, a full and final release of the Released Claims regardless of any such mistake.

**Section 4.4 --- Scope of Release.** The mutual releases set forth in this Article IV extend to all Released Claims, regardless of the legal or equitable theory upon which such claims are or could be based, including but not limited to claims based on contract (whether express, implied, or quasi-contractual), tort (whether intentional, negligent, or strict liability), statute, regulation, ordinance, or any other legal or equitable theory, and regardless of whether such claims arise under federal, state, or local law, including but not limited to claims under the California Business and Professions Code (including Section 17200 *et seq.*), the California Civil Code, the California Commercial Code, the Lanham Act, and the common law of any jurisdiction. The Parties intend that the releases set forth herein be construed as broadly as possible to effectuate the Parties\' intent to fully and finally resolve all disputes between them relating to the Action and the subject matter thereof.

**[ARTICLE V --- DISMISSAL OF ACTION]{.underline}**

**Section 5.1 --- Stipulation of Dismissal.** Within ten (10) business days following the Effective Date, the Parties shall execute, or shall cause their respective counsel of record to prepare, execute, and file with the Superior Court of the State of California, County of Los Angeles, a Joint Stipulation of Dismissal with Prejudice (the \"**Stipulation of Dismissal**\") in the Action (Case No. 21STCV-34872), dismissing with prejudice all claims, counterclaims, and cross-claims asserted in the Action. The Stipulation of Dismissal shall provide that each Party shall bear its own attorneys\' fees, costs, and expenses incurred in connection with the Action, except as otherwise expressly provided in this Agreement. The Parties shall cooperate in good faith to prepare and file the Stipulation of Dismissal in a form acceptable to both Parties and their respective counsel.

**Section 5.2 --- Court Retention of Jurisdiction.** The Stipulation of Dismissal filed pursuant to Section 5.1 shall expressly provide that the Superior Court of the State of California, County of Los Angeles, shall retain jurisdiction over the Parties and the subject matter of this Agreement for the purpose of enforcing the terms and provisions of this Agreement, including the settlement payment obligations set forth in Article II, pursuant to California Code of Civil Procedure Section 664.6. The Parties consent to such continued jurisdiction and agree not to oppose any motion to enforce this Agreement brought pursuant to Section 664.6 on the ground that the Court lacks jurisdiction.

**[ARTICLE VI --- CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**

**Section 6.1 --- Confidential Terms.** The Parties agree that the terms and conditions of this Agreement, including without limitation the Settlement Amount, the payment terms, the specific provisions of the mutual releases, and any information exchanged between the Parties during settlement negotiations, shall be and shall remain strictly confidential and shall not be disclosed, disseminated, published, or otherwise communicated to any third party, except as expressly set forth in Section 6.2 below. Each Party shall take all reasonable steps to ensure that its officers, directors, employees, agents, and representatives comply with the confidentiality obligations set forth in this Section 6.1.

**Section 6.2 --- Permitted Disclosures.** Notwithstanding Section 6.1, the Parties may disclose the terms and conditions of this Agreement under the following circumstances:

> \(a\) To their respective attorneys, accountants, auditors, tax advisors, and financial advisors who have a reasonable need to know such information in connection with the provision of professional services to the disclosing Party, provided that such persons are informed of the confidential nature of this Agreement and agree to maintain the confidentiality thereof;
>
> \(b\) To their respective insurers, including without limitation Pinnacle National Insurance Co. (for Cascade), as reasonably necessary to obtain insurance contributions, reimbursement, or coverage in connection with the Settlement Amount or the Action;
>
> \(c\) As required by applicable federal, state, or local law, regulation, or regulatory requirement, including without limitation any securities disclosure obligations to which Cascade may be subject as a publicly traded company listed on the Nasdaq Stock Market (ticker symbol: CRHI), including disclosures required under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, and the rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission promulgated thereunder;
>
> \(d\) In response to a valid subpoena, court order, or governmental investigation or inquiry, provided that the disclosing Party shall, to the extent legally permissible, give the other Party prompt written notice of such required disclosure (and in any event not less than ten (10) business days\' prior written notice, if practicable) and a reasonable opportunity to seek a protective order, motion to quash, or other appropriate relief prior to such disclosure;
>
> \(e\) As reasonably necessary to enforce the terms and provisions of this Agreement in any legal proceeding; and
>
> \(f\) As otherwise agreed in writing by both Parties.

**Section 6.3 --- Public Statements.** In the event that either Party is asked about the resolution of the Action by any member of the press, media, industry analyst, business partner, supplier, customer, or any other person or entity, such Party may state only that \"the matter has been resolved to the mutual satisfaction of the parties\" and shall not disclose the Settlement Amount, any other financial terms, or any other specific terms or conditions of this Agreement. Each Party shall use reasonable efforts to ensure that its officers, directors, employees, agents, representatives, and counsel comply with this limitation on public statements.

**[ARTICLE VII --- NON-DISPARAGEMENT]{.underline}**

**Section 7.1 --- Mutual Non-Disparagement.** Each Party agrees that it shall not, and shall cause its officers, directors, and authorized spokespersons not to, directly or indirectly, make, publish, issue, or cause to be made, published, or issued any disparaging, derogatory, defamatory, or negative statements, comments, or remarks, whether written, oral, electronic, or in any other medium, about the other Party, its officers, directors, employees, products, services, business practices, financial condition, or corporate reputation, in connection with the Action, the events giving rise to the Action, the settlement of the Action, or this Agreement. For purposes of this Section 7.1, \"disparaging\" means any statement that is reasonably likely to diminish the reputation of the other Party or any of its officers, directors, employees, products, or services in the estimation of a reasonable person.

**Section 7.2 --- Scope.** Without limiting the generality of Section 7.1, the non-disparagement obligation set forth herein applies specifically to the following individuals in their capacities as officers, directors, or authorized representatives of the respective Parties:

> \(a\) On behalf of Vantor: Richard \"Rick\" Ellsworth (Founder and Chief Executive Officer), Patricia Sung (Chief Financial Officer), Thomas Brennecke (Executive Vice President, Supply Chain Operations), and Deborah Marcelino (Senior Vice President, Legal Affairs and General Counsel); and
>
> \(b\) On behalf of Cascade: Margaret Prumvane (Chief Executive Officer), Raj Subramanian (President and Chief Operating Officer), Lena Torvik (Executive Vice President, Procurement and Strategic Sourcing), David Pruitt (General Counsel and Corporate Secretary), and Annika Bergström (Senior Vice President, Corporate Communications and Investor Relations).

Each Party shall use reasonable efforts to inform the individuals identified in this Section 7.2 of the non-disparagement obligations set forth herein.

**Section 7.3 --- Exceptions.** The non-disparagement obligations set forth in this Article VII shall not apply to:

> \(a\) Truthful testimony or statements compelled by a valid subpoena, court order, or other legal process in any judicial, arbitral, administrative, or regulatory proceeding;
>
> \(b\) Communications with governmental agencies, regulatory authorities, or law enforcement agencies, including any statements made in response to inquiries from or investigations by the Securities and Exchange Commission, the Federal Trade Commission, or any state attorney general\'s office; or
>
> \(c\) Statements made in the good-faith exercise of any Party\'s or individual\'s legal rights, including the filing of any complaint, charge, or report with any governmental agency.

**[ARTICLE VIII --- NO INJUNCTIVE RELIEF; NO RESTRICTIONS ON FUTURE BUSINESS]{.underline}**

**Section 8.1 --- No Injunctive Relief.** This Agreement does not include, and shall not be construed to include, any form of injunctive, equitable, or declaratory relief of any kind or nature. Neither Party is enjoined, restrained, or otherwise restricted by this Agreement from engaging in any lawful business activity, and this Agreement shall not be interpreted as imposing any non-compete, non-solicitation, or similar restrictive covenant on either Party.

**Section 8.2 --- No Restrictions on Cascade\'s Supplier Relationships.** Nothing in this Agreement shall restrict, limit, impair, or otherwise affect Cascade\'s right to enter into, maintain, renew, extend, modify, or expand supply agreements, purchase agreements, distribution agreements, or any other commercial arrangements with any supplier, manufacturer, distributor, or vendor, including but not limited to Hemsworth Consumer Products LLC, Tridale Manufacturing Inc., and Orion Lifestyle Brands Corp. The Parties acknowledge that, as of the Effective Date, Cascade maintains the following existing agreements with the Suppliers, and this Agreement shall not affect or modify such agreements in any respect:

> \(a\) Supply Agreement with Hemsworth Consumer Products LLC, having a five (5)-year term, effective June 1, 2021, with an annual commitment of approximately Twenty-Eight Million Dollars (\$28,000,000);
>
> \(b\) Supply Agreement with Tridale Manufacturing Inc., having a three (3)-year term, effective August 15, 2021, with an annual commitment of approximately Nineteen Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$19,500,000); and
>
> \(c\) Supply Agreement with Orion Lifestyle Brands Corp., having a four (4)-year term, effective May 10, 2021, with an annual commitment of approximately Thirty-One Million Dollars (\$31,000,000).

**Section 8.3 --- No Restrictions on Vantor\'s Supplier Relationships.** Nothing in this Agreement shall restrict, limit, impair, or otherwise affect Vantor\'s right to enter into, maintain, renew, extend, modify, or expand supply agreements, purchase agreements, distribution agreements, or any other commercial arrangements with any supplier, manufacturer, distributor, or vendor, including but not limited to the right to pursue new exclusive supply arrangements or similar commercial relationships with any supplier, including the Suppliers.

**[ARTICLE IX --- REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES]{.underline}**

**Section 9.1 --- Authority.** Each Party represents and warrants to the other Party that: (a) it is a corporation or other legal entity duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of its state of incorporation or formation; (b) it has full corporate power and authority to enter into this Agreement, to perform its obligations hereunder, and to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby; (c) the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement by such Party has been duly authorized by all necessary corporate action, including any required approval by its board of directors or other governing body; and (d) this Agreement constitutes the valid, binding, and enforceable obligation of such Party, enforceable against such Party in accordance with its terms, subject to applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, fraudulent conveyance, and other similar laws affecting creditors\' rights generally and to general principles of equity.

**Section 9.2 --- Signatory Authority.** Each individual executing this Agreement on behalf of a Party represents and warrants that he or she is duly authorized to execute and deliver this Agreement on behalf of such Party and that such execution and delivery will bind such Party to the terms and conditions set forth herein. For Cascade, this Agreement is executed by David Pruitt, in his capacity as General Counsel and Corporate Secretary, acting pursuant to authorization from the Board of Directors of Cascade Retail Holdings Inc. For Vantor, this Agreement is executed by Richard \"Rick\" Ellsworth, in his capacity as Founder and Chief Executive Officer, acting pursuant to authorization from the Board of Directors of Vantor Holdings Corp.

**Section 9.3 --- No Assignment of Claims.** Each Party represents and warrants that, as of the Effective Date, it has not assigned, transferred, conveyed, pledged, hypothecated, or otherwise disposed of any of the Released Claims, or any interest therein, to any third party, and that no other person or entity has any interest in any of the Released Claims by virtue of any assignment, transfer, subrogation, or other transaction.

**Section 9.4 --- Voluntary Execution.** Each Party represents and warrants that it has entered into this Agreement voluntarily and of its own free will, after careful consideration and deliberation, and after consultation with its legal counsel. Each Party represents that it has not been coerced, intimidated, threatened, or unduly influenced by any person, entity, or circumstance in making its decision to enter into this Agreement. Cascade acknowledges that it has been advised in connection with this Agreement and the Action by its counsel of record, Calderwood & Harkness LLP. Vantor acknowledges that it has been advised in connection with this Agreement and the Action by its counsel of record, Kessler, Brandt & Whitfield LLP.

**Section 9.5 --- Understanding of Terms.** Each Party represents and warrants that it has read this Agreement in its entirety, that it fully understands all of the terms, conditions, and provisions contained herein, including the significance and legal consequences of the mutual releases set forth in Article IV and the waiver of California Civil Code Section 1542 set forth in Section 4.3, and that it has had a full and adequate opportunity to ask questions of its counsel and to negotiate the terms of this Agreement prior to execution.

**[ARTICLE X --- INDEMNIFICATION]{.underline}**

**Section 10.1 --- Indemnification by Vantor.** Vantor agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the Cascade Released Parties from and against any and all claims, actions, suits, proceedings, demands, judgments, losses, damages, liabilities, costs, or expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees and costs of litigation) arising out of or related to: (a) any breach by Vantor of any of its representations, warranties, covenants, or obligations under this Agreement; (b) any assertion by any third party of any claim that has been released by Vantor pursuant to Article IV; or (c) any misrepresentation by Vantor in connection with this Agreement.

**Section 10.2 --- Indemnification by Cascade.** Cascade agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the Vantor Released Parties from and against any and all claims, actions, suits, proceedings, demands, judgments, losses, damages, liabilities, costs, or expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees and costs of litigation) arising out of or related to: (a) any breach by Cascade of any of its representations, warranties, covenants, or obligations under this Agreement; (b) any assertion by any third party of any claim that has been released by Cascade pursuant to Article IV; or (c) any misrepresentation by Cascade in connection with this Agreement.

**[SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND MUTUAL RELEASE]{.underline}**

**(Execution Version)**

**April 22, 2024**

*Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC, et al.* Case No. 1021-00006 Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida

CONFIDENTIAL --- SUBJECT TO CONFIDENTIALITY PROVISIONS OF ARTICLE XII

Right-click to update Table of Contents

**SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND MUTUAL RELEASE**

This **SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND MUTUAL RELEASE** (this \"Agreement\") is entered into and made effective as of April 22, 2024 (the \"Effective Date\"), by and among the following parties:

**VERIMARK HOSPITALITY GROUP INC.**, a Delaware corporation, with its principal place of business at 2400 East Las Olas Boulevard, Suite 3100, Fort Lauderdale, Florida 33301, and whose common stock is listed on the Nasdaq Stock Market under the ticker symbol \"VHMK\" (hereinafter referred to as \"Verimark\" or \"VHG\");

and

**COASTAL PALMS FRANCHISE HOLDINGS LLC**, a Florida limited liability company, with its principal office at 9500 Gulf Shore Drive, Suite 450, Naples, Florida 34108 (hereinafter referred to as \"Coastal Palms\" or \"CPFH\");

**RANDALL \"RANDY\" BRECKER**, an individual residing in the State of Florida, who serves as the Managing Member and holds a sixty percent (60%) equity interest in Coastal Palms, and who also serves as the President of Suncoast Room Management Inc. (hereinafter referred to as \"R. Brecker\");

**THERESA BRECKER**, an individual residing in the State of Florida, who is a Member of and holds a fifteen percent (15%) equity interest in Coastal Palms (hereinafter referred to as \"T. Brecker\");

**NOLAN PRESCOTT**, an individual residing in the State of Florida, who is a Member of and holds a twenty-five percent (25%) equity interest in Coastal Palms (hereinafter referred to as \"Prescott\");

**GULF BREEZE HOSPITALITY LLC**, a Florida limited liability company (hereinafter referred to as \"Gulf Breeze\");

**SAVANNAH LODGING PARTNERS LLC**, a Georgia limited liability company (hereinafter referred to as \"Savannah Lodging\");

**SUNCOAST ROOM MANAGEMENT INC.**, a Florida corporation (hereinafter referred to as \"Suncoast\");

Coastal Palms, R. Brecker, T. Brecker, Prescott, Gulf Breeze, Savannah Lodging, and Suncoast are collectively referred to herein as the \"Coastal Palms Parties.\" Verimark and the Coastal Palms Parties are collectively referred to herein as the \"Parties\" and each individually as a \"Party.\"

**[RECITALS]{.underline}**

**WHEREAS:**

**A. Franchise Relationship.** Verimark operates and franchises approximately 340 branded hotel properties across the southeastern United States under the \"Verimark Suites,\" \"Verimark Select,\" and \"Verimark Grand\" flags. For fiscal year 2021, Verimark reported consolidated revenue of approximately \$1.42 billion, of which the franchise segment contributed approximately \$218 million. Coastal Palms is the operator of twenty-two (22) franchised hotel properties --- eighteen (18) operating under the Verimark Suites flag and four (4) operating under the Verimark Select flag --- located across the States of Florida and Georgia, comprising approximately 3,740 total guest rooms. The first Franchise License Agreement (\"FLA\") between Verimark and Coastal Palms was executed on June 15, 2007, for a Verimark Suites property located in Naples, Florida. Over the following years, Coastal Palms and its affiliates executed a total of twenty-two (22) individual FLAs with Verimark, the most recent of which was dated September 3, 2019. Each FLA provides for a twenty (20)-year initial term and is governed by the laws of the State of Florida, with mandatory venue for any disputes in Broward County, Florida. Under each FLA, Coastal Palms is required to pay the following fees: (i) a royalty equal to five percent (5%) of Gross Room Revenue (\"GRR\") (FLA § 4.1); (ii) a marketing-fund contribution equal to two and one-half percent (2.5%) of GRR (FLA § 4.2); and (iii) a technology fee of twelve dollars and fifty cents (\$12.50) per available room per month, adjusted annually for changes in the Consumer Price Index, with such adjustment capped at three percent (3%) per year (FLA § 4.3). Late-payment interest under the FLAs accrues at a rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, compounded monthly (FLA § 4.6). Additionally, FLA § 15.3 provides for liquidated damages upon termination for cause in an amount equal to three times (3×) the trailing-twelve-month royalties per property.

**B. The Litigation.** On November 8, 2021, a former Coastal Palms regional controller, Janet Kerrigan, reported to Verimark\'s compliance hotline allegations of systematic revenue underreporting by the Coastal Palms Parties. In response, Verimark retained Thornbury & Associates CPAs LLP to conduct a franchise-compliance audit of the Coastal Palms properties. Thornbury\'s preliminary findings, delivered to Verimark on January 18, 2022, indicated that the audited properties had underreported GRR by approximately twenty-six percent (26%) for the period spanning fiscal years 2019 through 2021. Verimark issued a Notice of Material Breach to Coastal Palms on February 4, 2022, demanding that Coastal Palms cure the identified breaches within thirty (30) days in accordance with FLA § 14.1. Coastal Palms, through its counsel Whitfield, Barrow & Crane LLP, responded by letter dated February 28, 2022, denying any material breach and contesting the methodology and conclusions of the Thornbury audit. No cure was tendered by Coastal Palms within the thirty (30)-day period, which expired on March 6, 2022. On March 7, 2022, Verimark filed a ten-count Complaint in the Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida, bearing Case Number 1021-00006 (the \"Litigation\"), asserting claims for: (i) breach of contract --- royalties; (ii) breach of contract --- marketing fund; (iii) breach of contract --- technology fees; (iv) breach of the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing; (v) fraudulent concealment; (vi) negligent misrepresentation; (vii) unjust enrichment; (viii) declaratory judgment; (ix) accounting; and (x) civil conspiracy. In the Complaint, Verimark claimed damages in the approximate aggregate amount of \$150,000,000, consisting of: (a) \$16,095,000 in direct underpayments of royalties, marketing-fund contributions, and technology fees; (b) \$28,400,000 in contractual late-payment interest calculated in accordance with FLA § 4.6; and (c) \$105,500,000 in liquidated damages calculated in accordance with FLA § 15.3. On April 18, 2022, Coastal Palms filed its Answer, Affirmative Defenses, and Counterclaim, asserting a counterclaim in the amount of \$12,000,000 for alleged brand-standard violations by Verimark and alleged over-billing for technology services. During discovery, Verimark\'s forensic accounting expert, Dr. Sharon Kettlewell, CPA/CFF, CFE, of Ridgeline Forensic Advisory LLC, prepared an expert report estimating cumulative underreported GRR of \$197,800,000 over the period from 2013 through 2021. Coastal Palms\' damages expert, Professor Grant Hargrove, PhD, CPA, of Hargrove Economic Consulting Inc., prepared a competing expert report opining that any underpayment totaled no more than \$6,200,000.

**C. Summary Judgment Ruling.** On February 9, 2024, the Court (the Honorable Richard M. Calloway, Circuit Judge) entered an Order granting Verimark\'s Motion for Partial Summary Judgment on Count I (Breach of Contract --- Royalties) and Count II (Breach of Contract --- Marketing Fund), finding as a matter of law that Coastal Palms\' exclusion of revenues collected by Suncoast Room Management Inc. from its calculation and reporting of GRR constituted a material breach of FLA §§ 4.1 and 4.2. The Court denied Coastal Palms\' Cross-Motion for Summary Judgment on all counts and deferred the determination of damages to trial.

**D. Mediation and Settlement.** On February 23, 2024, the Parties agreed to submit their dispute to mediation before the Honorable Patricia Everwood (Retired), of Everwood Dispute Resolution PLLC. A two-day mediation session was conducted on March 14 and 15, 2024, at 396 Alhambra Circle, Suite 800, Coral Gables, Florida 33134. A tentative settlement was reached on the second day of mediation, March 15, 2024, and the Parties executed a written term sheet memorializing the principal terms of the settlement on March 22, 2024. The Parties now desire to fully and finally resolve all claims and counterclaims in the Litigation, and all related disputes among the Parties, on the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement.

**E. Desire to Settle.** The Parties acknowledge the uncertainty, risk, and expense inherent in continued litigation and trial, and each Party has made an independent assessment of the merits and risks of its respective claims and defenses. The Parties desire to avoid the further burden and expense of trial and to resolve their disputes amicably and in full. Entry into this Agreement is not, and shall not be construed as, an admission of liability, wrongdoing, or the validity of any claim or defense by any Party. Each Party has been represented by competent legal counsel of its choosing in the negotiation and execution of this Agreement, and each Party has had a full and fair opportunity to review, analyze, and negotiate the terms set forth herein.

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual promises, covenants, releases, and agreements set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

**[ARTICLE I --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Article I shall have the meanings ascribed to them elsewhere in this Agreement.

**1.1** \"**Agreement**\" means this Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release, together with all Exhibits and Schedules attached hereto, which are incorporated herein by reference and made a part hereof.

**1.2** \"**Closing**\" means the consummation of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement on the Closing Date, including the execution and delivery of this Agreement by all Parties, the payment of the Initial Payment, and the execution and delivery of all ancillary documents required to be delivered at or prior to the Closing.

**1.3** \"**Closing Date**\" means April 22, 2024.

**1.4** \"**Collateral Properties**\" means the eight (8) unencumbered hotel properties identified in Schedule 3.1 hereto, which serve as collateral for the security interest granted to Verimark pursuant to Article III.

**1.5** \"**Complaint**\" means the ten-count Complaint filed by Verimark on March 7, 2022, in Case No. 1021-00006, in the Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida, together with all amendments thereto.

**1.6** \"**Counterclaim**\" means the \$12,000,000 counterclaim filed by Coastal Palms on April 18, 2022, in the Litigation, asserting claims for alleged brand-standard violations and over-billing.

**1.7** \"**Court**\" means the Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida.

**1.8** \"**De-Identification Deadline**\" means August 20, 2024, which is one hundred twenty (120) days from the Closing Date.

**1.9** \"**Enhanced Audit Protocol**\" means the enhanced audit and reporting requirements applicable to the Retained Properties, as set forth in Article VIII of this Agreement and as more fully described in Exhibit D attached hereto.

**1.10** \"**Event of Default**\" has the meaning set forth in Section 2.7 of this Agreement.

**1.11** \"**Existing FLAs**\" means the twenty-two (22) Franchise License Agreements between Verimark and Coastal Palms and/or its affiliates (including Gulf Breeze and Savannah Lodging), the first of which was executed on June 15, 2007, and the most recent of which was executed on September 3, 2019, governing the operation of the Properties under the Verimark Brands.

**1.12** \"**GRR**\" or \"**Gross Room Revenue**\" has the meaning ascribed to such term in Section 4.1 of each FLA, which generally includes all revenue derived from or attributable to the rental of guest rooms at the applicable Property, regardless of the method of collection, booking channel, or collecting entity.

**1.13** \"**Initial Payment**\" means the cash payment of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) payable by Coastal Palms to Verimark at Closing in accordance with Section 2.2 of this Agreement.

**1.14** \"**Ironclad**\" means Ironclad National Bank, a national banking association, which holds first-lien mortgage loans on eighteen (18) of the twenty-two (22) Properties, with an aggregate outstanding principal balance of approximately Ninety-Four Million Dollars (\$94,000,000) as of the date hereof.

**1.15** \"**Litigation**\" means the action styled *Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC, et al.*, Case No. 1021-00006, pending in the Circuit Court of the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County, Florida, including all claims, counterclaims, cross-claims, and third-party claims asserted therein.

**1.16** \"**New FLAs**\" means the new ten (10)-year Franchise License Agreements to be executed by Verimark and the applicable Coastal Palms Party for each of the Retained Properties, substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit C.

**1.17** \"**Payment Schedule**\" means the schedule of payments set forth in Article II and as more fully described in Exhibit A attached hereto.

**1.18** \"**Personal Guaranties**\" means the individual guaranty agreements to be executed by R. Brecker and Prescott, each substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit E, pursuant to which R. Brecker and Prescott jointly and severally guarantee all obligations of the Coastal Palms Parties under this Agreement.

**1.19** \"**Properties**\" means the twenty-two (22) hotel properties operated by the Coastal Palms Parties under the Existing FLAs.

**1.20** \"**Retained Properties**\" means the eight (8) Properties identified in Section 7.1 of this Agreement and in Exhibit C that will continue to be franchised under the New FLAs, consisting of four (4) properties in Naples, Florida; two (2) properties on Marco Island, Florida; and two (2) properties in Tampa, Florida.

**1.21** \"**Security Agreement**\" means the security agreement to be executed by Coastal Palms in favor of Verimark, substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit F, granting Verimark a first-priority security interest in the Collateral Properties to secure the Structured Payments and other obligations under this Agreement.

**1.22** \"**Settlement Amount**\" means the aggregate sum of Eighty-Seven Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$87,500,000), payable by the Coastal Palms Parties to Verimark in accordance with Article II of this Agreement.

**1.23** \"**Structured Payments**\" means the eight (8) semi-annual payments of Seven Million Eight Hundred Twelve Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$7,812,500) each, totaling Sixty-Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$62,500,000), payable in accordance with Section 2.3 of this Agreement, the first such payment being due on October 22, 2024, and the last such payment being due on April 22, 2028, as more fully described in the Payment Schedule attached hereto as Exhibit A.

**1.24** \"**Surrendered Properties**\" means the fourteen (14) Properties identified in Section 7.1 and Exhibit B of this Agreement that are subject to franchise surrender, de-identification, and termination of the applicable Existing FLAs.

**1.25** \"**Verimark Brands**\" means \"Verimark Suites,\" \"Verimark Select,\" and \"Verimark Grand,\" together with all associated trademarks, service marks, logos, trade dress, proprietary systems (including reservation systems, property management systems, and revenue management systems), and all other intellectual property owned, licensed, or controlled by Verimark in connection with the branding and operation of its franchised hotel properties.

**[ARTICLE II --- SETTLEMENT PAYMENT]{.underline}**

**Section 2.1 --- Total Settlement Amount.** In full and final settlement of all claims, counterclaims, causes of action, and disputes among the Parties, whether asserted or unasserted, known or unknown, arising from or relating to the Existing FLAs, the Litigation, or the subject matter thereof, the Coastal Palms Parties shall pay to Verimark a total Settlement Amount of Eighty-Seven Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$87,500,000), payable as follows:

> \(a\) The Initial Payment of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000), payable at the Closing in accordance with Section 2.2 below; and
>
> \(b\) The Structured Payments totaling Sixty-Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$62,500,000), payable in eight (8) semi-annual installments of Seven Million Eight Hundred Twelve Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$7,812,500) each, in accordance with Section 2.3 below.

The Payment Schedule setting forth the dates, amounts, and interest calculations for all payments under this Article II is attached hereto as Exhibit A and incorporated herein by reference.

**Section 2.2 --- Initial Payment.** On the Closing Date, Coastal Palms shall pay to Verimark the Initial Payment of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) by wire transfer of immediately available funds from the escrow account established at Ironclad National Bank for the purposes of this settlement to Verimark\'s designated account. Verimark shall provide Coastal Palms with complete wire-transfer instructions for the designated receiving account no later than three (3) business days prior to the Closing Date. Upon receipt of the Initial Payment, Verimark\'s counsel, Calderwood & Harkness LLP, at 110 SE 6th Street, Suite 2800, Fort Lauderdale, Florida 33301, shall promptly issue a written confirmation of receipt to counsel for the Coastal Palms Parties. The obligation to make the Initial Payment is unconditional and shall not be subject to any right of setoff, counterclaim, defense, or deduction.

**Section 2.3 --- Structured Payments.** Following the payment of the Initial Payment, Coastal Palms shall pay to Verimark the remaining Sixty-Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$62,500,000) in eight (8) equal semi-annual installments of Seven Million Eight Hundred Twelve Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$7,812,500) each, on the following schedule:

> \(a\) The first installment shall be due and payable on October 22, 2024.
>
> \(b\) The second installment shall be due and payable on April 22, 2025.
>
> \(c\) The third installment shall be due and payable on October 22, 2025.
>
> \(d\) The fourth installment shall be due and payable on April 22, 2026.
>
> \(e\) The fifth installment shall be due and payable on October 22, 2026.
>
> \(f\) The sixth installment shall be due and payable on April 22, 2027.
>
> \(g\) The seventh installment shall be due and payable on October 22, 2027.
>
> \(h\) The eighth and final installment shall be due and payable on April 22, 2028.

All Structured Payments shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated by Verimark in accordance with the wire-transfer instructions provided pursuant to Section 2.2, or to such other account as Verimark may designate in writing from time to time upon not less than ten (10) business days\' prior notice to Coastal Palms.

**Section 2.4 --- Interest on Structured Payments.** Interest shall accrue on the outstanding principal balance of the Structured Payments at a rate of six and one-half percent (6.5%) per annum, simple interest, calculated on the basis of a 365-day year and the actual number of days elapsed. Interest shall begin to accrue on the Closing Date and shall be calculated on the then-outstanding principal balance of the Structured Payments. Interest payments shall be due and payable concurrently with each semi-annual installment payment. The amount of interest due with each installment shall be calculated by multiplying the outstanding principal balance as of the first day of the applicable interest period by the annual interest rate of 6.5%, and then multiplying the result by a fraction, the numerator of which is the actual number of days elapsed during such interest period and the denominator of which is 365. A detailed schedule setting forth the estimated interest amounts due with each installment is set forth in Exhibit A.

**Section 2.5 --- Late Payments.** Any Structured Payment (including any concurrent interest payment) not received by Verimark within ten (10) business days of its scheduled due date shall bear additional default interest at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month on the overdue amount, calculated from the original due date until the date on which such overdue amount is received by Verimark in full. This default interest shall be in addition to, and not in substitution for, the interest otherwise payable under Section 2.4. If Coastal Palms fails to cure a late payment within thirty (30) days after written notice from Verimark specifying the overdue payment and the amount due, such failure shall constitute an Event of Default under Section 2.7 of this Agreement. Nothing in this Section 2.5 shall be construed to extend the due date for any Structured Payment or to waive Verimark\'s right to declare an Event of Default following the expiration of the applicable cure period.

**Section 2.6 --- Prepayment.** Coastal Palms may, at its option, prepay all or any portion of the Structured Payments at any time without premium, penalty, or additional charge of any kind. Any partial prepayment shall be applied first to any accrued and unpaid interest on the outstanding principal balance of the Structured Payments, and second to the scheduled installments in inverse order of maturity (i.e., applied first to the most distant scheduled installment, then to the next most distant, and so on), thereby reducing the total interest obligation over the remaining term. Coastal Palms shall provide Verimark with not less than five (5) business days\' prior written notice of any prepayment, specifying the amount and intended date of such prepayment. Verimark shall recalculate the interest amounts due on any remaining installments following any partial prepayment and shall provide an updated Payment Schedule to Coastal Palms within ten (10) business days of receipt of any such prepayment.

**Section 2.7 --- Events of Default and Acceleration.** An \"Event of Default\" shall be deemed to have occurred upon the happening of any of the following:

> \(a\) **Payment Default.** Failure by any Coastal Palms Party to make any payment of the Structured Payments, accrued interest, or any other monetary obligation under this Agreement within thirty (30) days of the date on which Verimark delivers written notice to Coastal Palms specifying such payment default;
>
> \(b\) **Covenant Default.** Breach by any Coastal Palms Party of any material covenant, agreement, or obligation under this Agreement (other than a payment obligation, which is governed by clause (a) above) that remains uncured for thirty (30) days after Verimark delivers written notice to Coastal Palms specifying such breach in reasonable detail;
>
> \(c\) **Bankruptcy or Insolvency.** The commencement of any voluntary or involuntary proceeding under the United States Bankruptcy Code, Title 11, United States Code, or under any state insolvency, receivership, dissolution, or similar statute, by or against any Coastal Palms Party, or the appointment of a receiver, trustee, custodian, or similar official for the business, assets, or property of any Coastal Palms Party, or the making of a general assignment for the benefit of creditors by any Coastal Palms Party;
>
> \(d\) **Breach of Representations and Warranties.** Any representation or warranty made by any Coastal Palms Party in this Agreement or in any ancillary document delivered in connection herewith that is materially inaccurate, false, or misleading as of the date on which it was made, and such inaccuracy, falsity, or misleading character is not cured within thirty (30) days after written notice from Verimark specifying the same;
>
> \(e\) **De-Identification Failure.** Failure by any Coastal Palms Party to comply with the de-identification requirements set forth in Article VII of this Agreement by the De-Identification Deadline.

Upon the occurrence of an Event of Default, Verimark may, at its sole election and upon written notice to Coastal Palms, declare the entire outstanding principal balance of the Structured Payments, together with all accrued and unpaid interest thereon and all other amounts owing under this Agreement, immediately due and payable in full, without further notice, demand, presentment, or protest, all of which are hereby waived by the Coastal Palms Parties. Acceleration of the Structured Payments pursuant to this Section 2.7 shall not constitute a waiver of, or limit, any other rights or remedies available to Verimark at law or in equity, including, without limitation, the right to enforce the Security Agreement, to seek collection under the Personal Guaranties, to pursue foreclosure on the Collateral Properties, and to seek injunctive or other equitable relief from the Court.

**Section 2.8 --- Tax Treatment.** Each Party shall be solely responsible for the payment of all federal, state, and local taxes, and for the filing of all tax returns and reports, arising from or attributable to the payments received or made by such Party under this Agreement. The Parties agree that, for federal and state income-tax purposes, the Settlement Amount shall be treated by all Parties as compensatory damages and that no portion of the Settlement Amount shall be characterized as punitive damages, penalties, or interest for tax purposes, except to the extent required by applicable law. The Coastal Palms Parties shall be solely responsible for any and all withholding obligations, including but not limited to any obligation to withhold and remit taxes on behalf of Verimark, if any such obligation exists under applicable law. No Party shall take any position on any tax return or in any proceeding before any taxing authority that is inconsistent with the treatment described in this Section 2.8, unless required to do so by a final determination (as defined in Section 1313(a) of the Internal Revenue Code) of a court of competent jurisdiction or an applicable taxing authority.

**[ARTICLE III --- SECURITY FOR STRUCTURED PAYMENTS]{.underline}**

**Section 3.1 --- Security Interest.** To secure the prompt and full payment and performance of all obligations of the Coastal Palms Parties under this Agreement, including, without limitation, the payment of all Structured Payments, accrued interest thereon, default interest, and any indemnification obligations arising under Article X, Coastal Palms hereby grants to Verimark a first-priority security interest in the eight (8) unencumbered hotel properties identified in Schedule 3.1 attached hereto (the \"Collateral Properties\"), together with all improvements, fixtures, furnishings, equipment, accounts, general intangibles, and proceeds related thereto (collectively, the \"Collateral\"). The aggregate appraised value of the Collateral Properties, as determined by independent appraisals conducted by licensed commercial real-estate appraisers within the ninety (90)-day period preceding the Closing Date, is not less than Seventy-One Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$71,200,000). The security interest granted hereunder shall be evidenced by the Security Agreement, which shall be substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit F and shall be executed and delivered concurrently with the execution of this Agreement.

**Section 3.2 --- UCC Filings.** To perfect the security interest granted under Section 3.1, Coastal Palms hereby authorizes Verimark, and Verimark\'s counsel, Calderwood & Harkness LLP, to prepare, execute, and file on behalf of Coastal Palms UCC-1 Financing Statements with the Florida Secured Transaction Registry and with any other filing office in any jurisdiction where filing may be necessary or advisable to perfect or maintain Verimark\'s security interest in the Collateral. The UCC-1 Financing Statement shall identify the following:

> **Debtor:** Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC, 9500 Gulf Shore Drive, Suite 450, Naples, Florida 34108
>
> **Secured Party:** Verimark Hospitality Group Inc., 2400 East Las Olas Boulevard, Suite 3100, Fort Lauderdale, Florida 33301

Coastal Palms shall execute and deliver all additional documents, instruments, and agreements, including without limitation continuation statements, amendments, and such other filings and recordings, as may be reasonably necessary or requested by Verimark from time to time to perfect, preserve, and maintain the first-priority status of Verimark\'s security interest in the Collateral. Coastal Palms shall bear all costs and expenses associated with such filings.

**Section 3.3 --- Personal Guaranties.** Concurrently with the execution of this Agreement, R. Brecker and Prescott shall each execute and deliver to Verimark a Personal Guaranty, substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit E, pursuant to which R. Brecker and Prescott shall jointly and severally, absolutely, unconditionally, and irrevocably guarantee the full and prompt payment and performance of all obligations of the Coastal Palms Parties under this Agreement, including, without limitation, all Structured Payments, accrued interest, default interest, indemnification obligations, and any and all other amounts that may become due and owing under this Agreement. The Personal Guaranties shall remain in full force and effect until all Structured Payments, accrued interest, and all other obligations of the Coastal Palms Parties under this Agreement have been paid or performed in full to the complete satisfaction of Verimark.

**Section 3.4 --- Relationship with Ironclad National Bank.** The Parties acknowledge and agree that Ironclad National Bank (\"Ironclad\") holds first-lien mortgage loans on eighteen (18) of the twenty-two (22) Properties, with an aggregate outstanding principal balance of approximately Ninety-Four Million Dollars (\$94,000,000) as of the date hereof. The Parties further acknowledge that the eight (8) Collateral Properties identified in Schedule 3.1, which secure Verimark\'s security interest under this Agreement, are unencumbered by any mortgage, lien, or security interest held by Ironclad. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed or interpreted so as to impair, subordinate, modify, or otherwise affect in any manner whatsoever the existing liens, security interests, or other rights of Ironclad under its mortgage-loan agreements with the Coastal Palms Parties. Coastal Palms represents and warrants that it has provided written notice to Ironclad of the existence and terms of this Agreement and the grant of the security interest to Verimark, and that Ironclad has not objected to the transactions contemplated hereby. Ironclad is an intended third-party beneficiary of this Section 3.4 and of Section 9.5 of this Agreement.

**Section 3.5 --- Release of Security Interest.** Upon the payment in full of all Structured Payments, accrued interest, default interest (if any), and all other obligations of the Coastal Palms Parties under this Agreement, Verimark shall, within thirty (30) days of such payment in full: (a) file UCC-3 Termination Statements with the Florida Secured Transaction Registry and all other applicable filing offices; and (b) execute and deliver to Coastal Palms such releases, satisfactions, and other documents and instruments as may be reasonably necessary to evidence the termination and release of Verimark\'s security interest in the Collateral. Verimark shall bear its own costs associated with the preparation and filing of such termination statements and releases.

**[ARTICLE IV --- MUTUAL RELEASE]{.underline}**
