**A.** *The Charter-Party.* On December 3, 2020, Aegean Fortuna Shipholding (as Owner) and Northwind (as Charterer) entered into a time charter-party on the New York Produce Exchange Form 2015 (NYPE 2015), as amended by Addenda Nos. 1 through 4 thereto (Charter-Party Reference No. NW-TSL-CP-2020-1203) (the \"Charter-Party\"), for the vessel M/V *Aegean Fortuna* (IMO No. 9847231), a Supramax dry bulk carrier of approximately 58,200 deadweight tonnage (\"DWT\"), flagged in the Republic of Liberia, for a charter period of thirty-six (36) months commencing on January 15, 2021 and expiring on January 14, 2024, at a daily hire rate of Fourteen Thousand Seven Hundred Fifty United States Dollars (\$14,750);
**B.** *The Litigation.* On October 2, 2023, Northwind commenced an action captioned *Northwind Maritime Corporation v. Thalassa Shipping & Logistics SA and Aegean Fortuna Shipholding Ltd.*, Index No. 655421/2023, in the Supreme Court of the State of New York, New York County, Commercial Division (the \"Action\"), asserting claims for breach of the Charter-Party arising from alleged mechanical failures of the Vessel\'s main engine, auxiliary systems, and cargo-handling equipment, as well as alleged deviations from agreed trade routes, and seeking damages in the aggregate amount of approximately Eighteen Million Three Hundred Thousand United States Dollars (\$18,300,000);
**C.** *The Answer and Counterclaim.* On November 17, 2023, the Thalassa Parties filed a Verified Answer in the Action denying liability on all counts and asserting affirmative defenses, including defenses based upon contractual limitation of liability, the Charterer\'s failure to mitigate damages, and the Charterer\'s alleged breaches of its own obligations under the Charter-Party, together with a counterclaim seeking One Million Six Hundred Twenty Thousand United States Dollars (\$1,620,000) in unpaid hire for the period October 1 through December 31, 2022 (the \"Counterclaim\");
**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements set forth herein, the payment of the Settlement Amount, and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:
**1.3** \"**Confidential Information**\" means the terms and conditions of this Agreement, the Settlement Amount, the payment schedule set forth in Section 2.1, the Escrow Agreement and the details thereof, all negotiations, draft agreements, mediation submissions, mediation statements, mediation briefs, and all other communications between and among the Parties, their counsel, and the mediator in connection with the mediation and the negotiation and execution of this Agreement.
**1.4** \"**Consent Judgment**\" means the form of consent judgment annexed hereto as **Exhibit D**, in the amount of the then-unpaid balance of the Settlement Amount, together with interest thereon at the rate of nine percent (9%) per annum (the statutory rate under New York law, as set forth in CPLR Section 5004), to be entered by the Court only upon the occurrence of a Payment Default as provided in Article 7.
**1.5** \"**Counterclaim**\" means the counterclaim filed by the Thalassa Parties on November 17, 2023 in the Action, seeking the sum of One Million Six Hundred Twenty Thousand United States Dollars (\$1,620,000) in unpaid hire for the period October 1 through December 31, 2022, together with interest, costs, and attorneys\' fees.
**1.11** \"**Final Payment Date**\" means the date on which the third and final installment of the Settlement Amount is deposited into the Escrow Account and released to Northwind in accordance with the terms of Section 2.1(c) and the Escrow Agreement.
**1.14** \"**Settlement Amount**\" means the aggregate sum of Seven Million Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand United States Dollars (\$7,850,000), payable in the installments and on the schedule set forth in Section 2.1.
**[ARTICLE 2 --- SETTLEMENT AMOUNT AND PAYMENT SCHEDULE]{.underline}**
**2.1** **Settlement Amount.** In full and final settlement of all claims and counterclaims asserted or that could have been asserted in the Action, and all other Released Claims as defined herein, the Thalassa Parties shall pay, or cause to be paid, to Northwind the aggregate Settlement Amount of Seven Million Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand United States Dollars (\$7,850,000), payable in three (3) installments as follows:
> **(a)** *First Installment.* Four Million United States Dollars (\$4,000,000), to be deposited by wire transfer of immediately available funds into the Escrow Account within thirty (30) calendar days of the Effective Date (i.e., on or before December 20, 2024).
> **(b)** *Second Installment.* Two Million United States Dollars (\$2,000,000), to be deposited by wire transfer of immediately available funds into the Escrow Account within ninety (90) calendar days of the Effective Date (i.e., on or before February 18, 2025).
> **(c)** *Third Installment.* One Million Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand United States Dollars (\$1,850,000), to be deposited by wire transfer of immediately available funds into the Escrow Account within one hundred fifty (150) calendar days of the Effective Date (i.e., on or before April 19, 2025).
The obligation to pay the Settlement Amount shall be a joint and several obligation of the Thalassa Parties.
**2.2** **Escrow Mechanism.** All installments of the Settlement Amount shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds in United States Dollars to Escrow Account No. ESC-2024-NYK-08831 at Atlantic Fiduciary Trust Company, in accordance with the wire transfer instructions set forth in the Escrow Agreement. Each installment deposited into the Escrow Account shall be released to Northwind by the Escrow Agent promptly upon receipt of joint written instructions from counsel for the Parties, being Calderwood & Harkness LLP (counsel for the Thalassa Parties) and Hargrove, Delacroix & Stern LLP (counsel for Northwind), in accordance with the terms and conditions of the Escrow Agreement. Any interest earned on funds held in the Escrow Account shall be distributed to the Party ultimately entitled to receive the underlying principal in accordance with the Escrow Agreement.
**2.3** **Funding Sources.** The source of the Settlement Amount shall be determined by the Thalassa Parties in their sole and absolute discretion. The Parties acknowledge that portions of the Settlement Amount may be funded by contributions from Thalassa\'s protection and indemnity insurer, Oceanus Mutual Protection & Indemnity Club, or from other insurance carriers maintained by the Thalassa Parties. The Parties further acknowledge and agree that any insurance-related arrangements, including the terms, timing, and conditions of insurance contributions, are solely between the Thalassa Parties and their respective insurers and do not in any way affect, diminish, or condition the Thalassa Parties\' obligations to pay the Settlement Amount to Northwind in full and on the schedule set forth herein. In no event shall any dispute between the Thalassa Parties and their insurers excuse or delay the Thalassa Parties\' payment obligations under this Agreement.
**2.4** **Taxes.** Each Party shall be solely responsible for its own tax obligations, if any, arising from the receipt or payment of the Settlement Amount, including any applicable income, withholding, value-added, or other taxes imposed by any governmental authority. No Party makes any representation or warranty to any other Party regarding the tax treatment or tax consequences of the Settlement Amount or any payment made hereunder. Each Party agrees to indemnify and hold harmless the other Parties from any tax liability, penalty, or interest arising from such Party\'s failure to comply with its own tax obligations in connection with this Agreement.
**3.1** **Release of Counterclaim.** Contemporaneously with the execution of this Agreement and as part of the consideration for the mutual release set forth in Article 4 and the payment of the Settlement Amount, the Thalassa Parties hereby irrevocably waive, release, and forever discharge all claims asserted in the Counterclaim, including, without limitation, the claim for One Million Six Hundred Twenty Thousand United States Dollars (\$1,620,000) in unpaid hire for the period October 1 through December 31, 2022, and all claims arising therefrom, related thereto, or that could have been asserted in connection therewith. The Thalassa Parties acknowledge and agree that this waiver is unconditional and is not contingent upon the receipt of any portion of the Settlement Amount.
**3.2** **No Offset.** For the avoidance of doubt, the Settlement Amount of Seven Million Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand United States Dollars (\$7,850,000) is payable by the Thalassa Parties to Northwind in full, without any offset, deduction, setoff, recoupment, or counterclaim on account of the Counterclaim or any other claim, demand, or cause of action that the Thalassa Parties may have or claim to have against Northwind, whether arising under the Charter-Party, at law, in equity, in admiralty, or otherwise. The Thalassa Parties expressly waive any right of setoff or recoupment with respect to the Settlement Amount.
**4.1** **Release by Northwind.** Effective upon the Effective Date and subject to receipt of the Settlement Amount in full in accordance with Article 2, Northwind, for itself and on behalf of its parents, subsidiaries, affiliates, predecessors, successors, assigns, officers, directors, members, managers, shareholders, employees, agents, attorneys, accountants, advisors, consultants, and representatives, and each of their respective heirs, executors, administrators, successors, and assigns (collectively, the \"Northwind Releasors\"), hereby fully, finally, and irrevocably releases, acquits, and forever discharges the Thalassa Parties and each of their respective parents, subsidiaries, affiliates (including, without limitation, Aegean Fortuna Shipholding Ltd. and any entity directly or indirectly controlling, controlled by, or under common control with Thalassa Shipping & Logistics SA), predecessors, successors, assigns, officers, directors, members, managers, shareholders, employees, agents, insurers (including, without limitation, Oceanus Mutual Protection & Indemnity Club and Fortis Marine Underwriters Ltd.), attorneys, accountants, advisors, consultants, and representatives, and each of their respective heirs, executors, administrators, successors, and assigns (collectively, the \"Thalassa Releasees\"), from any and all claims, demands, actions, causes of action, suits, debts, dues, sums of money, accounts, reckonings, bonds, bills, specialties, covenants, contracts, controversies, agreements, obligations, promises, variances, trespasses, judgments, executions, liens, liabilities, damages, losses, costs, and expenses of every kind, nature, and description whatsoever, whether known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, matured or unmatured, fixed or contingent, liquidated or unliquidated, accrued or unaccrued, in law, equity, admiralty, or otherwise, that the Northwind Releasors ever had, now have, or hereafter may have against the Thalassa Releasees, or any of them, arising out of, relating to, or in connection with the Charter-Party, the Vessel, the Action, or any of the acts, omissions, events, facts, circumstances, or transactions alleged or that could have been alleged in the Action (collectively, the \"Released Claims\").
> **(e)** all claims for unpaid hire, including the claims for \$1,620,000 in unpaid hire asserted in the Counterclaim;
**5.1** **Confidentiality Obligation.** The Parties agree that the terms and conditions of this Agreement, the Settlement Amount, the payment schedule, the mediation proceedings and submissions, and all negotiations, communications, and discussions leading to this Agreement (collectively, \"Confidential Information\") shall be kept strictly confidential and shall not be disclosed to any third party, except as expressly provided in Section 5.2 below. Each Party shall take reasonable steps to ensure that its officers, directors, employees, agents, and representatives who receive Confidential Information maintain the confidentiality thereof in accordance with this Article 5.
**5.4** **Public Statements.** Neither any Party nor its counsel shall issue any press release, public statement, public filing, or social media posting regarding this Agreement, the Settlement Amount, or the settlement of the Action without the prior written consent of the other Parties, which consent may be withheld in such Party\'s sole and absolute discretion. If any public statement is required by applicable law, regulation, or stock exchange rule, the Parties shall consult with each other and agree upon the content and timing of such statement prior to its issuance. Nothing in this Section 5.4 shall prevent any Party from stating, in response to any inquiry, that the Action has been resolved to the mutual satisfaction of the Parties.
**6.3** **Stipulation of discontinuance.** Within ten (10) business days of the Final Payment Date (i.e., the date of receipt and release of the third and final installment of the Settlement Amount in accordance with Section 2.1(c) and the Escrow Agreement), the Parties shall execute and cause to be filed with the Court the Stipulation of discontinuance With Prejudice in the form annexed hereto as **Exhibit C**, discontinuing the Action with prejudice, including all claims, counterclaims, cross-claims, and affirmative defenses, without costs to any Party except as otherwise expressly provided in this Agreement. Each Party shall bear its own costs, attorneys\' fees, and expenses in connection with the Action, except as otherwise provided herein.
**7.1** **Timely Payment Required.** The Parties expressly acknowledge and agree that time is of the essence with respect to each installment of the Settlement Amount due under Section 2.1. The failure to make any installment payment on or before its due date shall constitute a material breach of this Agreement, subject to the Cure Period set forth in Section 7.2.
**7.2** **Payment Default.** A \"Payment Default\" shall occur if any installment of the Settlement Amount is not deposited into the Escrow Account in the full amount required on or before the applicable due date set forth in Section 2.1, and such failure is not cured within ten (10) business days after such due date (each such ten (10) business day period, a \"Cure Period\"). A Payment Default shall be deemed to have occurred automatically upon the expiration of the applicable Cure Period without the need for any demand, notice of default, or other communication from Northwind to the Thalassa Parties. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the Thalassa Parties demonstrate that the failure to make timely payment was caused solely by an error in wire transfer processing by the transmitting or receiving bank, and the Thalassa Parties initiated the wire transfer on or before the applicable due date, such failure shall not constitute a Payment Default, provided that the full installment amount is deposited into the Escrow Account within the Cure Period.
**7.3** **Consent Judgment.** Upon the occurrence of a Payment Default, Northwind shall be entitled, without further notice to or demand upon the Thalassa Parties and without the necessity of any further proceeding, to present the Consent Judgment annexed hereto as **Exhibit D** to the Court for entry against the Thalassa Parties, jointly and severally, in the amount of the then-unpaid balance of the Settlement Amount, together with interest thereon at the rate of nine percent (9%) per annum (the statutory rate under New York law, as provided in CPLR Section 5004), calculated from the date of the Payment Default through the date of payment. The Thalassa Parties hereby irrevocably consent to the entry of the Consent Judgment in such amount and waive any and all defenses, objections, or challenges to the entry thereof, including any defense based on personal jurisdiction, improper venue, insufficiency of process, or insufficiency of service of process. The Thalassa Parties further acknowledge and agree that the Consent Judgment, once entered, shall be a final judgment enforceable in any court of competent jurisdiction.
**7.4** **Acceleration.** Upon the occurrence of a Payment Default with respect to any installment, all remaining unpaid installments of the Settlement Amount shall become immediately due and payable in full, without further notice or demand, and shall bear interest at the rate specified in Section 7.3 from the date of the Payment Default.
**7.5** **Costs of Enforcement.** In the event of a Payment Default, the Thalassa Parties shall be responsible for and shall promptly reimburse Northwind for all reasonable and documented costs and expenses, including reasonable attorneys\' fees and disbursements, expert fees, court costs, and other expenses, incurred by Northwind in connection with the enforcement of this Agreement, the collection of the unpaid Settlement Amount, and the entry, domestication, and enforcement of the Consent Judgment in any jurisdiction.
**9.1** **Lender Notification.** Within five (5) business days of the Effective Date, Thalassa shall notify Meridian Capital Bank AG, in writing, of the execution of this Agreement and the settlement of the Action in the aggregate amount of Seven Million Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand United States Dollars (\$7,850,000), as required pursuant to Section 8.14 of the Credit Agreement dated April 1, 2019 between Thalassa and Meridian Capital Bank AG (as amended, the \"Credit Agreement\"), which requires notification to the lender of material litigation settlements exceeding Five Million United States Dollars (\$5,000,000). Such notice shall be delivered in accordance with the notice provisions of the Credit Agreement. Thalassa shall provide Northwind with written confirmation that such notification has been timely delivered, including a copy of the notice as sent (redacted to remove commercially sensitive financial information unrelated to the settlement), within three (3) business days following delivery of such notice.
**10.1** This Agreement is entered into solely for the purpose of compromising and settling disputed claims and counterclaims between the Parties, and to avoid the expense, burden, inconvenience, and uncertainty of further litigation. Nothing contained in this Agreement, the negotiation of this Agreement, the payment of the Settlement Amount, the waiver of the Counterclaim, or the execution of this Agreement shall constitute, be construed as, or be admissible as evidence of, an admission of liability, fault, wrongdoing, or the validity or invalidity of any claim, counterclaim, defense, or position by any Party with respect to any matter whatsoever. Each Party expressly denies any liability, fault, or wrongdoing with respect to the claims and counterclaims asserted in the Action.
**Exhibit D:** Form of Consent Judgment, in the amount of the unpaid balance of the Settlement Amount plus interest at nine percent (9%) per annum, to be entered by the Court upon a Payment Default in accordance with Section 7.3.

**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP**

**Attorneys at Law**

1735 Market Street, Suite 3100 Philadelphia, PA 19103

Telephone: (215) 884-7200 Facsimile: (215) 884-7201

600 Lexington Avenue New York, NY 10022

www.calderwoodharkness.com

March 22, 2024

**VIA HAND DELIVERY AND FIRST-CLASS U.S. MAIL** **Copy via Certified Mail, Return Receipt Requested (No. 7020 1810 0003 4472 6891)**

Appeals Officer Noreen Castañeda Internal Revenue Service IRS Appeals Office 290 Broadway, 30th Floor Manhattan, New York 10007

> **Re:** Penterra Pharmaceuticals Corp. **EIN:** 22-3741856 **Tax Years:** 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020 **IRS Exam Team ID:** LB&I-NE-TP-2022-00641 **C&H Matter Number:** 1018-00009
>
> **Re:** Acceptance of Settlement Offer --- Penterra Pharmaceuticals Corp.; EIN 22-3741856; Tax Years 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020; Proposed IRC § 482 Transfer Pricing Adjustments

Dear Appeals Officer Castañeda:

**[I. Introduction and Authorization]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"C&H\" or the \"Firm\") represents Penterra Pharmaceuticals Corp. (\"PPC\" or the \"Company\"), a Delaware corporation headquartered at 2200 Independence Boulevard, Princeton Junction, New Jersey 08550. PPC is a publicly traded corporation listed on the Nasdaq Stock Market under ticker symbol PPCA. The Company is a multinational pharmaceutical enterprise engaged in the research, development, manufacture, and commercialization of proprietary therapeutic products across multiple therapeutic areas.

Our representation of PPC has been duly authorized pursuant to IRS Form 2848 (Power of Attorney and Declaration of Representative), which was filed with the Internal Revenue Service on June 8, 2022. The Form 2848 authorizes the following attorneys and practitioners at Calderwood & Harkness LLP to represent PPC in connection with the above-referenced examination and all related proceedings: Leonard Cross (Partner), Sylvia Hartwell (Partner), Garrett Simmons (Associate), and Leila Nazari (Associate). Calderwood & Harkness was retained as outside tax counsel to PPC effective June 2, 2022, shortly after the IRS opened its examination of the Company\'s federal income tax returns for the tax years at issue.

The purpose of this letter is to formally communicate PPC\'s acceptance, in its entirety, of the settlement offer extended by you on March 15, 2024, resolving all transfer pricing adjustments proposed by the Internal Revenue Service under Section 482 of the Internal Revenue Code (\"IRC\") for tax years 2017, 2018, 2019, and 2020. This letter sets forth the terms of the settlement as understood by PPC, identifies the agreed-upon adjustments for each tax year, addresses the treatment of penalties and interest, and requests that the settlement be memorialized through a Closing Agreement on IRS Form 906. We have enclosed a draft of the proposed Closing Agreement for your review and comment.

**[II. Background and Procedural History]{.underline}**

We believe it is useful, for the sake of a complete record, to briefly summarize the procedural history of this matter from the inception of the examination through the present.

On May 16, 2022, the IRS Large Business & International Division (\"LB&I\") initiated an examination of PPC\'s federal income tax returns (Forms 1120) for tax years 2017, 2018, 2019, and 2020, as communicated to PPC by means of Letter 2205-A. The examination was assigned Exam Team identification number LB&I-NE-TP-2022-00641 and was conducted under the supervision of Supervisory Revenue Agent Gerald Meskill and Lead Revenue Agent Patricia Dunleavy.

During the course of the examination, the IRS issued a total of forty-seven (47) Information Document Requests (\"IDRs\") between June 2022 and September 2023. PPC, through undersigned counsel and in coordination with PPC\'s in-house tax department under the direction of Marcus Whitfield, Vice President of Global Tax, responded to each IDR in a timely and comprehensive manner. At no point during the examination did the IRS assert that PPC failed to cooperate or provide requested information. PPC produced, among other materials, voluminous financial data, intercompany agreements, board minutes, economic analyses, and contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation for each of the tax years under examination.

The examination focused principally on PPC\'s transfer pricing methodology governing intercompany transactions between PPC and its wholly owned Irish subsidiary, Penterra Biopharma International DAC (\"PBI\"), a designated activity company organized under the laws of Ireland. Two primary categories of intercompany transactions were at issue: (i) the qualified cost-sharing arrangement (\"CSA\") entered into between PPC and PBI, effective July 1, 2012, pursuant to which PBI shares in the costs and risks of intangible development activities in exchange for the right to exploit resulting intangible property outside the Americas region; and (ii) the legacy intellectual property royalty arrangement under which PBI pays a running royalty to PPC for the continued use of pre-CSA intangible property in non-Americas markets.

On October 12, 2023, the IRS examination team issued a Notice of Proposed Adjustment (\"NOPA\") proposing net adjustments totaling \$380,400,000 across all four tax years. PPC received the corresponding 30-Day Letter on November 8, 2023. Pursuant to a written extension of time granted by the examination team, PPC timely filed its formal Protest on December 22, 2023. The Protest set forth PPC\'s detailed factual, legal, and economic objections to each of the proposed adjustments and requested a conference with the IRS Independent Office of Appeals.

The case was assigned to you, Appeals Officer Castañeda, in January 2024. An Appeals conference was held on February 28, 2024, at the IRS Appeals Office in Manhattan, New York. Calderwood & Harkness was represented at the conference by Leonard Cross, Sylvia Hartwell, and Garrett Simmons. PPC was represented by Marcus Whitfield (Vice President, Global Tax) and Deborah Staines (General Counsel). Dr. Helena Vasquez, Managing Director of Whitmore Valuation Group LLC, participated as PPC\'s independent economic expert and presented testimony regarding the arm\'s-length character of PPC\'s transfer pricing methodology.

Following the Appeals conference, and at your request, PPC submitted a supplemental written submission on March 8, 2024, which included additional comparable uncontrolled license agreement data and an updated benchmarking analysis prepared by Dr. Vasquez and her team at Whitmore Valuation Group LLC. This supplemental data further supported PPC\'s position that its transfer pricing methodology, including the CSA cost-sharing ratios and the legacy royalty rate, fell within the arm\'s-length range.

On March 15, 2024, you communicated a settlement offer to undersigned counsel proposing a resolution of all disputed transfer pricing adjustments for tax years 2017 through 2020. PPC has carefully reviewed the terms of that offer, and, as set forth in this letter, hereby accepts the settlement in its entirety.

**[III. Summary of Original Proposed Adjustments]{.underline}**

For completeness and to provide context for the agreed-upon settlement, we briefly recite the IRS\'s proposed adjustments as set forth in the NOPA dated October 12, 2023.

**A. CSA Cost-Sharing Ratio Adjustments**

The IRS proposed increasing PBI\'s cost-sharing percentages under the CSA by approximately eight (8) to twelve (12) percentage points across each tax year. The IRS contended that the cost-sharing ratios, as applied by PPC and PBI, underallocated development costs to PBI relative to PBI\'s anticipated share of the reasonably anticipated benefits from the intangible development activities. The IRS\'s proposed adjustments would have resulted in additional cost-sharing payments from PBI to PPC, as follows:

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Tax Year**      **PPC\'s Applied CSA %**   **IRS Proposed CSA %**   **Proposed Additional Cost-Sharing Payment**
  ----------------- -------------------------- ------------------------ ----------------------------------------------
  2017              38.2%                      48.2%                    \$48,730,000

  2018              39.6%                      50.6%                    \$57,610,000

  2019              41.1%                      52.3%                    \$62,850,000

  2020              42.7%                      53.7%                    \$65,820,000

  **Total**                                                             **\$235,010,000**
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**B. Legacy IP Royalty Rate Adjustments**

The IRS further proposed increasing the royalty rate applicable to PBI\'s license of pre-CSA legacy intangible property from 4.5% to 11.0% of non-Americas net sales. The IRS contended that the 4.5% royalty rate applied by PPC and PBI did not reflect the arm\'s-length compensation for the valuable pharmaceutical intellectual property licensed to PBI, and that an appropriate royalty rate---based on the IRS\'s own comparable uncontrolled transaction analysis---would be 11.0% of relevant net sales. The proposed royalty rate adjustments were as follows:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Tax Year**                        **Proposed Additional Royalty Payment**
  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------------
  2017                                \$52,949,000

  2018                                \$49,549,500

  2019                                \$44,967,000

  2020                                \$40,566,500

  **Total**                           **\$188,040,000**
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

**C. Correlative Offset**

The examination team allowed a correlative offset of (\$42,650,000) to avoid double-counting of income that would otherwise be attributed to PPC under both the CSA cost-sharing ratio adjustment and the legacy IP royalty rate adjustment.

**D. Net Proposed Adjustment and Penalty**

The net proposed adjustment across all four tax years, after application of the correlative offset, was \$380,400,000. In addition, the IRS proposed the imposition of a twenty percent (20%) substantial valuation misstatement penalty under IRC § 6662(e) on the underpayment of tax attributable to the proposed transfer pricing adjustments. The estimated penalty amount was approximately \$15,977,000.

PPC contested all of the proposed adjustments, including both the CSA cost-sharing ratio adjustments and the legacy IP royalty rate adjustments, in their entirety, in its Protest filed December 22, 2023, and through the presentations made at the Appeals conference on February 28, 2024.

**[IV. Acceptance of Settlement Offer]{.underline}**

PPC hereby formally and unconditionally accepts the settlement offer communicated by Appeals Officer Castañeda on March 15, 2024, in its entirety and without modification. PPC\'s acceptance of the settlement has been duly authorized by the Company\'s senior management, including Rajesh Iyer, Chief Financial Officer, and Catherine Falk, Chief Executive Officer.

**A. Total Settlement Adjustment Amount**

The total agreed-upon adjustment under the settlement is **\$47,600,000** across all four tax years under examination (2017, 2018, 2019, and 2020). This settlement amount represents approximately 12.51% of the \$380,400,000 net proposed adjustment originally set forth in the NOPA. PPC and the IRS have agreed that this amount represents a fair and reasonable resolution of the disputed transfer pricing issues, taking into account the respective litigation hazards faced by both parties.

**B. Allocation of Settlement Adjustment by Tax Year**

The parties have agreed to allocate the total settlement adjustment among the four tax years as follows:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Tax Year**                        **Agreed-Upon Adjustment**
  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------
  2017                                \$11,200,000

  2018                                \$12,400,000

  2019                                \$12,800,000

**[SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND MUTUAL RELEASE]{.underline}**

Effective Date: July 14, 2023

This **SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND MUTUAL RELEASE** (this \"Agreement\") is entered into as of July 14, 2023 (the \"Effective Date\"), by and among the following parties:

**(1) MARGUERITE D. FONSECA**, an individual residing at 2817 Cheremoya Avenue, Los Angeles, California 90068 (\"Fonseca\");

**(2) DESMOND R. RENNICK**, an individual residing at 438 Georgina Avenue, Santa Monica, California 90402 (\"Rennick\"); and

**(3) RENNICK SLATE VENTURES LLC**, a California limited liability company with its principal office at 1925 Ocean Park Boulevard, Suite 200, Santa Monica, California 90405, Employer Identification Number 84-3056178 (\"RSV\" and, together with Rennick, the \"Rennick Parties\").

Each of Fonseca, Rennick, and RSV is sometimes referred to herein individually as a \"Party\" and collectively as the \"Parties.\"

**[RECITALS]{.underline}**

**A.** Fonseca and Rennick are the partners of Coastal Meridian Productions LLP, a California limited liability partnership (\"CMP\"), Employer Identification Number 83-2197644, formed pursuant to that certain Partnership Agreement dated March 8, 2017, as amended by that certain First Amendment to Partnership Agreement dated January 15, 2019 (as so amended, the \"Partnership Agreement\"). CMP maintains its principal office at 1140 North La Brea Avenue, Suite 300, Los Angeles, California 90038, and its registered agent for service of process is Pacific Coast Registered Agents, Inc., 4200 Wilshire Boulevard, Suite 610, Los Angeles, California 90010.

**B.** Under the Partnership Agreement, Fonseca holds a fifty-five percent (55%) partnership interest in CMP and Rennick holds a forty-five percent (45%) partnership interest in CMP. Fonseca contributed Two Million Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$2,850,000) in initial capital, and Rennick contributed Two Million Three Hundred Thirty-One Thousand Eight Hundred Eighteen Dollars (\$2,331,818) in initial capital, for a total initial capitalization of Five Million One Hundred Eighty-One Thousand Eight Hundred Eighteen Dollars (\$5,181,818).

**C.** Since its formation, CMP has produced and commercially exploited four feature-film properties: *Iron Lullaby* (2018), *The Perdition Room* (2019), *Salt Wind* (2020), and *Nightjars* (2021). Through the second quarter of calendar year 2022, these four properties generated aggregate gross receipts of approximately Twenty-Three Million Two Hundred Twenty Thousand Dollars (\$23,220,000).

**D.** A dispute arose between the Parties (the \"Dispute\") regarding, among other things: (i) management fees paid by CMP to RSV during the period from 2018 through mid-2022, totaling Two Million Six Hundred Ninety-Four Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$2,694,500), which Fonseca contends exceeded the five percent (5%) management-fee cap set forth in Section 6.2 of the Partnership Agreement --- the permissible aggregate amount under the cap being One Million One Hundred Sixty-One Thousand Dollars (\$1,161,000), resulting in alleged excess fees of One Million Five Hundred Thirty-Three Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$1,533,500); and (ii) the reclassification of Eight Hundred Forty-Seven Thousand Two Hundred Dollars (\$847,200) in domestic distribution revenues as recoupable advance repayments, which Fonseca contends was not authorized under the Partnership Agreement and improperly diverted funds from the distributable profit pool.

**E.** On January 24, 2023, Fonseca commenced a civil action styled *Fonseca v. Rennick et al.*, filed in the Superior Court of the State of California, County of Los Angeles, bearing Case Number 23STCV01897 (the \"Action\"). Rennick filed an answer and counterclaim in the Action on March 6, 2023. The counterclaim asserted, among other things, claims for breach of fiduciary duty and tortious interference with prospective economic advantage.

**F.** The Parties participated in a full-day mediation session on May 19, 2023, before the Honorable Patricia Villareal (Ret.), conducted under the auspices of Apex Mediation Services, located at 633 West 5th Street, Suite 2600, Los Angeles, California 90071. Following the mediation, the Parties continued arms-length negotiations and ultimately agreed upon the material terms of a resolution, which were memorialized in a Settlement Term Sheet dated June 8, 2023 (the \"Settlement Term Sheet\"), executed by all Parties and their respective counsel.

**G.** The Parties now wish to fully and finally resolve the Dispute, including all claims and counterclaims asserted in the Action, and all other claims, known or unknown, relating to CMP\'s financial affairs from inception through December 31, 2022, on the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement.

**H.** Fonseca is represented in this matter by Calderwood & Harkness LLP, 725 South Flower Street, Suite 4200, Los Angeles, California 90017. The Rennick Parties are represented in this matter by Hargrove, Pettit & Sun LLP, 800 South Figueroa Street, Suite 3100, Los Angeles, California 90017. Each Party acknowledges having had the opportunity to review this Agreement with their respective counsel and having received legal advice regarding the terms, conditions, and consequences of executing this Agreement.

**[AGREEMENT]{.underline}**

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants, promises, and agreements set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged by each Party, the Parties agree as follows:

**[Section 1: SETTLEMENT PAYMENT]{.underline}**

**1.1 Payment Amount and Schedule.** As settlement consideration for the claims asserted by Fonseca against the Rennick Parties, Rennick shall pay, or cause to be paid, to Fonseca the aggregate sum of Nine Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars (\$975,000) (the \"Settlement Amount\"), payable in two installments as follows:

> **(a) First Installment.** Six Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$600,000), payable by wire transfer of immediately available funds to a bank account designated by Fonseca in writing to Rennick or his counsel no later than five (5) business days after the Effective Date. The First Installment shall be due and payable within fifteen (15) business days of the Effective Date (the \"First Installment Due Date\"). The Parties acknowledge that, based on the Effective Date of July 14, 2023, and excluding weekends and federal bank holidays, the First Installment Due Date falls on August 4, 2023.
>
> **(b) Second Installment.** Three Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars (\$375,000), payable by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the same bank account designated by Fonseca pursuant to Section 1.1(a) above, on or before October 15, 2023 (the \"Second Installment Due Date\").

For purposes of this Agreement, each of the First Installment Due Date and the Second Installment Due Date may be referred to individually as an \"Installment Due Date\" and collectively as the \"Installment Due Dates.\" Payment shall be deemed received on the date the wire transfer is credited to Fonseca\'s designated account.

**1.2 Late Payment.** In the event that any installment of the Settlement Amount is not received by Fonseca on or before its applicable Installment Due Date, the unpaid amount shall bear interest at the rate of ten percent (10%) per annum, calculated on a simple interest basis from the applicable Installment Due Date through and including the date of actual receipt of such payment by Fonseca. The accrual of interest under this Section 1.2 shall not limit or waive any other rights or remedies available to Fonseca under this Agreement, at law, or in equity, including the right to seek enforcement of this Agreement pursuant to California Code of Civil Procedure Section 664.6 as contemplated by Section 7.1 hereof.

**1.3 Source of Funds.** The Settlement Amount shall be the personal obligation of Rennick individually and shall not be paid, directly or indirectly, from the funds, accounts, assets, or revenues of CMP. Rennick represents and warrants that he has sufficient personal financial resources and liquidity to satisfy the Settlement Amount in accordance with the payment schedule set forth in Section 1.1 above. Nothing in this Section 1.3 shall prohibit Rennick from using funds distributed to him by CMP in the ordinary course of business in accordance with the Partnership Agreement and the Restated Waterfall (as defined below), provided that no CMP distribution shall be accelerated, preferentially directed, or otherwise manipulated for the purpose of funding the Settlement Amount.

**[Section 2: RESTATED DISTRIBUTION WATERFALL]{.underline}**

Simultaneously with the execution of this Agreement, the Parties shall execute the Restated Distribution Waterfall for Coastal Meridian Productions LLP in the form attached hereto as **Exhibit A** (the \"Restated Waterfall\"). The Restated Waterfall has been negotiated in good faith by the Parties and their respective counsel and accountants. Effective as of January 1, 2023, the Restated Waterfall shall supersede and replace, in their entirety, all prior waterfall schedules, distribution provisions, and allocation methodologies set forth in the Partnership Agreement or adopted by the partners of CMP, including without limitation Schedule B to the Partnership Agreement and any informal or written amendments or modifications thereto. In the event of any conflict or inconsistency between the terms of the Restated Waterfall and the terms of the Partnership Agreement (as amended by the Second Amendment set forth in Section 5 hereof), the Restated Waterfall shall control with respect to all matters relating to the allocation, distribution, and priority of CMP revenues and proceeds.

**[Section 3: EXCESS MANAGEMENT FEES --- SATISFACTION]{.underline}**

The Parties acknowledge and agree to the following facts and resolutions with respect to the management fees paid by CMP to RSV during the period from 2018 through mid-2022:

> **(a)** During such period, CMP paid to RSV management fees in the aggregate amount of Two Million Six Hundred Ninety-Four Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$2,694,500) for management, administrative, and overhead services rendered by RSV to CMP in connection with the production, marketing, and distribution of CMP\'s feature-film properties.
>
> **(b)** Under Section 6.2 of the Partnership Agreement, management fees payable by CMP to any entity owned or controlled by a partner were subject to a cap of five percent (5%) of CMP\'s aggregate gross receipts. Based on aggregate gross receipts of Twenty-Three Million Two Hundred Twenty Thousand Dollars (\$23,220,000) through the second quarter of 2022, the permissible aggregate amount of such management fees was One Million One Hundred Sixty-One Thousand Dollars (\$1,161,000). The management fees actually paid to RSV therefore exceeded the permissible amount by One Million Five Hundred Thirty-Three Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$1,533,500) (the \"Excess Fees\").
>
> **(c)** The payment by Rennick of the Settlement Amount in accordance with Section 1 of this Agreement shall constitute full and complete satisfaction, settlement, and resolution of any and all claims, demands, causes of action, and liabilities that Fonseca or CMP may have against Rennick, RSV, or any of their respective affiliates, arising from, relating to, or in connection with the Excess Fees, including without limitation claims for breach of the Partnership Agreement, breach of fiduciary duty, unjust enrichment, conversion, accounting, constructive trust, disgorgement, or any other legal or equitable theory.
>
> **(d)** Upon Fonseca\'s receipt of the Settlement Amount in full, no further clawback, restitution, repayment, refund, offset, credit, or other remedy of any kind shall be required of or available against Rennick, RSV, or any of their respective affiliates with respect to the Excess Fees. For the avoidance of doubt, this Section 3 does not release or waive any rights of Fonseca with respect to management fees paid or payable by CMP on or after January 1, 2023, which shall be governed exclusively by the Restated Waterfall and Section 10 of this Agreement.

**[Section 4: RECLASSIFIED REVENUES --- RESTORATION]{.underline}**

**4.1 Restoration to Distributable Profit Pool.** The Parties acknowledge that the aggregate sum of Eight Hundred Forty-Seven Thousand Two Hundred Dollars (\$847,200) in domestic distribution revenues received by CMP was reclassified on CMP\'s books and records as recoupable advance repayments. The Parties agree that such reclassification was not authorized under the Partnership Agreement and that the reclassified amounts shall be restored to CMP\'s distributable profit pool, with such restoration treated as retroactive to the fiscal quarters in which the revenues were originally received by CMP, as follows:

> **(a)** Five Hundred Thirty-Eight Thousand Two Hundred Dollars (\$538,200) attributable to domestic distribution revenues received in connection with *Salt Wind*, to be restored to the distributable profit pool for the third quarter of calendar year 2020 (Q3 2020); and
>
> **(b)** Three Hundred Nine Thousand Dollars (\$309,000) attributable to domestic distribution revenues received in connection with *Iron Lullaby*, to be restored to the distributable profit pool for the first quarter of calendar year 2021 (Q1 2021).

**4.2 Accountant Restatement.** Within thirty (30) days following the Effective Date, CMP\'s independent accountant, Clearfield & Moss CPAs, shall restate the applicable waterfall schedules and distribution records for Q3 2020 and Q1 2021 to reflect the restoration of revenues set forth in Section 4.1 above. The restated schedules shall recalculate each partner\'s distributable share for the affected quarters in accordance with the Partnership Agreement as in effect during those periods. To the extent that the restatement results in an adjustment to distributions owed by one Party to the other for the affected periods, any net amount owed to Fonseca shall be credited against the Settlement Amount, and any net amount owed to Rennick shall be offset against his obligation to pay the Settlement Amount. The Parties and their respective counsel shall cooperate in good faith with Clearfield & Moss CPAs to facilitate the timely completion of the restatement contemplated by this Section 4.2.

**[Section 5: PARTNERSHIP GOVERNANCE REFORMS (SECOND AMENDMENT)]{.underline}**

The Partnership Agreement is hereby further amended as set forth in this Section 5 (the \"Second Amendment\"). The Second Amendment shall be effective as of the Effective Date and shall be binding upon the Parties and upon CMP. Except as expressly modified by this Section 5, the Partnership Agreement (as previously amended) shall remain in full force and effect. In the event of any conflict between the provisions of this Section 5 and the provisions of the Partnership Agreement, the provisions of this Section 5 shall control.

**5.1 Dual-Signature Requirement.** Section 4.3 of the Partnership Agreement is hereby amended to add the following provision: Any single expenditure, commitment, or disbursement by or on behalf of CMP in an amount exceeding Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$25,000.00) shall require the prior written approval of both Fonseca and Rennick. For purposes of this Section 5.1, a \"single expenditure\" shall include any individual payment, invoice, purchase order, contract commitment, or series of related transactions that, in the aggregate, exceed the foregoing threshold. Written approval may be given by email from the approving partner\'s email address of record with CMP, provided that the email expressly references the specific expenditure and the amount thereof. Neither partner shall unreasonably withhold, condition, or delay approval of any expenditure that is consistent with CMP\'s approved annual operating budget and the ordinary course of CMP\'s business.

**5.2 Quarterly Financial Reporting.** Section 7.1 of the Partnership Agreement is hereby amended to require that CMP\'s independent accountant shall prepare and distribute to both Fonseca and Rennick a quarterly financial-reporting package within forty-five (45) days following the end of each calendar quarter. Each quarterly financial-reporting package shall include, at a minimum: (a) an unaudited balance sheet as of the quarter-end date; (b) an unaudited income statement for the quarter then ended and for the year-to-date period; (c) a statement of cash flows for the quarter then ended; (d) a detailed waterfall schedule showing the calculation and allocation of distributable profits for the quarter; (e) an accounts receivable aging report; and (f) a schedule of all management fees, related-party transactions, and overhead allocations for the quarter. The quarterly financial-reporting packages shall be delivered to each partner at the address set forth in the preamble to this Agreement, or to such other address as a partner may designate in writing, and simultaneously by electronic mail to email addresses designated by each partner.

**5.3 Annual Audit.** Section 7.2 of the Partnership Agreement is hereby amended to require that the books and records of CMP shall be subject to an annual audit conducted in accordance with generally accepted auditing standards as promulgated by the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants. The audit report, including the auditor\'s opinion, audited financial statements, and any management letter, shall be issued and distributed to both partners within ninety (90) days following the end of each fiscal year of CMP. The cost of each annual audit shall be a CMP partnership expense.

**5.4 Independent Accountant.** Clearfield & Moss CPAs (Howard Moss, CPA, Partner-in-Charge; 9100 Sunset Boulevard, Suite 220, West Hollywood, California 90069) shall continue to serve as CMP\'s independent accountant for purposes of the quarterly financial reporting required by Section 5.2 and the annual audit required by Section 5.3. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the annual audits for calendar years 2023 and 2024 shall be subject to the oversight and review of Tillerman Forensic Advisory LLC (Greta Sørensen, CPA, CFF, Principal; 350 South Grand Avenue, Suite 1480, Los Angeles, California 90071). Tillerman\'s oversight role shall include, without limitation, the right to: (a) review Clearfield & Moss\'s audit workpapers, methodologies, and conclusions; (b) conduct independent testing of selected account balances and transactions; (c) communicate directly with Clearfield & Moss regarding audit findings; and (d) issue a supplemental report to both partners summarizing its oversight activities and any concerns identified. Tillerman\'s fees and expenses for the oversight engagement shall be a CMP partnership expense, provided that such fees and expenses shall not exceed Forty Thousand Dollars (\$40,000) per audit cycle without the prior written consent of both partners. Following the completion of the calendar year 2024 audit oversight engagement, Tillerman\'s oversight role shall terminate unless both partners agree in writing to extend it.

**[Section 6: MUTUAL RELEASE]{.underline}**

**6.1 Fonseca Release.** Effective upon Fonseca\'s receipt of the First Installment, Fonseca, for herself and on behalf of her heirs, executors, administrators, personal representatives, successors, and assigns, hereby irrevocably and unconditionally releases, acquits, and forever discharges each of the Rennick Parties and their respective agents, employees, officers, managers, members, representatives, attorneys, accountants, insurers, heirs, executors, administrators, personal representatives, successors, and assigns (collectively, the \"Rennick Released Parties\") from any and all claims, counterclaims, cross-claims, demands, actions, causes of action, suits, debts, dues, sums of money, accounts, reckonings, bonds, bills, specialties, covenants, contracts, controversies, agreements, promises, variances, trespasses, damages, judgments, executions, liabilities, obligations, costs, expenses, and attorney\'s fees of every kind and nature whatsoever, whether at law or in equity, whether based on contract, tort, statute, or any other theory of recovery, whether known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, matured or unmatured, liquidated or unliquidated, fixed or contingent, which Fonseca now has, has ever had, or may hereafter have against any of the Rennick Released Parties, arising from, relating to, or in connection with the Dispute, the Action, the Excess Fees, the reclassified revenues described in Section 4, or CMP\'s financial affairs generally for the period from CMP\'s inception through and including December 31, 2022 (collectively, the \"Fonseca Released Claims\"). The Fonseca Released Claims do not include claims arising from a breach of this Agreement.

**6.2 Rennick Release.** Effective upon execution of this Agreement, each of the Rennick Parties, for themselves and on behalf of their respective heirs, executors, administrators, personal representatives, members, managers, successors, and assigns, hereby irrevocably and unconditionally releases, acquits, and forever discharges Fonseca and her agents, employees, representatives, attorneys, accountants, insurers, heirs, executors, administrators, personal representatives, successors, and assigns (collectively, the \"Fonseca Released Parties\") from any and all claims, counterclaims, cross-claims, demands, actions, causes of action, suits, debts, dues, sums of money, accounts, reckonings, bonds, bills, specialties, covenants, contracts, controversies, agreements, promises, variances, trespasses, damages, judgments, executions, liabilities, obligations, costs, expenses, and attorney\'s fees of every kind and nature whatsoever, whether at law or in equity, whether based on contract, tort, statute, or any other theory of recovery, whether known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, matured or unmatured, liquidated or unliquidated, fixed or contingent, which the Rennick Parties now have, have ever had, or may hereafter have against any of the Fonseca Released Parties, arising from, relating to, or in connection with the Dispute, the Action, the counterclaim filed in the Action, the Excess Fees, the reclassified revenues described in Section 4, or CMP\'s financial affairs generally for the period from CMP\'s inception through and including December 31, 2022 (collectively, the \"Rennick Released Claims\"). The Rennick Released Claims do not include claims arising from a breach of this Agreement.

**6.3 California Civil Code Section 1542 Waiver.** Each Party acknowledges that he or she has been advised by his or her respective legal counsel regarding, and is familiar with, the provisions of California Civil Code Section 1542, which provides as follows:

> **\"A GENERAL RELEASE DOES NOT EXTEND TO CLAIMS THAT THE CREDITOR OR RELEASING PARTY DOES NOT KNOW OR SUSPECT TO EXIST IN HIS OR HER FAVOR AT THE TIME OF EXECUTING THE RELEASE AND THAT, IF KNOWN BY HIM OR HER, WOULD HAVE MATERIALLY AFFECTED HIS OR HER SETTLEMENT WITH THE DEBTOR OR RELEASED PARTY.\"**

Each Party, being aware of said provision of law, hereby expressly waives and relinquishes all rights and benefits that he, she, or it may have under California Civil Code Section 1542, and under any other statute, rule, regulation, or common-law principle of similar effect in any jurisdiction, with respect to the Fonseca Released Claims (in the case of Fonseca) or the Rennick Released Claims (in the case of the Rennick Parties), as applicable. Each Party understands and acknowledges that the significance and consequence of this waiver of California Civil Code Section 1542 is that, even if a Party should eventually suffer additional damages arising out of the facts, circumstances, or transactions that are the subject of the released claims, such Party will not be able to make any claim for those damages. Each Party acknowledges that he, she, or it intends these consequences even as to claims that may exist as of the date of this Agreement but which such Party does not know to exist, and which, if known, would have materially affected such Party\'s decision to execute this Agreement. Each Party further acknowledges that this waiver was separately bargained for and is a key element of this Agreement.

**[Section 7: DISMISSAL OF ACTION]{.underline}**

**7.1 Joint Stipulation.** Within five (5) business days following Fonseca\'s receipt of the First Installment, the Parties, through their respective counsel of record, shall execute and file with the Superior Court of the State of California, County of Los Angeles, a Joint Stipulation for Dismissal of the Action (Case No. 23STCV01897), with prejudice, with each side bearing its own attorney\'s fees and costs. The Joint Stipulation shall provide that the Court shall retain jurisdiction over the Parties and the subject matter of this Agreement pursuant to California Code of Civil Procedure Section 664.6 for purposes of enforcing the terms and conditions of this Agreement, including without limitation the payment obligations set forth in Section 1 hereof. Counsel for Fonseca shall prepare the initial draft of the Joint Stipulation and circulate it to counsel for the Rennick Parties for review and approval, such approval not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed.

**7.2 Counterclaim Dismissal.** Simultaneously with the filing of the Joint Stipulation described in Section 7.1 above, Rennick shall dismiss with prejudice his counterclaim filed in the Action on March 6, 2023, including all claims and causes of action asserted therein, with each side bearing its own attorney\'s fees and costs with respect to the counterclaim. If required by the Court\'s local rules, the dismissal of the counterclaim may be included within the Joint Stipulation for Dismissal.

**[Section 8: NON-DISPARAGEMENT]{.underline}**

From and after the Effective Date, no Party shall, directly or indirectly, make, publish, authorize, ratify, or cause to be made or published, whether orally, in writing, or through any electronic or digital medium (including without limitation social media platforms, blogs, podcasts, press releases, and industry publications), any statement, comment, or communication that is derogatory, defamatory, disparaging, or injurious to the reputation, business, or personal standing of any other Party, in connection with CMP, the Action, the Dispute, the subject matter of this Agreement, or the events, transactions, or circumstances giving rise thereto. Nothing in this Section 8 shall prohibit any Party from: (a) making truthful statements in response to a lawful subpoena, court order, or government investigation; (b) providing truthful testimony in any judicial, arbitral, or administrative proceeding; or (c) communicating in good faith with his, her, or its legal or tax advisors regarding the matters addressed in this Agreement.

**[Section 9: CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**

**9.1 General Obligation.** The Parties shall keep strictly confidential the existence and terms of this Agreement, the Settlement Amount, the payment schedule, and all related negotiations and communications, and shall not disclose such information to any third party, except:

> **(a)** to their respective legal counsel, tax advisors, accountants, and financial advisors, each of whom shall be informed of and bound by the confidentiality obligations set forth in this Section 9;
>
> **(b)** as may be required by applicable law, regulation, subpoena, court order, or governmental investigation or proceeding; and
>
> **(c)** to Ridgeline Commercial Bank (555 West 7th Street, 18th Floor, Los Angeles, California 90014) and its authorized representatives, solely to the extent necessary in connection with CMP\'s existing One Million Four Hundred Thousand Dollar (\$1,400,000) revolving credit facility and any renewals, amendments, or refinancings thereof, provided that any such disclosure shall be accompanied by a written request that the recipient maintain the disclosed information in confidence.

**9.2 Notice of Compelled Disclosure.** In the event that any Party receives a subpoena, court order, regulatory demand, or other legal process that would require or compel disclosure of the terms of this Agreement or any information subject to the confidentiality obligations of Section 9.1, the Party receiving such legal process (the \"Compelled Party\") shall, to the extent legally permissible, provide prompt written notice to the other Parties of such legal process no fewer than five (5) business days prior to making any such disclosure. The notice shall include a copy of the legal process and a description of the information proposed to be disclosed. The other Parties shall have the right, at their own expense, to seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy to prevent or limit such disclosure. The Compelled Party shall cooperate reasonably with any such efforts. If, after reasonable efforts, a protective order or other remedy is not obtained, the Compelled Party may disclose only that portion of the confidential information that is legally required to be disclosed.

**[Section 10: RSV GOING FORWARD]{.underline}**

The Parties acknowledge that RSV has provided and may continue to provide management, administrative, production, and other professional services to CMP in connection with the ongoing exploitation of CMP\'s existing film library and any future projects undertaken by CMP. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to terminate or prohibit the engagement of RSV by CMP; provided, however, that any continuing or future services rendered by RSV to CMP on or after the Effective Date shall be subject to the following conditions:

> **(a)** All invoices submitted by RSV to CMP for management services, overhead, administrative support, or any other services shall be subject to the management-fee cap of three percent (3%) of CMP\'s applicable gross receipts, as set forth in the Restated Waterfall. Any invoice or aggregate invoices from RSV that would cause total management fees paid to RSV in any calendar year to exceed such cap shall not be payable by CMP unless both partners expressly consent in writing to the excess amount.
>
> **(b)** Each individual RSV invoice submitted to CMP, regardless of amount, shall be subject to the dual-signature approval requirement set forth in Section 5.1 of this Agreement. No RSV invoice shall be paid by CMP without the prior written approval of both Fonseca and Rennick. For the avoidance of doubt, this requirement applies in addition to, and not in lieu of, the general dual-signature requirement for expenditures exceeding Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$25,000) set forth in Section 5.1.

**[Section 11: REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES]{.underline}**

Each Party hereby represents and warrants to the other Parties, as of the Effective Date, as follows:

> **(a) Authority.** Such Party has full legal right, power, capacity, and authority to execute, deliver, and perform this Agreement and to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby. In the case of RSV, the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement have been duly authorized by all necessary action on the part of RSV, and this Agreement constitutes the valid and binding obligation of RSV, enforceable against RSV in accordance with its terms.
>
> **(b) Voluntary Execution.** This Agreement has been executed freely and voluntarily by such Party, without coercion, duress, or undue influence. Such Party has had the opportunity to review this Agreement with his, her, or its legal counsel, has in fact consulted with legal counsel regarding the terms and consequences of this Agreement, and fully understands the terms and significance hereof. Such Party has had a reasonable period of time within which to consider this Agreement before executing it.
>
> **(c) No Prior Assignment.** Such Party has not heretofore assigned, transferred, conveyed, pledged, hypothecated, or otherwise disposed of, in whole or in part, any claim, demand, cause of action, right, or interest released, compromised, or otherwise addressed by this Agreement. No other person or entity has any interest in any of the claims, demands, or causes of action referred to in this Agreement by reason of any assignment, grant, or transfer made or purported to have been made by such Party.

PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL --- ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT

**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP** 110 SE 6th Street, Suite 2800 Fort Lauderdale, Florida 33301 Telephone: (954) 555-7200 \| Facsimile: (954) 555-7201

**[MEMORANDUM]{.underline}**

**PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL --- ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT**

**Date:** April 26, 2024

**TO:** Matter File --- *Verimark Hospitality Group Inc. v. Coastal Palms Franchise Holdings LLC et al.*

**FROM:** Priya Anand, Responsible Partner (FL Bar No. 0087451) Douglas Carmichael, Billing Partner (FL Bar No. 0093217)

**RE:** Matter Closing Memorandum --- Case No. 1021-00006 (Circuit Court of the 17th Judicial Circuit, Broward County, Florida)

**MATTER NUMBER:** 1044-00007

**STATUS:** **CLOSED --- April 26, 2024**

**[I. PURPOSE AND SCOPE OF MEMORANDUM]{.underline}**

**[B. Nature of the Dispute]{.underline}**

This matter involved a breach-of-contract action arising from Coastal Palms\' systematic underreporting of Gross Room Revenue (\"GRR\") over a nine-year period spanning 2013 through 2021. The underreporting resulted in the chronic and substantial underpayment of three categories of fees owed to Verimark under the parties\' Franchise License Agreements: (i) royalties, calculated at five percent (5%) of GRR pursuant to FLA § 4.1; (ii) marketing-fund contributions, calculated at two and one-half percent (2.5%) of GRR pursuant to FLA § 4.2; and (iii) technology fees, assessed at \$12.50 per available room per month, with consumer price index adjustments capped at three percent (3%) annually, pursuant to FLA § 4.3.

The revenue-diversion scheme at the heart of this dispute operated as follows: Beginning no later than January 2013, Coastal Palms, acting through and at the direction of Randall Brecker, established Suncoast Room Management Inc. as a nominally separate management company. Suncoast collected revenues from direct bookings --- a category encompassing walk-in guests paying at the front desk, corporate accounts that booked directly with the properties rather than through Verimark\'s centralized reservation system, and guests who booked through the unbranded website gulfcoastrooms.com, which Suncoast created and operated. Suncoast retained a twelve percent (12%) \"management fee\" on all revenues it collected. Critically, neither Suncoast\'s gross collections nor the management fee were included in the GRR figures that Coastal Palms reported to Verimark for purposes of calculating royalties, marketing-fund contributions, and technology fees.

In addition to the Suncoast-based diversion, Coastal Palms also systematically underreported revenue from third-party online travel agencies (\"OTAs\") by netting commissions paid to the OTAs against GRR before reporting it to Verimark. This netting practice violated the FLAs\' definition of GRR, which was defined on a gross basis without deduction for commissions, discounts, or fees paid to intermediaries.

The underreporting was estimated at between twenty-two percent (22%) and thirty-one percent (31%) of actual GRR across the portfolio, with variation by individual property and by year. The total underreported GRR over the nine-year period was estimated at approximately \$197.8 million. For fiscal year 2021 alone --- the year immediately preceding the discovery of the scheme --- Coastal Palms reported GRR of \$112.4 million, whereas estimated true GRR was \$145.6 million, representing an underreporting of approximately \$33.2 million for that single year.

> • **Section 4.3 --- Technology Fee:** Franchisee to pay a technology fee of \$12.50 per available room per month, subject to annual CPI adjustment capped at three percent (3%) per year, to support Verimark\'s centralized reservation system, property-management system integrations, and brand technology platforms.
>
> • **Section 4.6 --- Late-Payment Interest:** Any amounts not paid when due to bear interest at a rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, compounded monthly, until paid in full.

> • **Section 8.2 --- Audit Rights:** Verimark entitled to audit franchisee\'s financial records upon ten (10) business days\' written notice. If an audit reveals an underpayment exceeding two percent (2%) of reported GRR for the audited period, the franchisee bears all audit costs.

**[III. ENGAGEMENT HISTORY AND KEY MILESTONES]{.underline}**

**[A. Pre-Litigation Phase (November 2021 -- March 2022)]{.underline}**

The origins of this matter trace to a whistleblower complaint received by Verimark\'s compliance hotline. On **November 8, 2021**, Janet Kerrigan, a former regional controller for Coastal Palms who had been terminated in October 2021, contacted the Verimark compliance hotline and reported allegations of systematic revenue diversion by Coastal Palms and its affiliated entity, Suncoast Room Management Inc. Ms. Kerrigan alleged that Randall Brecker had directed property-level accounting staff to exclude direct-booking revenues collected by Suncoast from the GRR reports submitted to Verimark, and that this practice had been ongoing for several years.

On **November 15, 2021**, Calderwood & Harkness LLP, operating under a separate pre-engagement letter agreement with Verimark for advisory services, provided a preliminary analysis of the whistleblower allegations. Yuki Nakamura prepared a memorandum to Priya Anand assessing the legal implications of the allegations under the FLAs, the potential scope of damages, and the recommended investigative steps. The memorandum concluded that, if substantiated, the allegations described conduct that would constitute both a material breach and a potentially incurable breach under FLA § 14.2(c).

On **November 22, 2021**, Verimark engaged **Thornbury & Associates CPAs LLP** (lead audit partner: Malcolm Thornbury, CPA; principal office: 1551 N. Flagler Drive, Suite 800, West Palm Beach, Florida 33401) to conduct a franchise-compliance audit of Coastal Palms\' ten (10) highest-grossing properties pursuant to the audit-rights provisions of FLA § 8.2. The audit scope covered fiscal years 2019 through 2021 and was designed to test the accuracy of GRR reporting against available bank records, OTA statements, and property-management system data.

On **January 18, 2022**, Thornbury delivered its preliminary findings. The audit revealed that the ten (10) audited properties had underreported GRR by approximately twenty-six percent (26%) for the period 2019--2021. Extrapolation of these findings across all twenty-two (22) Coastal Palms properties and the full nine-year period of 2013--2021 yielded an estimated \$197.8 million in total underreported GRR. These preliminary findings confirmed the substance of Ms. Kerrigan\'s whistleblower allegations and provided the evidentiary foundation for the pre-suit demand and the subsequent litigation.

On **February 4, 2022**, Verimark issued a formal Notice of Material Breach to Coastal Palms under FLA § 14.1, demanding that Coastal Palms cure the breach within thirty (30) days by, among other things, providing a full accounting of all revenues collected by Suncoast Room Management Inc. and remitting all underpaid royalties, marketing-fund contributions, and technology fees, together with applicable late-payment interest. Concurrently, Priya Anand transmitted a companion pre-suit demand letter to Nathan Whitfield III of WBC, advising that Calderwood & Harkness LLP had been engaged to pursue Verimark\'s claims and that litigation would follow if the breach was not cured within the cure period.

On **February 28, 2022**, WBC responded on behalf of Coastal Palms, denying any material breach. WBC asserted that Suncoast\'s revenues were properly excluded from GRR under what WBC characterized as a \"reasonable interpretation\" of the FLA\'s GRR definition, arguing that revenues collected by a separate management entity fell outside the scope of \"Gross Room Revenue\" as defined in the FLAs. WBC further contended that Verimark had been aware of Suncoast\'s role because Suncoast was identified in property-management agreements submitted during the franchise-application process.

On **March 6, 2022**, the thirty (30)-day cure period expired without any cure being tendered by Coastal Palms. At this juncture, Verimark authorized Calderwood & Harkness LLP to proceed with the filing of a breach-of-contract action.

On **June 14, 2022**, the initial Case Management Conference was held before Judge Calloway. The Court set the matter for trial in February 2024 and established a discovery schedule with fact-discovery closing in August 2023.

On **August 8, 2022**, a subpoena duces tecum was served on **Ironclad National Bank** (Devon Schultz, Senior Vice President, at 225 Peachtree Street NE, Suite 2600, Atlanta, Georgia 30303), seeking loan documents and financial statements submitted by Coastal Palms in connection with Ironclad\'s approximately \$94 million in first-lien mortgage loans on eighteen (18) of the twenty-two (22) Coastal Palms properties. The financial statements submitted to Ironclad were expected to --- and ultimately did --- reflect the true revenue figures, creating a critical inconsistency with the GRR reports submitted to Verimark.

On **August 22, 2022**, Coastal Palms made its initial document production, consisting of approximately 84,000 documents. On **August 30, 2022**, Calderwood & Harkness LLP transmitted a detailed deficiency letter identifying twenty-three (23) categories of documents that were either missing entirely or incomplete, with particular emphasis on the absence of Suncoast Room Management Inc. financial records, gulfcoastrooms.com booking data, and bank statements for accounts maintained in Suncoast\'s name.

**4. Discovery Disputes and Motion to Compel**

On **September 8, 2022**, Calderwood & Harkness LLP sent a formal meet-and-confer letter to WBC regarding the deficient production, specifically demanding production of all Suncoast Room Management Inc. records. WBC responded by asserting that Suncoast was a separate entity not subject to the discovery requests directed to Coastal Palms, notwithstanding that Suncoast was a named defendant in the action and was managed and controlled by Randall Brecker, the Managing Member of Coastal Palms.

On **September 15, 2022**, having been unable to resolve the dispute through the meet-and-confer process, Verimark filed a Motion to Compel Production of Suncoast Room Management Inc. Records. The motion was supported by a memorandum of law addressing the alter-ego and common-control doctrines and the relevance of the Suncoast records to the damages analysis.

On **October 28, 2022**, the Court granted Verimark\'s Motion to Compel, ordering Coastal Palms and Suncoast to produce all responsive documents within twenty-one (21) days. The Court found that the records sought were clearly within the control of the defendants and were directly relevant to the claims at issue.

On **November 18, 2022**, Coastal Palms made a supplemental production consisting of approximately 312,000 additional documents, including the Suncoast Room Management Inc. financial records that had been the subject of the Motion to Compel. The total volume of data processed on Verimark\'s side reached approximately 2.3 million documents comprising approximately 1.1 terabytes of data.

On **November 28, 2022**, Verimark served its Second Request for Production, consisting of thirty-four (34) requests targeting Suncoast financial data, OTA contracts, and gulfcoastrooms.com booking logs in greater detail.
